questions.stem: What does the news report say about Nancy Gifford?

options.label: A
options.text: She was born months after the end of World War I.

options.label: B
options.text: She has been living in her house throughout her life.

options.label: C
options.text: She suffered a great deal during the Second World War.

options.label: D
options.text: She is a 102-year-old woman living in Somerset Village.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） She was born months after the end of World War I.
【定位】Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War, and spent 102 years
living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street.
南希·吉福德出生于第一次世界大战结束数月后，并在萨默塞特郡斯特里特村的一栋三居室房
屋里住了102年。
【信号】首段人物定义句。新闻首段在抛出事件（104岁老妇卖房）后，用 Nancy Gifford was
born months after the end of the First World War 给出人物关键身份信息，直接回应题
干所问。
【替换】Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War ↔
She was born months after the end of World War I.
同义替换：the First World War = World War I
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
原文说 the house she has lived in since she was two years old，并非一生都在此居住；
She has been living in her house throughout her life. 把起点从两岁偷换为'一生'。
借用原文：the house she has lived in since she was two years old
C) 过度推断
原文仅说 having lived in it through the Second World War，表示她经历了二战，但并
未说她 suffered a great deal；She suffered a great deal during the Second World
War. 把'经历'强改为'遭受巨大痛苦'。
借用原文：having lived in it through the Second World War
D) 偷换概念
原文说 Nancy Gifford 是 A 104-year-old woman，且 spent 102 years living in her
three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street；She is a 102-year-old
woman living in Somerset Village. 把居住时长误植为年龄，同时把 Somerset Village of
Street 简化为 Somerset Village。
借用原文：A 104-year-old woman

questions.stem: Why is Mrs. Gifford selling the house?

options.label: A
options.text: She has been persuaded by the estate agent.

options.label: B
options.text: She needs the money badly for her health.

options.label: C
options.text: She is leaving Glastonbury Village.

options.label: D
options.text: She is moving to a nursing home.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） She is moving to a nursing home.
【定位】Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury
because of her health.
吉福德夫人因为健康原因，正在出售房屋并搬到附近格拉斯顿伯里的一家养老院。
【信号】because of 因果信号。答案句以 because of her health 结尾，直接回答 Why；卖房与搬
去养老院是并列结果，健康才是原因。
【替换】Mrs. Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of
her health
↔ She is moving to a nursing home.
因果同构：卖房是为搬去养老院
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
原文 According to the estate agent, the house was built in 1882... 只说明中介提供了房
屋信息，并未说 Mrs. Gifford 是被中介说服卖房；She has been persuaded by the
estate agent. 把'中介存在'曲解为'被中介说服'。
借用原文：According to the estate agent
B) 偷换概念
原文 because of her health 说明健康是原因，但并未说她 needs the money badly；She
needs the money badly for her health. 把'因健康搬家'偷换成'因健康急需钱'。
借用原文：because of her health
C) 与原文相反
原文说 moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury，即她要搬去格拉斯顿伯里；
She is leaving Glastonbury Village. 把'搬入附近格拉斯顿伯里'说成'离开格拉斯顿伯里'，
方向相反。
借用原文：moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 The navy rescued a man who survived 24 days floating in the sea on a boat by eating tomato sauce
and vegetable powder. The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to
his rescue.
海军救起了一名男子，他靠食用番茄酱和蔬菜粉，在一艘船上漂浮海上生存了24天。这名47岁的男子在
船上用英语写下了“HELP”一词，这对他的获救起到了关键作用。
2 The man told authorities that his experience began in December when currents swept the sailboat out
to sea while he was making repairs. To survive, the man collected rainwater with a cloth. He had to
constantly remove water from the boat to prevent it from sinking. He also tried to light a fire to send a
distress signal without success. Finally, a plane passed by and he signaled with a mirror. He said
the navy told him that he was spotted when the plane passed again. The sailboat was abandoned at
sea when the man was picked up by a nearby merchant ship. He was found in good health but had
lost weight.
这名男子告诉当局，他的遭遇始于12月，当时他正在维修帆船，洋流将帆船冲向了大海。为了生存，他用
一块布收集雨水。他不得不不断将船里的水排出去，以防船只沉没。他还试图生火发出求救信号，但没有
成功。最后，一架飞机经过时，他用镜子发出了信号。他说，海军告诉他，飞机再次经过时发现了他。这
名男子被附近的一艘商船救起时，帆船已被遗弃在海上。他被发现时身体状况良好，但体重有所下降。

questions.stem: What does the news report say was key to the man's rescue?

options.label: A
options.text: The navy's timely arrival.

options.label: B
options.text: His rich sailing experience.

options.label: C
options.text: The word HELP written on the boat.

options.label: D
options.text: His use of a mirror to send a signal.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） The word HELP written on the boat.
【定位】The man, 47, wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue.
这名47岁的男子在船身上用英文写下了"HELP"（救命）一词，而这正是他获救的关键。
【信号】非限制性定语从句 'which was key to his rescue' 直接点题。which was key to his
rescue 把前文的 'wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat' 明确标注为获救关键，
是新闻中少见的显性答案标记。
【替换】wrote the word "HELP" in English on the boat ↔ The word HELP written on the boat
动作名词化 + 核心信息保留
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
The navy's timely arrival 中的 navy 确实出现在录音中，但原文只说 The navy rescued a
man，海军是执行救援的一方，而非 'key to his rescue' 所指的原因。
借用原文：The navy rescued a man
B) 未提及
His rich sailing experience 中的 sailing experience 在整段录音中没有任何对应信息，属
于无中生有。
D) 原词陷阱
His use of a mirror to send a signal 中的 mirror 确实在 he signaled with a mirror 中出
现，但这是男子在飞机经过时的求救尝试；原文明确说 key 是 HELP，镜子只是另一条求生
手段。
借用原文：he signaled with a mirror

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man when he was rescued?

options.label: A
options.text: He lost all consciousness.

options.label: B
options.text: He was in good condition.

options.label: C
options.text: He was too distressed to pick himself up.

options.label: D
options.text: He entirely abandoned himself to despair.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） He was in good condition.
【定位】He was found in good health but had lost weight.
他被发现时身体状况良好，但体重减轻了。
【信号】新闻结尾总结人物状态的收束句。He was found in good health 中的 was found 是被救
后的总结性动词，in good health 直接回应题干 'when he was rescued' 的状态询问。
【替换】in good health ↔ He was in good condition
近义形容词替换
【排除】A) 偷换概念
He lost all consciousness 中的 lost 可能让考生联想到 had lost weight，但 weight 与
consciousness 是完全不同的概念，属于偷换概念。
借用原文：had lost weight
C) 未提及
He was too distressed to pick himself up 中的 distressed 与 pick himself up 在录音中
均未出现，且与 'in good health' 的正面评价相反。
D) 原词陷阱
He entirely abandoned himself to despair 中的 abandoned 可能让考生联想到 The
sailboat was abandoned at sea，但原文主语是 sailboat（船被遗弃），选项却把它改成
He abandoned himself（自暴自弃），且 despair 在录音中从未出现。
借用原文：The sailboat was abandoned at sea

questions.stem: What do we learn about the elementary and middle schools to be closed in Denver?

options.label: A
options.text: Their efforts to provide social services have been ignored.

options.label: B
options.text: They have been criticized by the Denver school board.

options.label: C
options.text: They have taken various steps to get more funding.

options.label: D
options.text: Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline.
【定位】The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to
make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment.
丹佛公立学校董事会准备关闭几所中小学，以弥补因入学人数下降而造成的预算减少。
【信号】因果信号 caused by。答案句中 caused by declining enrollment 直接给出关闭学校的
causal chain：预算减少 ← 入学下降 ← 学校关闭。
【替换】declining enrollment ↔ Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline.
同义替换 declining = on a noticeable decline
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 A 说‘提供社会服务的努力被忽视’，但录音末句只说 cannot provide the same
mental health supports, social and emotional services，是预算不足导致无法提供，并
非努力被忽视；social services 这个词录音确实念到了，但语义与选项不符。
借用原文：social and emotional services
B) 未提及
选项 B 说学校被校董会批评，但录音中校董会是作出关闭决定的主体，并未出现 criticized
的语义，属于无中生有。
C)
选项 C 说学校采取各种措施争取资金，但录音讲的是‘因预算减少而关校’，没有提到学校主
动 steps to get more funding，属于无中生有。

questions.stem: What does the Denver district expect to do in the next three years?

options.label: A
options.text: Approve criteria for closing schools with decreased funding.

options.label: B
options.text: Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.

options.label: C
options.text: Decide which elementary and middle schools to close.

options.label: D
options.text: Alter its per-pupil funding policy on a rational basis.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.
【定位】In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle
school students, it said.
该地区表示，在未来三年内，预计中小学入学人数将减少3000人。
【信号】时间信号 + 数字信号。答案句中 In the next three years 与 expects to enroll 3,000
fewer 形成时间与数字的双重信号，直接对应题干。
【替换】enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students ↔
Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.
原词复现
【排除】A)
选项 A 说‘批准关闭标准’，但录音中 The school board approved criteria 用一般过去时，
表示已经批准，不是 expect to do 的未来动作。
借用原文：The school board approved criteria
C) 答非所问
选项 C 说‘决定关闭哪些中小学’，但录音中 The specific schools will be announced in
the coming days 指近期宣布，不是 in the next three years 的预期动作；属于答非所
问。
借用原文：The specific schools will be announced in the coming days
D) 偷换概念
选项 D 说‘改变 per-pupil funding 政策’，但录音只是用 per-pupil funding 解释预算计算
方式，并未说要 alter policy，属于偷换概念。
借用原文：per-pupil funding

questions.stem: Why are some schools in Denver to be closed according to the district spokesperson?

options.label: A
options.text: To enable the district to remain competitive.

options.label: B
options.text: To avoid a negative impact on its economy.

options.label: C
options.text: To keep the district free of debt.

options.label: D
options.text: To obtain the expected funding.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） To keep the district free of debt.
【定位】"We know that there are impacts and it's heartbreaking and difficult work. But in order for the
district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said.
‘我们知道这会带来影响，这是令人心碎且艰难的工作。但为了让学区不负债，这是必须采取
的一步，’他说。
【信号】目的信号 in order for... to stay out of debt。发言人先用 But 转折，再用 in order
for the district to stay out of debt 点明关闭学校的根本目的，答案落点在 stay out
of debt。
【替换】stay out of debt ↔ To keep the district free of debt.
同义替换 stay out of = keep... free of
【排除】A) 未提及
选项 A 说‘让学区保持竞争力’，但录音全文未出现 competitive / competition 等词，属于
无中生有。
B) 原词陷阱
选项 B 说‘避免对经济造成负面影响’，但录音中 there are impacts 是承认影响存在，并未
说 avoid negative impact on its economy；impact 原词出现，但语义被扭曲。
借用原文：there are impacts
D) 原词陷阱
选项 D 说‘为了获得预期资金’，但录音讲的是预算减少、按 per-pupil funding 计算缺口，
关闭学校是为了 stay out of debt（减少支出/避免负债），而不是 obtain funding（获得
资金）；funding 原词出现，但目的被替换。
借用原文：decreased budget

questions.stem: Why does the woman call the man?

options.label: A
options.text: To book tickets for a musical.

options.label: B
options.text: To enquire about the price of cats.

options.label: C
options.text: To pay for her afternoon flight to London.

options.label: D
options.text: To have her personal computer repaired.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） To book tickets for a musical.
【定位】I've been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats in London on the evening of May the
28th, but I can't get the computer to accept my card payment.
我一直在尝试预订5月28日晚上伦敦音乐剧《猫》的门票，但电脑不接受我的银行卡支付。
【信号】被问者直接说明来电目的。女士在第二段直接说 I've been trying to book tickets for the
musical Cats，这是对话开头最典型的“说明来意”句型，答案落在此处。
【替换】book tickets for the musical Cats ↔ To book tickets for a musical.
同义替换：具体剧名概括为 musical
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
选项 B 的 cats 盗用了录音原词 Cats，但录音中 Cats 是音乐剧名，不是宠物猫，更不存在
“询问猫的价格”。
借用原文：the musical Cats
C) 张冠李戴
选项 C 的 London 和 afternoon 都是录音里出现的词（in London 与问候语 good
afternoon），但录音说的是伦敦的演出，不是下午的航班，属于把地点词和时间词张冠李
戴。
借用原文：in London
D) 原词陷阱
选项 D 的 computer 盗用了 the computer to accept my card payment，但女士说电脑
只是不接受支付，并没有说要修电脑，核心目的仍是订票。
借用原文：I can't get the computer to accept my card payment

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's husband?

options.label: A
options.text: He frequents the Lion Theatre.

options.label: B
options.text: He knows how to sell things well.

options.label: C
options.text: He is a computer science expert.

options.label: D
options.text: He is away on a business trip.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） He is away on a business trip.
【定位】My husband usually does all of these things, but he is in Italy on a business trip until next
Thursday, and I know how quickly these things can sell out.
我丈夫通常做这些事，但他现在在意大利出差，要到下周四才回来，而且我知道这些票卖得
很快。
【信号】转折 but 后出关键信息。女士说 My husband usually does all of these things, but...，
转折词 but 之后 usually 所暗示的“常规情况”被颠覆，真正要考的丈夫当前状态落在 but
后面。
【替换】he is in Italy on a business trip ↔ He is away on a business trip.
同义替换：具体地点概括为 away
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 A 的 Lion Theatre 盗用了 the Lion Theatre in London，但那是 Cats 演出的剧院，
与丈夫是否常去无关。
借用原文：the Lion Theatre in London
B) 未提及 选项 B 的 sell things well 在录音中没有对应表述，属于无中生有。
C) 张冠李戴
选项 C 的 computer 盗用了 the computer 与 I'm not very good with computers，但录
音只说女士自己不擅长电脑，并未说丈夫是电脑专家。
借用原文：I'm not very good with computers

questions.stem: What does the man say about the tickets at the front?

options.label: A
options.text: They are sold at a discount.

options.label: B
options.text: They are in low demand.

options.label: C
options.text: They are no longer available.

options.label: D
options.text: They are not too expensive.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） They are no longer available.
【定位】Actually, all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway.
其实，前排的票反正都已经卖完了。
【信号】Actually 引出事实修正。男士先用 But I can offer you two upstairs near the middle 给
出替代方案，随后用 actually 进一步说明原因——前排票已售罄，答案句就在 actually
之后。
【替换】all the tickets at the front are already sold out ↔ They are no longer available.
同义替换：sold out = no longer available
【排除】A) 未提及 选项 A 的 discount 在录音中没有对应信息，属于无中生有。
B) 与原文相反
选项 B 说“需求低”，但录音说 all the tickets at the front are already sold out，说明需求
很高，选项与原文相反。
借用原文：all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway
D) 未提及
选项 D 的 not too expensive 涉及价格评价，但录音中完全没有讨论票价高低。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she is scared of?

options.label: A
options.text: Heights.

options.label: B
options.text: Circus.

options.label: C
options.text: Wild animals.

options.label: D
options.text: Dark nights.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Heights.
【定位】I'm scared of heights, and you can never see anything if you are too high up anyway.
我恐高，而且坐得太高的话根本什么都看不见。
【信号】直接陈述 scared of。女士说 I'm scared of heights， scared of 是题目关键词的直接复
现，答案紧随其后。
【替换】I'm scared of heights ↔ Heights.
原词复现
【排除】B) 未提及
选项 B 的 Circus 与音乐剧主题相近，但录音中没有提到马戏团，属于利用话题场制造的无
中生有干扰。
C) 偷换概念
选项 C 的 Wild animals 盗用了音乐剧名 Cats 给人的动物联想，但录音根本没有提到野生
动物。
借用原文：the musical Cats
D) 未提及
选项 D 的 Dark nights 在录音中没有对应内容，属于常见恐惧意象的凭空设置。

questions.stem: Why hasn't the man answered the woman's text messages lately?

options.label: A
options.text: He finds it bothersome to reply.

options.label: B
options.text: He has switched off his phone.

options.label: C
options.text: He hasn't got the time to text back.

options.label: D
options.text: He doesn't know how to respond.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） He has switched off his phone.
【定位】Oh, I didn't know you had sent any. I turned off my phone almost a week ago and haven't
turned it back on since then.
哦，我不知道你发了短信。我大概一周前关掉了手机，之后就没再打开过。
【信号】直接应答 + 关键动作。女人一开口就问为何没回短信，男人用 I turned off my phone
almost a week ago and haven't turned it back on since then. 直接给出原因，这是对话
中被问者的核心应答句。
【替换】I turned off my phone almost a week ago and haven't turned it back on since then. ↔
He has switched off his phone.
同义词替换（turn off = switch off）
【排除】A) 未提及 男人从未表达回复短信令他厌烦，属于无中生有。
C) 未提及
录音中男人说的是『我不知道你发了短信』和『关机』，没有提到没时间回短信。
D) 原词陷阱
录音说 I didn't know you had sent any.，是『不知道你发了短信』，选项 He doesn't
know how to respond. 把不知对象偷换成『不知如何回应』。
借用原文：I didn't know you had sent any.

questions.stem: What was the man shocked to realize after he downloaded the APP?

options.label: A
options.text: His lack of sufficient sleep at night.

options.label: B
options.text: His addiction to mobile phone games.

options.label: C
options.text: His excessive use of the mobile phone.

options.label: D
options.text: His high frequency of surfing the net.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） His excessive use of the mobile phone.
【定位】Well, I downloaded an APP that recorded how much time I spent on my phone. And I was
shocked to realize I was using my phone an average of 8 hours a day, and on my worst day, I
used it for 12 hours.
嗯，我下载了一个记录手机使用时长的APP。我震惊地发现我平均每天用手机8小时，最多
的一天用了12小时。
【信号】题干关键词原词复现 + 数据强调。男人的话里出现 shocked to realize，与题干 shocked
to realize 原词呼应，后面 8 hours a day、12 hours 用具体数字凸显『使用过度』。
【替换】I was using my phone an average of 8 hours a day, and on my worst day, I used it for 12 hours. ↔
His excessive use of the mobile phone.
数字概括为『过度使用』
recorded how much time I spent on my phone ↔ His excessive use of the mobile phone.
时间记录映射到使用强度
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
女人提到自己的朋友玩手机游戏『all day and into the night』，这说的是朋友，不是男人
的情况。
借用原文：he sometimes played them all day and into the night.
B) 原词陷阱
女人问 Were you addicted to mobile phone games?，男人回答 No, my problem was I
was spending too much time on social media...，选项 His addiction to mobile phone
games. 直接盗用问句原词，却被明确否定。
借用原文：Were you addicted to mobile phone games?
D) 未提及
录音只提到 social media / messaging / commenting，没有说 surfing the net，属于用
近义概念捏造。

questions.stem: What did the man spend much time doing with his phone?

options.label: A
options.text: Shopping online and paying for his purchases.

options.label: B
options.text: Communicating with friends on social media.

options.label: C
options.text: Exploring whatever content to his liking.

options.label: D
options.text: Sharing and posting pictures and videos.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Communicating with friends on social media.
【定位】No, my problem was I was spending too much time on social media, messaging friends and
commenting on other people's posts.
不，我的问题是我花了太多时间在社交媒体上，给朋友发消息、评论别人的帖子。
【信号】否定后的真正落点。女人先猜测是游戏，男人用 No, my problem was I was spending
too much time on social media, messaging friends and commenting on other
people's posts. 纠正并给出真实答案，否定词 No 后面才是考点。
【替换】spending too much time on social media, messaging friends ↔
Communicating with friends on social media.
动名词短语同义替换
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
选项 Shopping online and paying for his purchases. 来自女人说的 shopping online
and paying for everything with my phone，不是男人的行为。
借用原文：shopping online and paying for everything with my phone.
C) 未提及 录音没有提到 exploring content / whatever to his liking。
D) 偷换概念
录音说 commenting on other people's posts，选项 Sharing and posting pictures and
videos. 添加了 pictures and videos，并把 commenting 换成 sharing，属于偷换概念。
借用原文：commenting on other people's posts.

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she has to use her mobile phone?

options.label: A
options.text: She prefers chatting with others online to meeting them.

options.label: B
options.text: There are few physical stores near where she lives.

options.label: C
options.text: Ordering meals online is a great convenience to her.

options.label: D
options.text: She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.
【定位】That's great for you, but my friends and family don't live in this city, so we can't see each
other often, and I don't have any choice but to chat with them online.
这对你很好，但我的朋友和家人不住在这个城市，所以我们不能经常见面，我别无选择，只
能和他们在线聊天。
【信号】but 后的不得已理由。女人先肯定男人的做法，随即用 but my friends and family don't
live in this city... I don't have any choice but to chat with them online 给出自己的难
处，but 与 have no choice but to 共同标出答案落点。
【替换】my friends and family don't live in this city, so we can't see each other often ↔
She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.
『不住同城』替换为『far away』
I don't have any choice but to chat with them online ↔
She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.
『不得不聊』对应『需要聊』
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
录音说 I don't have any choice but to chat with them online，是客观无奈；选项 She
prefers chatting with others online to meeting them. 却说她更喜欢线上聊天，改变了
语义极性。
借用原文：I don't have any choice but to chat with them online.
B) 张冠李戴
选项 There are few physical stores near where she lives. 借用了男人说的 I go to
physical stores and pay in cash.，但说话人与话题都不属于女人。
借用原文：I go to physical stores and pay in cash.
C) 答非所问
录音中女人提到的是 shopping online / paying for everything，没有提到 ordering
meals online，且这也不是她必须使用手机的核心理由。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the gap in wage gains between job switchers and those who stay in their jobs?

options.label: A
options.text: It is now narrowing.

options.label: B
options.text: It keeps increasing.

options.label: C
options.text: It has remained huge.

options.label: D
options.text: It will soon disappear.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） It is now narrowing.
【定位】But the gap is now closing.
但这个差距现在正在缩小。
【信号】转折 but 后直接给出结论。But the gap is now closing. 中 But 承接前一句“跳槽者去年工
资涨幅更高”，转折后才是当前真实趋势；后文又重复 The gap in wage gains between
people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing.，形成
强调。
【替换】the gap is now closing ↔ It is now narrowing.
同义替换 closing = narrowing
【排除】B) 与原文相反 录音说差距在 closing，而 It keeps increasing. 说持续扩大，正好相反。
C) 张冠李戴
录音提到过去差距通常约 one percentage point，七月扩大到 2.6 percentage points，但
这些都是铺垫；It has remained huge. 把过去某一时刻的较大差距偷换成“一直很大”，与
now closing 矛盾。
借用原文：In July though, the gap widened to 2.6 percentage points.
D) 过度推断
closing 只表示“缩小”，不等于“完全消失”；It will soon disappear. 把趋势推向极端，录音
未提。

questions.stem: What do we learn about wage growth now?

options.label: A
options.text: It is fluctuating between 5-7%.

options.label: B
options.text: It is slowing down for everyone.

options.label: C
options.text: It is faster for those who stay in their jobs.

options.label: D
options.text: It is inadequate for dealing with inflation.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） It is slowing down for everyone.
【定位】But now wage growth is slowing down for everyone, and job switchers are getting smaller
wage bumps in their new jobs.
但现在所有人的工资增长都在放缓，跳槽者在新工作中获得的工资涨幅也变小了。
【信号】But now 时间转折 + for everyone 绝对化表述。But now wage growth is slowing
down for everyone 中 But now 把话题拉回当下，for everyone 给出全称范围，是细节题
中最直接的答案信号。
【替换】wage growth is slowing down for everyone ↔ It is slowing down for everyone.
原句复现
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
录音提到 7.3% 和 5.4%，而 It is fluctuating between 5-7%. 把这两个数字捏成一个
“5%-7% 之间波动”的说法，但录音说的是两类人各自的平均涨幅，并非整体在 5-7% 之间
波动。
借用原文：those who change jobs get an average 7.3% raise every year, while those who stay get a

questions.stem: What is the labor market likely doing according to the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Booming.

options.label: B
options.text: Stabilizing.

options.label: C
options.text: Struggling.

options.label: D
options.text: Cooling.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Cooling.
【定位】The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn't overcoming the
historic imbalance between employers and employees in the U.S.
劳动力市场可能在降温，因为即使工人短缺也无法扭转美国雇主与雇员之间长期存在的不
平衡。
【信号】结论句 + because 因果解释。The labor market is likely cooling 位于段落中部，是作者
给出的判断；后接 because 解释原因，进一步确认该句为结论落点。
【替换】The labor market is likely cooling ↔ Cooling.
原词复现
【排除】A) 与原文相反
录音说市场 likely cooling，Booming. 表示繁荣火热，方向完全相反；且录音提到
demand for workers has reached or is nearing its peak，暗示上升空间已尽。
借用原文：The labor market is likely cooling
B) 偷换概念
录音说 cooling（降温），Stabilizing. 说稳定，是两个不同的状态；降温意味着从高点回
落，稳定则意味着保持不变。
C) 未提及
录音没有提到 labor market 在 struggling；文中说的是工资增长放缓、市场降温，这是周
期性描述，并非“ struggling（挣扎）”这种带有困难色彩的评价。

questions.stem: What does a new study show about highly processed foods?

options.label: A
options.text: They have smaller amounts of nutrients than unprocessed diets.

options.label: B
options.text: Their contribution to calorie consumption is hard to determine.

options.label: C
options.text: They account for nearly half of the average American diet.

options.label: D
options.text: Their low price and convenience negatively impact health.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Their low price and convenience negatively impact health.
【定位】But a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health.
但一项新研究表明，它们低廉的价格和便利是以健康为代价的。
【信号】研究结论信号句。录音用 a new study shows that 引出结论，其后 their low price and
convenience come at a cost to health 直接对应选项 D 的核心语义。
【替换】their low price and convenience come at a cost to health ↔
Their low price and convenience negatively impact health.
同义替换：以健康为代价=对健康有负面影响
【排除】A) 与原文相反
录音明确说 both diets had the same amounts of nutrients，即两种饮食营养成分相同；
选项 A 却说 smaller amounts of nutrients，与原文相反。
借用原文：both diets had the same amounts of nutrients
B) 未提及
录音只提到 they consumed about 500 more calories per day，给出了具体数字，从未
说 contribution to calorie consumption is hard to determine。
C) 偷换概念
录音说 make up as much as 60% of the average American diet，而 nearly half 约等于
50%，数字被偷换；同时它用了 average American diet 这一原词来增强诱惑力。
借用原文：make up as much as 60% of the average American diet

questions.stem: What are highly processed foods linked to, according to other research?

options.label: A
options.text: A strong desire to overeat.

options.label: B
options.text: A lack of nutrients like fiber.

options.label: C
options.text: A higher risk of cancer and obesity.

options.label: D
options.text: A greater intake of sugar and salt.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） A higher risk of cancer and obesity.
【定位】It wasn't a shock to find highly processed foods weren't healthy; other research has linked
them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity.
发现加工食品不健康并不令人惊讶；其他研究已把它们与更高的癌症和肥胖风险联系起来。
【信号】其他研究关联句。录音中 other research has linked them to 是明显的考点信号，后面的
a higher risk of cancer and obesity 即为问题所问的关联内容。
【替换】a higher risk of cancer and obesity ↔ A higher risk of cancer and obesity.
关键短语直接复现
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
录音先说 other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity，随后
才讲新试验发现 'causes people to overeat'；选项 A 把 'overeating' 这个结果张冠李戴到
other research 上。
借用原文：causes people to overeat
B) 与原文相反
录音 both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber and salt 说明
营养成分含量相同，选项 B 却说 A lack of nutrients like fiber，与原文相反。
借用原文：both diets had the same amounts of nutrients, like sugar, fat, fiber and salt
D) 偷换概念
录音 sugar, fat and salt didn't seem to be what caused people to overeat 表明糖、脂
肪、盐并非导致暴食的原因；选项 D 却说 'A greater intake of sugar and salt'，把原文的
否定/排除偷换成了肯定的健康风险关联。
借用原文：sugar, fat and salt didn't seem to be what caused people to overeat

questions.stem: What do people tend to do when eating highly processed foods?

options.label: A
options.text: Eat more quickly.

options.label: B
options.text: Feel full sooner.

options.label: C
options.text: Chew thoroughly.

options.label: D
options.text: Swallow bit by bit.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Eat more quickly.
【定位】The study also found that, when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster.
研究还发现，当人们吃高度加工的饮食时，他们吃得更快。
【信号】研究发现的行为结果。录音用 The study also found that 引出另一项发现，其后 people
ate faster 直接回答题干所问的行为。
【替换】people ate faster ↔ Eat more quickly.
同义替换：ate faster = eat more quickly
【排除】B) 与原文相反
录音 you're not giving your guts enough time to signal to your brain that you've had
enough calories and that you're full 说明大脑更晚收到饱腹信号；选项 B 说 Feel full
sooner，与原文相反。
借用原文：you're not giving your guts enough time to signal to your brain that you've had enough
calories and that you're full
C) 偷换概念
录音 Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and
swallow 只说更容易咀嚼吞咽，并未说人们会 chew thoroughly；恰恰相反，软食更可能
减少咀嚼。
借用原文：Highly processed food tends to be softer, which makes it easier to chew and swallow
D) 偷换概念
录音 easier to chew and swallow 表示吞咽更容易、更快，而选项 D 'Swallow bit by bit'
暗示慢、分小口吞，语义相反。
借用原文：easier to chew and swallow

questions.stem: How do people generally account for differences between men and women in the amount of time spent on housework?

options.label: A
options.text: By attributing them to current cultural influences.

options.label: B
options.text: By attributing them to conservative thinking.

options.label: C
options.text: In terms of new genetic findings.

options.label: D
options.text: In terms of personal preferences.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） By attributing them to conservative thinking.
【定位】Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores
around the house. This is generally attributed to backward thinking and conservative values.
But new research shows that such differences could be linked to differences in the
preferences of males and females.
女性仍然比男性花更多时间照顾孩子和做家务。这通常被归因于落后思想和保守价值观。但
新研究表明，这种差异可能与男性和女性的偏好差异有关。
【信号】观点对比结构。答案句藏在转折之前：前一句 This is generally attributed to backward
thinking and conservative values. 给出'通常看法'，But new research shows that such
differences could be linked to differences in the preferences of males and females.
引出转折后的新研究。题干问 generally，所以取 but 前的内容。
【替换】backward thinking and conservative values ↔ conservative thinking.
同义概括
This is generally attributed to ↔ By attributing them to conservative thinking.
结构改写
【排除】A) 偷换概念
A 项 By attributing them to current cultural influences. 把录音里的 conservative
values 改头换面成'当代文化影响'，原文说的是'保守'而非'当代文化'，方向相反。
C) 未提及
C 项 In terms of new genetic findings. 中的 genetic 在原文完全没有出现，录音只提到
preferences，属于凭空捏造。
D) 原词陷阱
D 项 In terms of personal preferences. 确实是录音原词 preferences of males and
females，但它属于 but 之后的新研究发现，不是题干问的'人们通常'的看法。看到原词就
想选是第一大陷阱。
借用原文：preferences of males and females

questions.stem: What did men lean toward doing according to the new study?

options.label: A
options.text: Sharing with women the chores they see necessary.

options.label: B
options.text: Dividing housework that is demanding for women.

options.label: C
options.text: Performing household tasks that they enjoy.

options.label: D
options.text: Doing tasks that are physically challenging.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Performing household tasks that they enjoy.
【定位】In general, both men and women took more responsibility for tasks they liked. For example,
men liked yard care and home maintenance more than women. They leaned toward wanting
primary responsibility for such tasks.
总体而言，男性和女性都会对自己喜欢的任务承担更多责任。例如，男性比女性更喜欢庭院
护理和房屋维修。他们倾向于想要主要负责这类任务。
【信号】研究结论+例证。答案信号是 In general, both men and women took more
responsibility for tasks they liked. 这一研究总括句，随后用 men liked yard care and
home maintenance more than women 举例支撑。
【替换】tasks they liked ↔ Performing household tasks that they enjoy.
同义词替换
took more responsibility for ↔ Performing household tasks that they enjoy.
动作概括
【排除】A) 未提及
A 项 Sharing with women the chores they see necessary. 中的 see necessary 在原文中
没有对应表述，属于无中生有。
B) 偷换概念
B 项 Dividing housework that is demanding for women. 把录音里'男女共同选择自己喜
欢的任务'改成了'对女性来说繁重的家务'，demanding 在原文没有依据。
D) 未提及
D 项 Doing tasks that are physically challenging. 看似能解释 yard care / home
maintenance，但原文从未用 physically challenging 描述这些任务，考生若凭常识推断就
会掉坑。

questions.stem: What should we keep in mind as regards any research on group differences?

options.label: A
options.text: The large within-group differences.

options.label: B
options.text: The great similarities across groups.

options.label: C
options.text: The researchers' subjective biases.

options.label: D
options.text: The noticeable overgeneralizations.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） The large within-group differences.
【定位】Keep in mind, however, that, as with any research on group differences, there were large
within-group differences.
然而，请记住，正如任何关于群体差异的研究一样，群体内部也存在很大的差异。
【信号】提醒信号词 keep in mind。答案句以 Keep in mind, however, 开头，直接对应题干 keep
in mind，后面跟的就是注意事项。
【替换】large within-group differences ↔ The large within-group differences.
原词复现
as with any research on group differences ↔ The large within-group differences.
题干同义对应
【排除】B) 与原文相反
B 项 The great similarities across groups. 说'群体间高度相似'，而原文 large within-
group differences 强调的是'群体内差异大'，方向相反。
借用原文：large within-group differences
C) 未提及
C 项 The researchers' subjective biases. 中的 subjective biases 在原文没有提到，原文
强调的是群体内部差异，不是研究者偏见。
D) 过度推断
D 项 The noticeable overgeneralizations. 是对群体差异研究可能存在的问题的推断，但
原文只说 within-group differences 大，并未说这是 overgeneralization。

questions.stem: What did previous research reveal about gender differences in attitudes toward family and career?

options.label: A
options.text: They seem to be universal.

options.label: B
options.text: They impact people's whole life.

options.label: C
options.text: They shape one's role in society.

options.label: D
options.text: They appear at an early age.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） They appear at an early age.
【定位】The authors noted that previous research revealed gender differences in attitudes towards
family and career. These differences appear as early as six years old.
作者指出，先前的研究揭示了人们在家庭和职业态度上的性别差异。这些差异早在六岁时就
出现。
【信号】研究结论句。答案信号是 previous research revealed，直接对应题干 previous research
reveal；后一句 These differences appear as early as six years old. 给出具体特征。
【替换】appear as early as six years old ↔ They appear at an early age.
概括改写
【排除】A) 过度推断
A 项 They seem to be universal. 把原文的性别差异推断为'普遍存在'，但原文只提到 six
years old 就出现，并未说 universal。
B) 未提及
B 项 They impact people's whole life. 中的 whole life 在原文没有对应表述，原文只提到
六岁出现，未说影响一生。
C) 偷换概念
C 项 They shape one's role in society. 把 attitudes towards family and career 偷换成
role in society，扩大了概念范围。

questions.stem: Why was Keith Stonehouse left with a $1,000 bill?

options.label: A
options.text: He had bought meals with his online food ordering account.

options.label: B
options.text: His son had used his cell phone to pay for playing a game.

options.label: C
options.text: His son had ordered food from several restaurants.

options.label: D
options.text: He had dined out at a famous five-star restaurant.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） His son had ordered food from several restaurants.
【定位】A man was left with a $1,000 bill, after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food
from several restaurants last weekend.
上周末，一名男子的6岁儿子从多家餐馆点了一桌虚拟盛宴，结果他留下了一张1000美元的
账单。
【信号】after 因果链。新闻首句用 after his 6-year-old son ordered... 直接交代了账单产生的原
因：after 前面是结果（$1,000 bill），后面是原因（儿子点餐）。
【替换】his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants ↔
His son had ordered food from several restaurants.
概括式同义替换
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
录音确实出现了 'online food ordering account'，但用该账户点餐的是儿子，不是父亲；
A 把动作主体从 son 偷换成 He，属于典型的主体张冠李戴。
借用原文：his father's online food ordering account
B) 原词陷阱
录音提到父亲 'let his son use his cell phone to play a game'，但儿子实际上没玩游戏，
而是去点餐了；B 把 'play a game' 偷换成 'pay for playing a game'，动作和目的都错
了。
借用原文：let his son use his cell phone to play a game
D) 未提及
录音从未提到 'five-star restaurant'，也未说父亲外出就餐；D 用高档餐厅制造生活常识诱
惑，属于录音中找不到依据的干扰。

questions.stem: What does the news report say Keith Stonehouse is planning to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Teach his son a lesson.

options.label: B
options.text: Change his password.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask his neighbors for help.

options.label: D
options.text: Buy a bigger refrigerator.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Change his password.
【定位】The father is planning to change his password.
这位父亲打算更改他的密码。
【信号】planning to 直接对应题干。is planning to change his password 中的 'planning to' 与
题干 'is planning to do' 完全同构，后面接的 'change his password' 即为答案动作。
【替换】change his password ↔ Change his password.
原词复现 + 主语省略
【排除】A) 未提及
录音中没有出现 'teach his son a lesson' 或任何惩罚、教育的表述；A 是利用家长的'常识
反应'编造的合理但无依据选项。
C) 原词陷阱
录音确实提到 'invited some neighbors over to eat some of it'，但目的是分享食物，不
是 'ask his neighbors for help'；C 盗用 'neighbors' 一词并改变了动作性质。
借用原文：invited some neighbors over to eat some of it
D) 原词陷阱
录音提到 'Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators'，但完全没有 'buy a
bigger refrigerator' 的计划；D 用 'refrigerator' 这个原词做诱饵，把'已有冰箱'偷换成'要
买更大的冰箱'。
借用原文：refrigerators
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Animal behaviour experts looked at more than 100 research papers. They examined how visitors
affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. They found that elephants socialised more with
each other during public feeding times. After public feeding times, they were more likely to search for
food and less likely to be inactive. In the presence of many visitors, elephants were less likely to use
repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom.
动物行为专家查阅了100多篇研究论文。他们研究了参观者如何影响动物园中250多种动物的行为。他们
发现，在面向公众的喂食时段，大象彼此之间的社交活动更多。公众喂食时段结束后，大象更有可能寻找
食物，也不太可能处于不活动状态。在众多参观者在场时，大象较少表现出重复性行为，而这类行为通常
表明它们感到无聊。
2 Visitors had a similar effect on some other species too, including polar bears, certain jungle cats and
black-tailed plain dogs. Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely
become used to the presence of humans. Zoo visitors are often aspects of a zoo animal's environment
that animals cannot control, and as such can be stressful, although some species appear to show good
adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors.
参观者对其他一些物种也产生了类似影响，包括北极熊、某些丛林猫科动物和黑尾草原犬。一些动物物种
出生并成长于动物园，因此很可能已经习惯了人类的存在。对动物园里的动物而言，参观者通常是其环境
中动物无法控制的因素，因此可能会造成压力，尽管有些物种似乎表现出对参观者状况变化的良好适应
能力。

questions.stem: What did animal behaviour experts do according to the news report?

options.label: A
options.text: They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos.

options.label: B
options.text: They studied when the best time to feed animals in public was.

options.label: C
options.text: They studied how animals adapted themselves to life in zoos.

options.label: D
options.text: They examined what behaviours indicated animal boredom.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos.
【定位】They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos.
他们研究了游客如何影响动物园里250多个物种的行为。
【信号】直接陈述研究内容的动作句。Paragraph 1 开头先说专家 looked at more than 100
research papers，紧接着 They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more
than 250 species in zoos. 用 examined 直接回答题干；对新闻细节题，这种紧跟主题引
入的动作句就是答案落点。
【替换】They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos. ↔
They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos.
具体数量概括为 animal，研究对象一致
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
录音提到 during public feeding times 与 After public feeding times，但这是在说大象
的行为变化，B 项把 public feeding times 改成 'the best time to feed animals'，既偷换
概念又答非所问。
借用原文：public feeding times
C) 偷换概念
some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of
visitors 讲的是适应游客变化，C 项改成 'adapted themselves to life in zoos'，对象从
visitors 变成 zoos，属于偷换概念。
借用原文：good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors
D) 原词陷阱
repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom 只是研究中的一个发现细节，D 项
把它上升为专家的研究主题 'what behaviours indicated animal boredom'。
借用原文：repetitive behaviours which often indicate boredom

questions.stem: Why have some animal species likely become used to the presence of humans?

options.label: A
options.text: They socialise with zookeepers as well as with each other.

options.label: B
options.text: They show good adaptability to living with humans.

options.label: C
options.text: They have been kept as pets by humans.

options.label: D
options.text: They have been born and raised in zoos.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） They have been born and raised in zoos.
【定位】Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to
the presence of humans.
有些动物物种在动物园出生、长大，因此可能已经习惯了人类的存在。
【信号】因果连词 and so 把原因和结果钉在一起。题干中的 'become used to the presence of
humans' 与答案句后半句完全对应，前半句 'have been born and raised in zoos' 由 and
so 引出，正是问题要的 why。
【替换】have been born and raised in zoos ↔ They have been born and raised in zoos.
原因部分被原样截取，主语由 Some animal species 换成 They
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
elephants socialised more with each other 是 Paragraph 1 中关于大象的发现，与题干
问的 'some animal species' 习惯人类无关，且 zookeepers 在录音中从未出现。
借用原文：socialised more with each other
B) 答非所问
录音确实提到 some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing
conditions of visitors，但这是习惯人类之后表现出的能力，是结果；题干问 why，B 项答
非所问。
借用原文：good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors
C) 未提及 录音只说 born and raised in zoos 导致习惯人类存在，从未提到 as pets。

questions.stem: What is Denver doing with its popular electric bike incentive program?

options.label: A
options.text: Adjusting it.

options.label: B
options.text: Suspending it.

options.label: C
options.text: Reevaluating it.

options.label: D
options.text: Expanding it.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Suspending it.
【定位】Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.
丹佛正在暂停其受欢迎的电动自行车激励项目。
【信号】新闻首句直接点题。Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program
位于新闻首句，直接回答了 What is Denver doing 的问题；suspending 与选项 B 的核心
动词完全一致。
【替换】is suspending ↔ Suspending it
现在进行时动作直接对应
【排除】A) 答非所问
选项 A 的 Adjusting 看似与原文 plans design changes 沾边，但 design changes 是
plan（计划），不是当前正在做的动作，且题干问的是 doing（现在进行）。
借用原文：plans design changes to make participation easier
C) 未提及 选项 C 的 Reevaluating 在录音中没有对应表述，属于凭空捏造。
D) 偷换概念
选项 D 的 Expanding it 容易被 increase access to the program 诱惑，但 increase
access 是 plans（未来设计目标），且项目当前是暂停而非扩张。
借用原文：increase access to the program

questions.stem: How did the electric bike incentive program benefit residents?

options.label: A
options.text: They could buy an electric bike for $400 in April.

options.label: B
options.text: They could buy their first electric bike at a discount.

options.label: C
options.text: They could enjoy free after-sale service for their purchase.

options.label: D
options.text: They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified.
【定位】It allowed Denver residents to apply for $400 in government funds before buying an electric
bike from a participating shop. Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify
for $1,200.
它允许丹佛居民在从参与商店购买电动自行车之前申请400美元的政府资金。符合特定收入
资格的居民可以获得1,200美元。
【信号】居民获益的具体说明。题干 benefit residents 问居民如何受益，原文 allowed Denver
residents to apply for $400 和 Residents who met certain income qualifications
could qualify for $1,200 正是对居民所获资助的直接说明。
【替换】Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200 ↔
They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified
同义替换：资格条件与获得资助的改写
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 A 把 $400 in government funds 和 launched in April 两个原词拼凑成 buy an
electric bike for $400 in April，但原文说的是申请 $400 资金，不是花 $400 买车；April
是项目启动时间，不是买车时间。
借用原文：$400 in government funds before buying an electric bike; launched in April
B) 原词陷阱
选项 B 盗用原文 buying an electric bike，但原文说的是申请政府补贴，不是直接打折；
discount 在录音中并未出现。
借用原文：buying an electric bike from a participating shop
C) 未提及 选项 C 的 after-sale service 在原文中没有对应内容，属于无中生有。

questions.stem: What does the city of Denver expect to do early next year?

options.label: A
options.text: Put 400 more electric bikes on its streets.

options.label: B
options.text: Increase the program funding by 8 percent.

options.label: C
options.text: Resume its electric bike incentive program.

options.label: D
options.text: Invest millions of dollars into the local economy.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Resume its electric bike incentive program.
【定位】The city expects to resume the program early next year.
该市预计将于明年初恢复该项目。
【信号】题干关键词直接复现。原文 expects to resume the program early next year 与题干
expect to do early next year 的关键词 expects / early next year 直接对应，resume 就
是答案动作。
【替换】expects to resume the program early next year ↔ Resume its electric bike incentive program
同义替换：resume the program = Resume its electric bike incentive program
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 A 把 $400 和 put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets 拼凑成 Put 400 more electric
bikes on its streets，数字和时态都错了。
借用原文：$400 in government funds; put 4,400 electric bikes on the streets of Denver
B) 偷换概念
选项 B 的 8 percent 在原文中没有依据，可能是把 68% of the program funding 误听或
篡改而来。
借用原文：68% of the program funding
D) 与原文相反
选项 D 盗用原文 invested $8.6 million into the local economy，但原文用的是 invested
（已完成），而题干问的是 expect to do early next year（未来计划），时态不符。
借用原文：invested $8.6 million into the local economy

questions.stem: What exhibits does the man like best in the museum he visited?

options.label: A
options.text: The coin collection.

options.label: B
options.text: The primitive tools.

options.label: C
options.text: The ancient ornaments.

options.label: D
options.text: The 2,000-year-old clothes.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） The coin collection.
【定位】The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life, but my favorite is the
coin collection.
早期人类使用的原始工具能告诉我们很多关于他们生活的信息，但我最喜欢的是硬币收藏。
【信号】转折 but + favorite 点出最爱。男士先提 The primitive tools，随即用 but my favorite
is 把重点转向 coin collection，favorite 与题干 like best 同义。
【替换】my favorite is the coin collection ↔ The coin collection.
favorite = like best
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
The primitive tools. 确实出现在 The primitive tools early humans used...，但它是 but
之前的铺垫，与 like best 无关。
借用原文：The primitive tools early humans used tell a lot about their life
C) 未提及 录音中只提到 tools 与 coin collection，完全没有 ornaments 这一展品。
D) 偷换概念
The 2,000-year-old clothes. 盗用了 over 2,000 years old 这一数字，但原文说的是
coins，不是 clothes。
借用原文：some coins that are over 2,000 years old

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the old city centre?

options.label: A
options.text: It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets.

options.label: B
options.text: It attracts visitors from every corner of the world.

options.label: C
options.text: It has flowers displayed around the Trevi Fountain.

options.label: D
options.text: It is more attractive than the pictures in guidebooks.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets.
【定位】The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm.
街道狭窄但很美，充满了魅力。
【信号】直接描述 + but 强调 beautiful/charm。女士用 narrow but beautiful with plenty of
charm 直接描述 old city centre 的街道，but 后的 beautiful 与 charm 是评价重心。
【替换】The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm ↔
It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets.
charm→charming，同词保留 narrow but beautiful
【排除】B) 张冠李戴
It attracts visitors from every corner of the world. 盗用 it's like the whole world is
here on holiday，但这是对整个城市旺季的感受，不是 old city centre 本身。
借用原文：it's like the whole world is here on holiday
C) 原词陷阱
It has flowers displayed around the Trevi Fountain. 盗用 with flowers，但 flowers 是
在 Spanish steps 的台阶上，不是 Trevi Fountain 周围。
借用原文：with flowers that go up to a church
D) 过度推断
It is more attractive than the pictures in guidebooks. 中的 guidebooks 出现在 in all
the guidebooks，但女士只说 Trevi Fountain 上了 guidebooks，并未比较吸引力。
借用原文：in all the guidebooks

questions.stem: What does the man say about the square with the Spanish steps?

options.label: A
options.text: It is covered with wild grass.

options.label: B
options.text: It is very famous and pretty.

options.label: C
options.text: It is located away from an old church.

options.label: D
options.text: It is surrounded by Spanish-style houses.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） It is very famous and pretty.
【定位】It's a square where on one side, there are some very wide steps with flowers that go up to a
church. It's also in all the tourist guidebooks. It's very famous and pretty.
这是一个广场，其中一侧有非常宽阔、饰满鲜花的台阶通向一座教堂。它也在所有旅游指南
里。它非常有名而且漂亮。
【信号】连续介绍后 famous/pretty 给出评价。男士先说明 square 的物理特征，再用 It's very
famous and pretty. 给出总体评价，这是问题的直接回答。
【替换】It's very famous and pretty. ↔ It is very famous and pretty.
It's → It is 缩写展开，形容词原词保留
【排除】A) 未提及 录音提到 wide steps with flowers，完全没有 wild grass。
C) 与原文相反
It is located away from an old church. 与 steps with flowers that go up to a church 相
反。
借用原文：steps with flowers that go up to a church
D) 原词陷阱
It is surrounded by Spanish-style houses. 盗用 Spanish 一词，但原文只说 square with
the Spanish steps，未提 surrounding houses。
借用原文：visiting the square with the Spanish steps

questions.stem: What does the woman say she is going to do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Ask Kathy what her plan is.

options.label: B
options.text: Tell Kathy Mike will join them.

options.label: C
options.text: Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square.

options.label: D
options.text: Tell Kathy Mike would like to have a change.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square.
【定位】Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it.
让我先问问她，但我相信她会愿意的。
【信号】first 直接对应题干 first。女士用 Let me ask her first 明确动作的先后顺序，first 与题干
first 同词对应。
【替换】Let me ask her first ↔ Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square.
ask her → Ask Kathy；语境指约她看 square
【排除】A) 答非所问
Ask Kathy what her plan is. 把 ask her 曲解为询问计划，但前文已计划去看 square，实
际问的是愿不愿意加入。
B) 偷换概念
Tell Kathy Mike will join them. 把 ask 偷换成 tell，且 Kathy 是否加入尚未确定，不能提
前告知。
D) 张冠李戴
Tell Kathy Mike would like to have a change. 盗用 Doing tourist stuff with others
would be a welcome change，但这是 Mike 的想法，不是女士要 first 做的事。
借用原文：Doing tourist stuff with others would be a welcome change

questions.stem: What advice does the man want to get from the woman?

options.label: A
options.text: How to fit into the bigger picture.

options.label: B
options.text: How to get on with colleagues.

options.label: C
options.text: How to create a solid first impression.

options.label: D
options.text: How to succeed in a new job.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） How to succeed in a new job.
【定位】Can you give me advice about being successful at a new job? I start mine next week.
你能给我一些关于在新工作中取得成功的建议吗？我下周开始新工作。
【信号】开门见山的请求句。对话首句即以 Can you give me advice about… 直接提出求助，后接
I start mine next week 点明新工作背景，是整段对话的总起与问题来源。
【替换】being successful at a new job ↔ How to succeed in a new job.
同义转写
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
How to fit into the bigger picture. 中的 bigger picture 确实在 P10 出现，但它是女士后
续建议的内容，不是男士最初想获得的建议。
借用原文：fits into the bigger picture
B) 原词陷阱
How to get on with colleagues. 中的 colleagues 相关概念在 P3 出现，但那是男士表示
意识到同事重要性，并非他向女士寻求的核心建议。
借用原文：collaborate with my coworkers
C) 张冠李戴
How to create a solid first impression. 几乎原样出现在 P2，但那是女士给的第一条建
议，不是男士主动求的建议。
借用原文：create a solid first impression

questions.stem: What does the woman say is the most important thing for the man to do at first?

options.label: A
options.text: Get familiar with all the details of his job description.

options.label: B
options.text: Learn about the relations within the organization.

options.label: C
options.text: Recognize his own limitations and weaknesses.

options.label: D
options.text: Understand his role from various perspectives.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Understand his role from various perspectives.
【定位】The most important thing for you to do at first is to understand your role from
multiple perspectives.
你一开始要做的最重要的事，就是从多个角度理解你的角色。
【信号】最高级 + 建议句。The most important thing…is to… 是典型的答案信号，直接给出女士
认为的最优先行动。
【替换】understand your role from multiple perspectives ↔
Understand his role from various perspectives.
同义词替换
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Get familiar with all the details of his job description. 中的 job description 在 P6 原词
出现，但录音说的是 what you do is not just limited to your job description，即「不只
限于岗位描述」，恰恰否定了此项。
借用原文：job description
B) 偷换概念
Learn about the relations within the organization. 对应 how your work relates to
other people within the organization，但那是解释「为什么要多角度理解角色」的原
因，不是 the most important thing 本身。
借用原文：how your work relates to other people within the organization
C) 未提及
录音中没有任何地方提到 limitations and weaknesses 或让男士认识自身弱点。

questions.stem: What does the man say he is feeling a bit uneasy about?

options.label: A
options.text: Learning history.

options.label: B
options.text: Meeting his boss.

options.label: C
options.text: Creating reports for other departments to use.

options.label: D
options.text: Leaving his coworkers in the present company.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Meeting his boss.
【定位】I'm feeling a bit uneasy about meeting my boss as well.
我对去见我的老板也感到有点不安。
【信号】情感表达 + about 对象。feeling a bit uneasy about meeting my boss 直接陈述男士的
情绪及其对象。
【替换】meeting my boss ↔ Meeting his boss.
原词复现，人称转换
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Learning history. 中的 history 在 P9 出现，但那是男士举例「了解公司历史」，并非他感
到不安的对象。
借用原文：history of the company
C) 原词陷阱
Creating reports for other departments to use. 中的 reports 和 department 在 P7 出
现，但那是男士用来举例说明工作关联性，与不安情绪无关。
借用原文：reports that I create at the end of the month may be used by a team in
another department
D) 与原文相反
Leaving his coworkers in the present company. 中的 leaving 与录音中 collaborate
with my coworkers 的「合作」态度相反，且录音未提及任何离职/离开含义。
借用原文：collaborate with my coworkers

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man do to gain insight about the running of the business?

options.label: A
options.text: Get to know the decision-makers.

options.label: B
options.text: Acquire decision-making authority.

options.label: C
options.text: Promote its products and services.

options.label: D
options.text: Observe its overall management.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Get to know the decision-makers.
【定位】However, it's crucial that you get to know the people who have decision-making authority to
gain insight regarding how the business is run and decisions are made.
然而，你必须去认识那些有决策权的人，以便了解企业是如何运作、决策是如何做出的。
【信号】建议句 + 目的状语。it's crucial that you get to know…to gain insight regarding… 中，
主句给出建议动作，不定式给出目的，正好对应题干 to gain insight about the running
of the business。
【替换】get to know the people who have decision-making authority ↔ Get to know the decision-makers.
名词化同义替换
【排除】B) 偷换概念
Acquire decision-making authority. 盗用 decision-making authority 原词，但原文说的
是「认识拥有决策权的人」，而非男士自己去「获取」决策权。
借用原文：people who have decision-making authority
C) 原词陷阱
Promote its products and services. 中的 products and services 在 P10 出现，但那是
「了解公司业务」的内容，不是「了解企业运作与决策」的建议。
借用原文：products and services that the company exists to deliver
D) 过度推断
Observe its overall management. 看似与 how the business is run 相关，但原文具体建
议是「认识决策者」，而非泛泛地「观察整体管理」。
借用原文：how the business is run and decisions are made

questions.stem: What does research indicate about many consumers when they evaluate a purchase?

options.label: A
options.text: They do not tell marketers their feeling about a product.

options.label: B
options.text: They do not compare competing brands and prices.

options.label: C
options.text: They are not hesitant to contradict themselves.

options.label: D
options.text: They are not sure what they really like to buy.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） They do not compare competing brands and prices.
【定位】Many consumers report comparing multiple competing brands and prices when evaluating a
purchase. However, research indicates that this is not actually the case.
许多消费者声称自己在评估购买时会比较多个竞争品牌和价格。然而，研究表明事实并非
如此。
【信号】转折 however 否定前文自我报告。However, research indicates that this is not actually
the case. 中的 however 把前一句消费者自我报告的内容推翻，research indicates 后的否
定才是答案所在。
【替换】research indicates that this is not actually the case ↔
They do not compare competing brands and prices.
否定前文的同义改写
【排除】A) 偷换概念
原文讨论的是消费者真实想法与所说之间的矛盾，并非'是否告诉营销人员感受'，选项把话
题偷换成 marketers。
C) 原词陷阱
They are not hesitant to contradict themselves. 盗用了原文 What consumers really
think or feel often contradicts what they say. 中的 contradict，但原文是'所想/所感与所
说矛盾'，并非'毫不犹豫地自相矛盾'。
借用原文：What consumers really think or feel often contradicts what they say.
D) 未提及
原文只说消费者被 unconscious urges / emotion 驱动，并未说他们'不确定自己喜欢买什
么'，属于根据常识编造的选项。

questions.stem: What do good marketers keep in mind all the time?

options.label: A
options.text: Consumers are often attracted by new products.

options.label: B
options.text: Consumers tend to make decisions on the spot.

options.label: C
options.text: Consumers find it hard to resist temptation.

options.label: D
options.text: Consumers are actually driven by emotion.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Consumers are actually driven by emotion.
【定位】Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general.
Good marketers keep in mind this important fact all the time, and examples of emotion-based
campaigns are everywhere.
情感才是真正驱动购买行为、乃至一般决策的东西。优秀的营销人员始终牢记这一重要事
实，基于情感的营销活动例子比比皆是。
【信号】指代 this important fact 回指前句主旨。Good marketers keep in mind this
important fact all the time 中的 this important fact 明确回指上一句 Emotion is what
really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general.，答案就
在前一句。
【替换】Emotion is what really drives the purchasing behaviors, and also, decision making in general. ↔
Consumers are actually driven by emotion.
主动变被动，drive 同根转换
【排除】A) 未提及
原文提到 marketing campaigns 和各类产品，但从未说消费者'被新产品吸引'，属于无中
生有。
B) 原词陷阱
Consumers tend to make decisions on the spot. 盗用了原文 decision making in
general 中的 decision，但原文讲的是'决策一般被情感驱动'，不是'当场做决定'。
借用原文：decision making in general
C) 未提及
原文讲 emotion / unconscious urges 驱动消费者，但并未出现 temptation 或'难以抗拒
诱惑'的表述。

questions.stem: What should marketers do besides stressing the features of a product?

options.label: A
options.text: Draw consumers' attention to the luxury goods symbolizing quality life.

options.label: B
options.text: Leave consumers the impression they are doing nothing manipulative.

options.label: C
options.text: Highlight the emotional response it will trigger in the consumer.

options.label: D
options.text: Remind consumers of the wide connections it can help to build.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Highlight the emotional response it will trigger in the consumer.
【定位】As marketers, we should focus on the features of the product, but we must also sell the
lifestyle and the feeling. The key is to highlight the emotional response a consumer will have
by using the product.
作为营销人员，我们应该关注产品特性，但也必须推销生活方式和感觉。关键是突出消费者
使用产品后产生的情感反应。
【信号】but / also 补充 + The key is to 强调。but we must also sell the lifestyle and the
feeling 先补充应做之事，随后 The key is to highlight the emotional response... 用 The
key is to 进一步强调核心动作，答案落在这里。
【替换】highlight the emotional response a consumer will have by using the product ↔
Highlight the emotional response it will trigger in the consumer.
同义替换：have by using → trigger in
【排除】A)
Draw consumers' attention to the luxury goods symbolizing quality life. 盗用原文
Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world.
中的 luxury goods，但该句只是论证情感营销的例子，不是题干问的'除了 features 还应该
做什么'。
借用原文：Luxury goods target our feelings of self-worth, acceptance, and status in the world.
B) 原词陷阱
Leave consumers the impression they are doing nothing manipulative. 盗用原文
There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states of
emotion. 中的 manipulative，但原文是在为情感营销辩护，不是把它作为营销人员'应该做
的事'。
借用原文：There's nothing manipulative about helping consumers achieve desired states
of emotion.
D)
Remind consumers of the wide connections it can help to build. 盗用原文
Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a
broader network of people. 中的 connection / broader network，但这只是
communication devices 的例子，不是营销人员的总体做法。
借用原文：Communication devices excite us by offering a connection to friends, family and a
broader network of people.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about Americans?

options.label: A
options.text: They are taking in a lot of plastic.

options.label: B
options.text: They are polluting the environment.

options.label: C
options.text: They consume much processed food.

options.label: D
options.text: They make everything with plastics.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） They are taking in a lot of plastic.
【定位】Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic.
美国人正在摄入并吸入大量塑料。
【信号】段首总领句。Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic. 是第二段首
句，开门见山给出美国人摄入塑料的结论。
【替换】Americans are consuming and breathing in a lot of plastic ↔ taking in a lot of plastic
同义概括
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
原文 they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the
environment 说的是塑料 escape 到环境中，而不是美国人正在污染环境。
借用原文：they escaped the confines of packaging and objects and settled in the environment
C) 未提及
短文只提到 food we eat、the average American diet，没有说美国人 consume much
processed food。
D) 原词陷阱
原文 Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us
的主语是 plastics，而不是 Americans。
借用原文：Plastics have for years been used to make nearly everything that surrounds us

questions.stem: What counted as the biggest sources for Americans breathing in or consuming microplastics?

options.label: A
options.text: Beer, salts and added sugars.

options.label: B
options.text: Tap water and take-away food.

options.label: C
options.text: Food packages and plastic bags.

options.label: D
options.text: Air, bottled water and seafood.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Air, bottled water and seafood.
【定位】Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for
breathed-in or consumed microplastics.
数据显示，对美国人而言，空气、瓶装水和海鲜是吸入或摄入微塑料的最大来源。
【信号】Data shows＋最高级 biggest。Data shows that for Americans, air, bottled water and
seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics. 中
Data shows 引出结论，biggest sources 直接对应题干的 biggest sources。
【替换】air, bottled water and seafood were the biggest sources for breathed-in or consumed microplastics
↔ Air, bottled water and seafood
原词复现
【排除】A) 答非所问
原文 Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed
minimal amounts 说明啤酒、盐、添加糖所占比例更少或极小，不是 biggest sources。
借用原文：Added sugars accounted for less, and salts, tap water and beer contributed
minimal amounts
B) 偷换概念
原文 salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts 说明 tap water 是极小
量，不是最大来源；take-away food 则根本没出现。
借用原文：salts, tap water and beer contributed minimal amounts
C) 未提及
Food packages and plastic bags 听起来像塑料来源，但原文说的是 larger plastic
objects fragment into smaller pieces，并未把它们列为最大来源。

questions.stem: What does the passage say is still unknown?

options.label: A
options.text: How much plastic there is in the remaining 85% of Americans' typical diet.

options.label: B
options.text: What measures can be taken to prevent plastic objects from fragmenting.

options.label: C
options.text: What harm microplastics may actually do to the average Americans.

options.label: D
options.text: How many ways there are for microplastics to get into food and air.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） How much plastic there is in the remaining 85% of Americans' typical diet.
【定位】It's not yet known how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet.
典型饮食中剩余 85% 含有多少塑料尚不清楚。
【信号】not yet known 直接对应 unknown。It's not yet known how much plastic is
contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet. 中的 not yet known 与题干 still
unknown 同义。
【替换】how much plastic is contained in the remaining 85% of the typical diet ↔
How much plastic there is in the remaining 85% of Americans' typical diet
同义改写
【排除】B) 未提及
原文 Many start off as part of larger plastic objects, which over time fragment into
smaller and smaller pieces until they become tiny 只讲碎片化过程，没有讲如何
prevent。
借用原文：Many start off as part of larger plastic objects, which over time fragment into smaller
and smaller pieces until they become tiny
C) 未提及 短文只谈了微塑料的摄入量和来源，没有讲 harm 或实际危害。
D) 答非所问
原文 Microplastics get into food and air in several ways 已经说明有几种途径，因此“有
多少种方式”不是 still unknown。
借用原文：Microplastics get into food and air in several ways

questions.stem: What did over half of the respondents say in the survey?

options.label: A
options.text: They planned to adopt a pet animal.

options.label: B
options.text: They kept not only a dog but a cat.

options.label: C
options.text: They had at least one pet.

options.label: D
options.text: They liked cats more than dogs.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） They had at least one pet.
【定位】55% said they owned at least one pet.
55%的人说他们至少养了一只宠物。
【信号】数字比例直接作答。题干问『超过半数受访者说了什么』，而55% said they owned at
least one pet中55%正好对应over half，数字句就是答案句。
【替换】55% ↔ over half
数字同义替换
owned at least one pet ↔ had at least one pet
同义词替换
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
They planned to adopt a pet animal盗用了adopt a pet animal原词，但原文主语是
People looking to stay well as they age（希望保持健康的老年人），且说的是may want
to（可能想），并非调查中过半受访者的实际行为。
借用原文：People looking to stay well as they age may want to adopt a pet animal
B) 偷换概念
They kept not only a dog but a cat把原文Dogs were the most common pet, followed
by cats曲解为『同时养狗和猫』，但原文只说明狗最常见、猫次之，并未说同一人同时养两
种。
借用原文：Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats
D) 与原文相反
They liked cats more than dogs与原文Dogs were the most common pet, followed by
cats相反，原文表明狗比猫更常见，即人们更常养狗而非更喜欢猫。
借用原文：Dogs were the most common pet, followed by cats

questions.stem: What did most older pet owners in the survey say their pets provided?

options.label: A
options.text: A sense of pride.

options.label: B
options.text: A sense of duty.

options.label: C
options.text: A sense of purpose.

options.label: D
options.text: A sense of security.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） A sense of purpose.
【定位】Nearly 90% of older pet owners said their animals helped them enjoy life and feel loved;
roughly 80% said their pets reduced stress; and almost three-quarters said their pets provided
a sense of purpose.
近90%的老年宠物主人表示，他们的动物帮助他们享受生活并感到被爱；约80%的人说宠物
减轻了他们的压力；近四分之三的人说宠物给了他们一种目标感。
【信号】排比列举中的第三项。原文Nearly 90%...; roughly 80%...; and almost three-quarters
said their pets provided a sense of purpose用排比列举宠物带来的三种好处，题干问
『most』对应的是almost three-quarters（近四分之三）这一组，其后的provided a
sense of purpose即为答案。
【替换】almost three-quarters ↔ most
比例同义替换
their pets provided a sense of purpose ↔ A sense of purpose
原词复现
【排除】A) 未提及
A sense of pride中的pride在原文P2的排比列举中并未出现，原文只提到enjoy life、feel
loved、reduced stress和a sense of purpose。
B) 未提及
A sense of duty中的duty在原文P2中未出现；虽然照顾宠物可能隐含责任，但原文并未把
它作为宠物『提供』给主人的感受。
D) 未提及
A sense of security中的security在原文P2中未出现，原文只提到feel loved（感到被爱）
和reduced stress（减轻压力），并未涉及安全感。

questions.stem: What does the passage say people did report in the survey?

options.label: A
options.text: A few problems with keeping big animals.

options.label: B
options.text: Some disadvantages related to pet ownership.

options.label: C
options.text: A few cases of getting attacked by pet animals.

options.label: D
options.text: Some conflicts with neighbors due to pet keeping.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Some disadvantages related to pet ownership.
【定位】However, people did report a few disadvantages to pet ownership.
然而，人们确实报告了一些养宠物的缺点。
【信号】转折词however引出负面信息。前文P2讲宠物带来的种种好处，随后用However一转，引
出people did report a few disadvantages to pet ownership，正好对应题干所问。
【替换】a few disadvantages to pet ownership ↔ Some disadvantages related to pet ownership
同义替换+限定词替换
【排除】A) 未提及
A few problems with keeping big animals中的big animals在原文P2中并未出现，原文
只泛泛讨论pet ownership，未限定动物体型。
C) 偷换概念
A few cases of getting attacked by pet animals把原文6% of pet owners said they'd
fallen or injured themselves as a result of having a pet中的injured偷换为attacked by
pet animals，受伤不等于被动物攻击。
借用原文：6% of pet owners said they'd fallen or injured themselves as a result of having a pet
D) 未提及
Some conflicts with neighbors due to pet keeping中的neighbors和conflicts在原文P2
中均未提及，原文提到的缺点是difficulty traveling和financial strains。

questions.stem: What does research show interacting with pets can do?

options.label: A
options.text: Reduce as many symptoms of depression as medical help.

options.label: B
options.text: Improve people's health as much as physical activities.

options.label: C
options.text: Lower older people's stress as effectively as exercising.

options.label: D
options.text: Bring many of the same benefits as human social support.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Bring many of the same benefits as human social support.
【定位】Human social support comes with a host of health benefits—less stress, lower rates of long-
term disease and more—and research shows that interacting with pets can bring many of the
same benefits.
人类的社会支持带来诸多健康益处——压力更小、长期疾病发病率更低等等——研究表明，
与宠物互动也能带来许多同样的益处。
【信号】研究结论句直接作答。题干问research show interacting with pets can do，原文
research shows that interacting with pets can bring many of the same benefits直接
给出研究结论，是答案句。
【替换】interacting with pets can bring many of the same benefits ↔
Bring many of the same benefits as human social support
原句概括+比较对象补全
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Reduce as many symptoms of depression as medical help盗用了原文reduce
symptoms of depression原词，但额外添加了as...as medical help这一原文没有的医疗帮
助比较，属于强加了不存在的关系。
借用原文：animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety and encourage
physical activity
B) 偷换概念
Improve people's health as much as physical activities把原文encourage physical
activity（鼓励身体活动）偷换成『与身体活动效果一样好』，并添加了as much as比较，
原文并未将养宠物与physical activities作效果比较。
借用原文：animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety and encourage
physical activity
C) 偷换概念
Lower older people's stress as effectively as exercising把原文animals can lower stress
和encourage physical activity两个独立好处拼接成『降低压力的效果与锻炼一样好』，但
原文并未将lower stress与exercising进行效果比较。
借用原文：animals can lower stress, reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety and encourage
physical activity
