questions.stem: What does the news report say about Vaclav Bursa and Joanna Stephens?

options.label: A
options.text: They are young teenagers from Atlanta.

options.label: B
options.text: They won this year's 7 Mile Bridge Run.

options.label: C
options.text: They completed the race in less than 40 minutes.

options.label: D
options.text: They are both students at Marathon High School.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） They won this year's 7 Mile Bridge Run.
【定位】Vaclav Bursa, 15, of Big Pine Key, Florida, finished first overall. ... Joanna Stephens, 28, of
Atlanta, completed the course in 41 minutes and 12 seconds. She won the women's division
title and placed second overall.
来自佛罗里达州大派恩礁的 15 岁的瓦茨拉夫·布尔萨获得总排名第一。……来自亚特兰大的
28 岁的乔安娜·斯蒂芬斯以 41 分 12 秒完成赛程。她赢得女子组冠军，总排名第二。
【信号】两人各自的名次陈述。答案句不靠转折词，而靠「人物+成绩」的并列陈述定位：finished
first overall 和 won the women's division title 分别说明两人都拿了各自组别第一——他
们都是「这场 7 Mile Bridge Run 的获胜者」，这正是选项 B 的概括。
【替换】finished first overall ↔ won this year's 7 Mile Bridge Run
「总排名第一」=「赢了这场比赛」
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
选项盗了原文真实出现的地名「Atlanta」诱你听到就选，但 Atlanta 只属于 28 岁的
Stephens；15 岁的 Bursa 来自 Florida。说两人「都是来自亚特兰大的青少年」既错配了
城市，又把 28 岁的人也算成 teenager，双重不符。
借用原文：Joanna Stephens, 28, of Atlanta
C) 与原文相反
原文用时是 41 minutes and 1 second 与 41 minutes and 12 seconds，都是 41 分多，
明明大于 40 分钟；选项偏说「less than 40 minutes（少于 40 分钟）」。它盗用了「分钟
数」这个耳熟数字，却把实际 41 多分钟篡改成「不到 40 分」，方向正好相反。
借用原文：41 minutes and 1 second
D) 原词陷阱
「Marathon High School」原文确实出现，极易让人听到就选；但原文只说 He is a
student at Marathon High School，这个「He」指 Bursa 一人。选项说两人「都是
（both）」该校学生，把只属于 Bursa 的身份硬扣给了 Stephens。
借用原文：He is a student at Marathon High School

questions.stem: What do we learn about the April contest?

options.label: A
options.text: It drew competitors from more than 40 countries.

options.label: B
options.text: It is watched live online by fans all over the world.

options.label: C
options.text: It closed the city of Big Pine Key to traffic for three hours.

options.label: D
options.text: It is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern U.S.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） It is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern U.S.
【定位】The April contest is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States.
这场四月的赛事是美国东南部最受欢迎的跑步活动之一。
【信号】最高级定性句即结论。答案句靠最高级信号锁定：one of the most popular running
events in the southeastern United States 是对赛事地位的定性总结，几乎与选项 D 逐字
对应。听到「one of the most…」这种最高级评价句，要立刻意识到它往往就是某道题的
答案落点。
【替换】one of the most popular running events in the southeastern United States ↔
It is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern U.S.
几乎逐字对应，仅缩写化
【排除】A) 偷换概念
原文说 drew competitors from 41 US states——来自 41 个「州」，另有 Canada, the
UK and Switzerland 等少数几国选手。选项盗用「40 多」这个数量级，却把「states
（州）」偷换成「countries（国家）」，参赛国其实只有零星几个，远到不了 40 个。
借用原文：The race drew competitors from 41 US states.
B) 未提及
原文涉及「online」的只有 online registration opened in January——指线上「报名」，
全文从未说有人「在线观看直播（watched live online）」。选项把「线上报名」悄悄换成
「全球粉丝线上观看」，是没有原文支撑的编造。
借用原文：after online registration opened in January
C) 原词陷阱
原文是 closed the span between the Middle and Lower Keys to traffic for 3 hours
——封的是中、下礁岛之间的那段「桥/路」三小时；选项把「3 hours」和「closed」原样
搬来，却说封的是「the city of Big Pine Key（整座大派恩礁城）」，封闭对象被偷换了。
借用原文：The run closed the span between the Middle and Lower Keys to traffic for 3 hours
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 British astronaut Tim Peake is stepping down permanently from his role as a European astronaut. He's
going to take up a full-time position as ambassador for science and space instead—work he's been doing
since 2019. The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot was selected as a European Space
Agency astronaut in 2009. He flew to the space station for a 6-month tour in 2015. The tour saw him
control a robot on earth remotely from orbit. He also helped dock two spacecraft. Tim said, "Being an
astronaut has been the most extraordinary experience. I've had the privilege of working with an
exceptional team of individuals during the past 13 years with the agency. It has been incredibly exciting
and rewarding. By assuming the role of an ambassador for human flights to space, I'll continue to
support the European and the UK space agencies."

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about Tim Peake?

options.label: A
options.text: He was once a full-time ambassador.

options.label: B
options.text: He was soon to retire from the army.

options.label: C
options.text: He became an astronaut in 2015.

options.label: D
options.text: He used to be a helicopter pilot.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） He used to be a helicopter pilot.
【定位】The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot was selected as a European Space Agency
astronaut in 2009.
这位前英国陆军航空兵的直升机飞行员于 2009 年被选为欧洲航天局的宇航员。
【信号】former 点出'过去身份'。答案句开头的 The former British Army Air Corps helicopter
pilot 里 former(过去的)就是信号词：它直接交代了 Tim Peake 过去的身份是直升机飞行
员，正对 Q3 '关于他我们了解到什么'。
【替换】The former British Army Air Corps helicopter pilot ↔ He used to be a helicopter pilot.
former 名词 = used to be 动词
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
录音确实念到 ambassador，但说的是他将去 take up a full-time position as
ambassador——这是接下来要担任的新职，不是过去就当过；A 把'即将担任'说成 was
once(曾经是),时间方向错了。
借用原文：He's going to take up a full-time position as ambassador for science and space
B) 偷换概念
录音说的是他从'欧洲宇航员'岗位上 stepping down permanently from his role as a
European astronaut(永久卸任宇航员角色)，并非从军队退役；B 把'卸任宇航员'偷换成'即
将从军队退役'，army 一词也只在他过去身份里出现，并未说他要退役。
借用原文：Tim Peake is stepping down permanently from his role as a European astronaut
C) 张冠李戴
录音里 2015 对应的是 He flew to the space station for a 6-month tour in 2015.(2015
年飞往空间站)，而'被选为宇航员'是 selected as a European Space Agency astronaut in
2009(2009 年)；C 把 astronaut 与 2015 错配，年份张冠李戴。
借用原文：He flew to the space station for a 6-month tour in 2015.

questions.stem: What does Tim Peake say about his work with the European Space Agency?

options.label: A
options.text: It has been unbelievably exciting and rewarding.

options.label: B
options.text: It has been extraordinarily tough and demanding.

options.label: C
options.text: It has contributed a great deal to human flights to space.

options.label: D
options.text: It has given him exceptional privilege as an ambassador.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （态度观点题） It has been unbelievably exciting and rewarding.
【定位】It has been incredibly exciting and rewarding.
这(段经历)一直非常激动人心、收获满满。
【信号】引语里的评价形容词即落点。态度题的落点在当事人自述的评价词。录音引语里 It has
been incredibly exciting and rewarding. 用 exciting、rewarding 两个褒义形容词直接给
出他对工作的评价，正是答案句。
【替换】incredibly exciting and rewarding ↔ unbelievably exciting and rewarding
incredibly = unbelievably 同义替换
【排除】B) 与原文相反
extraordinarily tough and demanding 是负面评价，但他原话是 incredibly exciting and
rewarding(激动、有收获)这类褒义；B 把好评偷换成差评，极性正相反。录音里确有
extraordinary 一词(说 the most extraordinary experience)，B 借这个原词制造迷惑。
借用原文：Being an astronaut has been the most extraordinary experience.
C) 原词陷阱
录音确有 an ambassador for human flights to space 这串词，但那是讲他将担任的新角
色，不是评价这份工作'对航天贡献巨大'；题干问他怎么评价工作，C 答成'贡献'，是听到原
词就选的答非所问。
借用原文：By assuming the role of an ambassador for human flights to space
D) 张冠李戴
录音里 privilege 出现在 I've had the privilege of working with an exceptional team(有
幸与优秀团队共事)，讲的是与团队合作的荣幸，不是'作为 ambassador 的特殊荣誉'；D 把
privilege 和 ambassador 硬凑到一起，张冠李戴。
借用原文：I've had the privilege of working with an exceptional team of individuals

questions.stem: What do we learn about the five cats seen in the Asda store?

options.label: A
options.text: They are known for their loyalty to their owners.

options.label: B
options.text: They are brought in by the store's customers.

options.label: C
options.text: They are regular visitors to the store.

options.label: D
options.text: They are pets kept by the store staff.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） They are regular visitors to the store.
【定位】Regular shoppers at the supermarket are familiar with the sight of several cats settling down
in the shop aisles. There are now at least five different cats who come almost on a daily basis.
超市的常客们对几只猫在店内过道里安顿下来的景象已经习以为常。如今至少有五只不同的
猫几乎天天都来。
【信号】客观陈述句直接交代猫的常态。新闻里没有转折，答案就藏在平铺直叙交代事实的句子里：
several cats settling down in the shop aisles 配上 five different cats who come
almost on a daily basis，直接说明这几只猫是几乎天天来店里的常客。听到 "come
almost on a daily basis"（几乎每天都来）就该锁定这是答案句。
【替换】five different cats who come almost on a daily basis ↔ regular visitors to the store
"几乎每天来"="常客"
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
loyalty to their owners 抓住了录音里的 loyal 这个原词，可录音 The supermarket is
known for its loyal customers 说的是超市以"忠实顾客"闻名，忠诚指的是人、不是猫，更
没说猫忠于主人。听到 loyal 就选 A，正中原词陷阱。
借用原文：The supermarket is known for its loyal customers
B) 未提及
brought in by the store's customers 听起来合理，但录音明说猫是 wandered in and
made themselves comfortable（自己晃进来安顿下来），第一只是 one cat routinely
started visiting the store，没有任何"顾客带进来"的内容，属凭常识硬安、原文未提及。
借用原文：wandered in and made themselves comfortable
D) 原词陷阱
pets kept by the store staff 借了录音里的 staff 和 pet 两个原词，可录音里 Staff did
their best to discourage the pet from hanging around 说的是店员想方设法"赶"猫、不
让它逗留，恰恰说明猫不归店员所有。听到 staff、pet 就选 D，又是原词陷阱。
借用原文：Staff did their best to discourage the pet from hanging around

questions.stem: What did some customers think when they saw the first cat routinely appear in the store?

options.label: A
options.text: It might be a nuisance to the loyal shoppers.

options.label: B
options.text: It might have been abandoned by its owner.

options.label: C
options.text: It might be 12 months old.

options.label: D
options.text: It might have got lost.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） It might have got lost.
【定位】Local newspapers reported that puzzled customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find
out if the cat was lost.
当地报纸报道说，困惑的顾客在脸书群组里发帖，想弄清楚这只猫是不是走丢了。
【信号】顾客行为句直接道出"以为它丢了"。描述顾客当时反应的句子就是答案句：puzzled
customers posted on Facebook groups to try to find out if the cat was lost——困惑
的顾客发帖打听"猫是不是走丢了"。其中 if the cat was lost 直接点出顾客脑中的念头。听
到 puzzled（困惑的）和 lost 就该锁定。
【替换】to try to find out if the cat was lost ↔ It might have got lost.
"想弄清是否走丢"="它可能走丢了"
【排除】A) 答非所问
nuisance to the loyal shoppers 借了 loyal/shoppers 的影子，但录音里顾客看到第一只
猫时是 puzzled（困惑），去打听它是否走丢，并没有觉得它"惹人嫌"。猫多到要贴告示是
后文的事，且也没说它惹忠实顾客嫌，时间和内容都对不上。
借用原文：puzzled customers
B) 偷换概念
abandoned by its owner 与正解贴得最近，都是"它出事了"，但录音里顾客打听的是 if
the cat was lost（是否走丢），是"丢"不是"主人不要了"。况且下文 its owner assured
the concerned customers it was very much loved 说主人很爱它，根本没被遗弃。错在
偷换了"走丢"与"被弃"这两个相近却不同的概念。
借用原文：if the cat was lost
C) 原词陷阱
It might be 12 months old. 抓住录音真念过的 12 个月，但录音 The unusual situation
started about 12 months ago 说的是"这桩怪事大约始于 12 个月前"，12 个月是"猫开始
来店多久"，根本不是"猫 12 个月大"。听到 12 months 就选 C，是典型的数字原词陷阱。
借用原文：The unusual situation started about 12 months ago

questions.stem: What are customers asked not to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Feed the cats.

options.label: B
options.text: Remove any store signs.

options.label: C
options.text: Sit in the shop aisles.

options.label: D
options.text: Bring in pets with them.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Feed the cats.
【定位】They visit the store so much that staff have been forced to put up signs, asking their
customers not to feed them.
这些猫太常来店里，以至于店员不得不张贴告示，要求顾客不要喂它们。
【信号】请求句 asking…not to 直接给出禁止内容。答案句末尾的请求结构就是定位信号：asking
their customers not to feed them（要求顾客不要喂它们）。听到 not to + 动词，紧跟
的 feed 就是被禁止的那件事。这是"听要求句、抓 not to 后面的动作"的标准落点。
【替换】not to feed them ↔ Feed the cats.
"不要喂它们"对应被禁动作"喂猫"
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
Remove any store signs. 抓住录音真念过的 signs，可录音 staff have been forced to
put up signs 说的是店员"贴"告示，从没要求顾客"撤"告示。听到 signs 就选 B，正中原词
陷阱，且把"贴"反成了"撤"。
借用原文：staff have been forced to put up signs
C) 张冠李戴
Sit in the shop aisles. 借了录音原词 aisles，可录音 several cats settling down in the
shop aisles 说的是猫在过道里安顿，不是顾客坐过道，更没人要求顾客别坐。听到 aisles
就选 C，是原词陷阱加张冠李戴。
借用原文：several cats settling down in the shop aisles
D) 未提及
Bring in pets with them. 蹭了录音里的 pet 一词，但录音里店员唯一对顾客提的要求是
not to feed them（别喂猫），从没说过"别带宠物进店"。带宠物进店是凭常识联想出来
的，原文并未提及。
借用原文：asking their customers not to feed them

questions.stem: What has the woman been thinking of doing next semester?

options.label: A
options.text: Sharing her room with friends.

options.label: B
options.text: Cutting down her living expenses.

options.label: C
options.text: Living off campus.

options.label: D
options.text: Moving to the city center.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Living off campus.
【定位】W: I've been thinking about moving off campus next semester.
女：我一直在考虑下学期搬到校外去住。
【信号】开场首句直陈打算。信号是女方对话开场第一句的直接陈述 I've been thinking about
moving off campus next semester.，与题干 thinking of doing 完全对应——这就是承
载答案的那句。
【替换】moving off campus ↔ Living off campus
moving=living 同指搬离校园住
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
Sharing her room with friends. 借了后文女方说的 Three of my friends from the
dormitory would share the place with me，但那是『四人合租整套房子』，不是『与朋
友合住一个房间』，且非她最初的打算，是把后文细节错安到本题。
借用原文：Three of my friends from the dormitory would share the place with me
B) 原词陷阱
Cutting down her living expenses. 盗用了原文反复出现的 the expense 一词，但女方的
打算是搬出校外，省钱只是搬出后讨论的一个方面，不是她『在考虑做的事』本身，听到
expense 就选会落坑。
借用原文：And then there's the expense, too.
D) 与原文相反
Moving to the city center. 与原文正相反：女方说的是 if we move far enough from the
city center（搬到离市中心足够远的地方），选项却说搬向市中心，极性反了。
借用原文：if we move far enough from the city center

questions.stem: What does the man suggest the woman take into consideration?

options.label: A
options.text: The facilities available.

options.label: B
options.text: Various costs involved.

options.label: C
options.text: Changes in living conditions.

options.label: D
options.text: The distance to her home.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Various costs involved.
【定位】M: Are you sure about that? Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity
and gas. Have you factored those in?
男：你确定吗？大城市的房租很高，还有电费和燃气费。这些你都算进去了吗？
【信号】连列费用项+反问提醒。信号是男方一口气列出 Rents in big cities are high, and then
there's the cost of electricity and gas 并反问 Have you factored those in?——他反复
强调、要女方算进去的正是各项费用，这就是答案句。
【替换】Rents in big cities are high, and then there's the cost of electricity and gas ↔
Various costs involved
罗列各项费用=概括为各种费用
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
The facilities available. 看似贴居住话题，但原文男方提醒的是费用，厨房、卧室等设施是
后文女方自己列搬出去的好处 We'd have a kitchen，并非男方让她『考虑』的事，张冠李
戴。
借用原文：We'd have a kitchen, so we could cook ourselves.
C) 偷换概念
Changes in living conditions. 借用了贯穿全程的 living 一词，但男方让考虑的是『费用』
这一具体方面，不是笼统的『生活条件变化』，把具体范畴偷换成宽泛说法。
借用原文：if we move far enough from the city center, the rent is low enough
D) 原词陷阱
The distance to her home. 盗用了男方开头 so far from home 里的 home 一词，但那是
男方表达担忧的话，并非他要女方『纳入考虑』的方面，且真正反复提醒的是费用，听到
home 就选会落坑。
借用原文：living all by yourself in an apartment so far from home

questions.stem: What does the woman say she did during high school?

options.label: A
options.text: Went through much trouble.

options.label: B
options.text: Commuted to save money.

options.label: C
options.text: Studied on the bus.

options.label: D
options.text: Lived on campus.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Studied on the bus.
【定位】W: It's about an hour to campus, but there's no reason I can't study on the bus. After all, I did
that during high school and my commute was even longer then.
女：到学校大约一小时，但我没理由不能在公交车上学习啊。毕竟我高中时就是这么做的，
那时候我通勤路上的时间还更长呢。
【信号】时间词 during high school 处的回指。信号是题干时间词在原文的复现 I did that during
high school，而 that 回指紧挨着的 study on the bus——这句就是答案句。
【替换】I did that during high school ↔ Studied on the bus
that 回指 study on the bus
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
Went through much trouble. 借了男方的话 go through all that trouble，但那是男方对
『搬出去折腾』的评价，不是女方说她高中做过的事，把男方的话安到女方头上。
借用原文：go through all that trouble
B) 原词陷阱
Commuted to save money. 把原文出现的 commute（my commute was even longer）
和前文省钱话题拼在一起，但女方说高中时做的是在车上学习，并非『为省钱而通勤』，且
省钱是合租话题、不是高中经历。
借用原文：my commute was even longer then
D) 与原文相反
Lived on campus. 借用了贯穿全程的 campus、live 等词，但女方高中时是通勤
（commute 路上更长），恰恰说明她当时没住校，选项与原意相反。
借用原文：my commute was even longer then

questions.stem: What does the man say he'll do at the end of the conversation?

options.label: A
options.text: Discuss the matter with the woman's mother.

options.label: B
options.text: Make a decision within a few days.

options.label: C
options.text: Try his best to persuade his wife.

options.label: D
options.text: Weigh the benefits against the disadvantages.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Discuss the matter with the woman's mother.
【定位】M: I'm not convinced that the benefits are greater than the disadvantages, but I'll discuss this
with your mother.
男：我还不太相信好处大过坏处，不过我会和你妈妈商量一下这件事。
【信号】转折 but 后的 I'll 表态。信号是结尾男方转折词 but 之后的 I'll discuss this with your
mother——but 之后才是他真正要做的事，这就是答案句。
【替换】I'll discuss this with your mother ↔ Discuss the matter with the woman's mother
this=the matter、your mother=woman's mother
【排除】B) 未提及
Make a decision within a few days. 里 within a few days 录音从头到尾没出现，是凭
『商量后该尽快决定』的常识脑补出来的时限，原文未提。
C) 偷换概念
Try his best to persuade his wife. 把男方要找 mother（即他妻子）这层关系拿来，却说
成『努力说服妻子』，可原文是 discuss this with your mother——是平等商量，不是单
方说服，把『商量』偷换成『说服』。
借用原文：I'll discuss this with your mother
D) 原词陷阱
Weigh the benefits against the disadvantages. 盗用了同句 the benefits are greater
than the disadvantages 的原词，但那是男方表达『还没被说服』的态度（but 之前），不
是他说接下来要做的事；他要做的是商量，听到 benefits/disadvantages 就选会落坑。
借用原文：I'm not convinced that the benefits are greater than the disadvantages

questions.stem: What is the woman doing?

options.label: A
options.text: Interviewing the man.

options.label: B
options.text: Looking for Lawrence.

options.label: C
options.text: Choosing a present for her nephew.

options.label: D
options.text: Helping the man with his shopping.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Choosing a present for her nephew.
【定位】W: Good morning. I'm looking for a present for my nephew, Lawrence.
女：早上好。我在给我侄子劳伦斯找一份礼物。
【信号】开场自报来意。女士一开口就用 I'm looking for a present for my nephew 交代了来店目
的，这种"开场自述要做什么"的句子就是 What doing 题的答案句。
【替换】looking for a present for my nephew ↔ Choosing a present for her nephew
looking for=Choosing 同义改写
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
全程是女士向店员咨询、店员介绍商品，没有任何采访行为；Interviewing the man. 把"咨
询"误当"采访"，且弄反了谁主导对话。
B) 原词陷阱
录音确实念到了 Lawrence，但 Lawrence 是要送礼的侄子，女士并不是在"找劳伦斯本
人"；Looking for Lawrence. 偷了这个人名来骗"听到就选"。
借用原文：I'm looking for a present for my nephew, Lawrence
D) 与原文相反
是店员（男士）在帮女士选礼物，不是女士帮男士购物；Helping the man with his
shopping. 把帮忙的方向反了过来。

questions.stem: How does the man describe Bobo Man, the action figure?

options.label: A
options.text: Quite educational.

options.label: B
options.text: Incredibly popular.

options.label: C
options.text: Driven by batteries.

options.label: D
options.text: Obviously childish.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Incredibly popular.
【定位】M: For that age group, our biggest seller this year has been this action figure. It's called Bobo
Man, and it's incredibly popular.
男：对这个年龄段，我们今年卖得最好的就是这个人偶。它叫 Bobo Man，非常受欢迎。
【信号】店员正面推介的形容。男士介绍这件玩具时直接说 it's incredibly popular，这句正面评价
就是"他如何描述它"的答案句。
【替换】it's incredibly popular ↔ Incredibly popular.
原句直取，几乎零改写
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
educational 确实在录音出现，但那是女士后来问 something educational、指向拼图，并
非男士对 Bobo Man 的描述；Quite educational. 把后文别处的词搬来安到 Bobo Man 头
上。
借用原文：Perhaps something educational
C) 与原文相反
batteries 在录音里出现，但男士明确说 It has no batteries——它"没有"电池；Driven by
batteries. 取了原词却反了意思。
借用原文：It has no batteries
D) 未提及
录音从未把 Bobo Man 说成幼稚；男士只说它受欢迎、是动画主角。Obviously childish.
属于凭印象编的负面评价，原文无据。

questions.stem: What kind of game does the woman think would be good for Lawrence?

options.label: A
options.text: One he loves for helping exercise his mind.

options.label: B
options.text: One he can play together with his sister.

options.label: C
options.text: One he finds interesting and challenging.

options.label: D
options.text: One he can play either alone or in a group.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） One he can play together with his sister.
【定位】W: I like this sort of idea. Lawrence has a sister who is slightly older, so maybe a game that
they can play together would be good.
女：我喜欢这个主意。劳伦斯有个稍大一点的姐姐，所以也许一款他们能一起玩的游戏会
不错。
【信号】女士本人 so...would be good 的结论。女士先说有姐姐，再用 so maybe a game that
they can play together would be good 给出她看重的条件——"两人一起玩"，这正是
think...good 的答案句。
【替换】a game that they can play together ↔ One he can play together with his sister
they=他和姐姐，指代还原
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
exercising the mind 出现在录音，但那是男士介绍拼图时说 great for exercising the
mind，不是女士看重的理由；题干问的是女士的想法，故 One he loves for helping
exercise his mind. 张冠李戴。
借用原文：great for exercising the mind
C) 未提及
女士没有说看重"有趣又有挑战"；challenging 一词录音根本没出现。One he finds
interesting and challenging. 是凭印象编的卖点。
D) 张冠李戴
play either alone or in groups 确在录音，但那是男士介绍拼图的卖点 can be played
either alone or in groups，不是女士对劳伦斯看重的点；女士看重的是"和姐姐一起"。
One he can play either alone or in a group. 把店员的话当成女士的判断。
借用原文：can be played either alone or in groups

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about the game Battleships?

options.label: A
options.text: It has been enjoyed by kids for decades.

options.label: B
options.text: It always reminds people of times of war.

options.label: C
options.text: It has been played both indoors and outdoors.

options.label: D
options.text: It distinguishes itself as one of the oldest games.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） It has been enjoyed by kids for decades.
【定位】M: Of course you did. Everyone did. And kids enjoy it just as much today as you and I did
when we were young. Some games just never get old.
男：你当然玩过。人人都玩过。而且如今的孩子玩它玩得和当年的你我一样开心。有些游戏
就是永不过时。
【信号】多年仍受孩子喜爱的信息点。男士说 kids enjoy it just as much today as you and I did
when we were young，加上前文 It has been around since the 1930s，合起来支持"几
十年来一直被孩子喜爱"。
【替换】It has been around since the 1930s ↔ It has been enjoyed by kids for decades
since the 1930s=for decades
kids enjoy it just as much today as you and I did when we were young ↔
It has been enjoyed by kids for decades
孩子持续喜爱=enjoyed by kids
【排除】B) 过度推断
录音只说这游戏经典、不过时，从没说它"让人想起战争"。It always reminds people of
times of war. 是看 Battleships（战舰）这名字凭空联想，原文无据，且 always 太绝对。
C) 原词陷阱
女士提到 we had to stay indoors（下雨只能待室内玩），录音只说室内，从没说室外也
玩；It has been played both indoors and outdoors. 偷了 indoors 一词，却擅自加上
outdoors。
借用原文：we had to stay indoors
D) 过度推断
男士只说它是 a total classic、自 1930 年代就有，并没说它"是最古老的游戏之一"；It
distinguishes itself as one of the oldest games. 把"经典"拔高成"最古老之一"，程度过
头。
借用原文：It's a total classic

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about the paradox of choice?

options.label: A
options.text: A display of a variety of products increases consumers' interest.

options.label: B
options.text: Too many choices decrease one's desire to buy.

options.label: C
options.text: Fewer choices lead to lower customer satisfaction.

options.label: D
options.text: Customers given more choices are more likely to get confused.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Too many choices decrease one's desire to buy.
【定位】But here's the paradox of choice: if a person is presented with too many choices, they are
actually less likely to buy.
但这就是“选择悖论”：如果一个人面对太多选择，他实际上反而更不可能购买。
【信号】转折 But 加冒号点题，后半才是真意。前一句 We assume that if we offer our
customers more choices, then they'll be more likely to buy 是“我们以为”的错误假设，
紧跟 But here's the paradox of choice 用转折加冒号正式抛出概念，转折后的内容才是答
案句。
【替换】too many choices ↔ Too many choices
原词同形保留
less likely to buy ↔ decrease one's desire to buy
“更不可能买”=“降低购买欲”，同义改写
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 说陈列多样“增加兴趣”，借的是后文 created more interest里的 interest，但本题问的是
paradox of choice 的核心结论，原文用 But 推翻的正是“选项多就更想买”这种正向假设，
A 站在被推翻的一边。
借用原文：created more interest
C) 与原文相反
C 说“更少选择导致更低满意度”，盗用了原文 customer satisfaction 一词，但原文 the
bigger display of jams leads to lower customer satisfaction than the smaller display
说的是“更多”选择才满意度更低，C 把多少接反了，属与原文相反。
借用原文：lower customer satisfaction
D) 未提及
D 说顾客“get confused”（困惑），听上去像“选择多”的合理后果，但原文从头到尾只说更
不可能买、满意度更低，从未提到“困惑”，属凭常识脑补的未提及项。

questions.stem: What did the psychologists want to find out in their 2012 study about jams?

options.label: A
options.text: What kind of display results in more sales.

options.label: B
options.text: What kind of display creates more interest.

options.label: C
options.text: What kind of display attracts a greater crowd of customers.

options.label: D
options.text: What kind of display leads to greater customer satisfaction.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （目的题） What kind of display results in more sales.
【定位】Guess which display table led to more sales?
猜猜哪张陈列桌带来了更多销量？
【信号】设问句直接点出研究要回答的问题。原文以反问 Guess which display table led to more
sales?把整段研究的核心问题挑明——研究就是要看“哪种展示带来更多销量”，这个设问句
即研究目的的答案句。
【替换】which display table led to more sales ↔ What kind of display results in more sales.
“哪张桌带来更多销量”=“哪种陈列带来更多销量”
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
B 说研究想找“哪种展示引起更多兴趣”，借了原文 created more interest里的 interest，但
“更多兴趣”是研究顺带得出的结果，研究真正要找的是销量；B 把结果当成了研究目的。
借用原文：created more interest
C) 未提及
C 说研究想找哪种展示“吸引更大客流”，crowd of customers 原文压根没出现，是凭“大展
台显眼”的常识脑补出来的，属未提及。
D) 原词陷阱
D 说研究想找哪种展示带来“更高满意度”，借了原文 customer satisfaction 一词，但满意
度同样是研究附带得出的结论，不是 2012 研究设问要找的目标；与 B 同病，混淆结果与目
的。
借用原文：lower customer satisfaction

questions.stem: What is the finding of an extensive study published in 2015?

options.label: A
options.text: There are situations where customers buy nothing.

options.label: B
options.text: There are tricks to increase customer satisfaction.

options.label: C
options.text: There are ways to predict customer preferences.

options.label: D
options.text: There are rules that motivate customers to buy.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） There are rules that motivate customers to buy.
【定位】They found four rules that motivate consumers to buy: when people want to make a quick and
easy choice, when the product is complex, when it's difficult to compare alternatives, and
when consumers don't have clear preferences.
他们发现了促使消费者购买的四条规则：当人们想做一个又快又省事的选择时、当产品很复
杂时、当难以比较各个备选项时、以及当消费者没有明确偏好时。
【信号】found 加冒号列举，结论句标志。原文 They found four rules that motivate consumers
to buy以 found 引出、冒号后接四条列举，是这项 2015 研究的总结论句，正是“finding”
所在。
【替换】four rules that motivate consumers to buy ↔ There are rules that motivate customers to buy.
“motivate consumers to buy”=“motivate customers to buy”，近乎同形
【排除】A) 未提及
A 说研究发现“存在顾客什么都不买的情形”，听似贴合“选择多就不买”的主题，但 2015 研
究的发现明确是“four rules”，原文没说“buy nothing”，属把前文主题硬套到本题、未提
及。
B) 张冠李戴
B 说研究发现“提升满意度的技巧”，借了前文 customer satisfaction 一词，但满意度是前
一项果酱研究的内容，2015 研究找的是“促买规则”不是“提升满意度的技巧”，张冠李戴且偷
换概念。
借用原文：lower customer satisfaction
C) 偷换概念
C 说研究发现“预测顾客偏好的方法”，盗用了原文 consumers don't have clear
preferences里的 preferences，但原文说的是“消费者没有明确偏好”是促买的条件之一，绝
非“能预测偏好”，属偷换概念。
借用原文：consumers don't have clear preferences

questions.stem: What do many Americans think of volunteering?

options.label: A
options.text: Stressful.

options.label: B
options.text: Burdensome.

options.label: C
options.text: Worthwhile.

options.label: D
options.text: Energy-boosting.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （态度观点题） Worthwhile.
【定位】According to one survey, only 26% of Americans volunteered, despite reports that many
Americans view volunteering as worthwhile.
据一项调查，只有 26% 的美国人做过志愿服务，尽管有报道称许多美国人认为志愿服务是
值得做的。
【信号】题干同词 many Americans 在 despite 让步从句里现身。答案句里 many Americans
view volunteering as worthwhile 与题干 many Americans 完全对上，且 despite（尽
管）这个让步信号后面跟的正是‘大家的看法’，听到 despite + many Americans 就该锁定
这句。
【替换】view volunteering as worthwhile ↔ Worthwhile.
原句形容词被直接抽出做选项
【排除】A) 未提及
很多人想当然觉得志愿‘让人有压力’，但录音对态度只给了 worthwhile 一个正面评价，从
没说 stressful，属于用常识代替文本的硬伤。
B) 与原文相反
录音明确是 worthwhile（值得、正面），Burdensome（负担重的）是负面，方向相反；
预读时已把它和 worthwhile 分到对立两组，听出正面语气即可排除。
D) 答非所问
录音后文确实讲志愿能 boost happiness、提升健康，本项把这些好处浓缩成‘提神’来诱
选，但题干问的是 many Americans think of it 的评价，答案句只给了 worthwhile，本项
答非所问。
借用原文：boost happiness

questions.stem: How could companies ensure both employees and employers benefit from volunteering?

options.label: A
options.text: By linking it with employees' salary.

options.label: B
options.text: By taking it as the New Year resolution.

options.label: C
options.text: By improving work schedules.

options.label: D
options.text: By making it part of the job.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） By making it part of the job.
【定位】Most people cite time and conflicting work schedules as major barriers, but employees and
employers would actually benefit if companies made employee volunteering part of the job.
大多数人把时间和工作排期冲突列为主要障碍，但如果公司把员工志愿服务变成工作的一部
分，员工和雇主其实都会受益。
【信号】转折 but 之后才是真正答案，且 benefit 与题干呼应。but employees and employers
would actually benefit if companies made employee volunteering part of the job
里，转折词 but 后面才是作者的真意，且 benefit、employees and employers 与题干
both…benefit 直接对上，听到 but 紧跟 benefit 就锁定这句。
【替换】made employee volunteering part of the job ↔ By making it part of the job.
过去式陈述改写成 By doing，it 指代志愿
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 By linking it with employees' salary. 借 employees 这个录音高频词显得耳熟，但录
音从未说把志愿与‘薪水’挂钩，salary 是凭常识脑补的合理做法。
借用原文：employees and employers would actually benefit
B) 原词陷阱
录音确有 company volunteer programs could be the perfect 2025 resolution，本项
By taking it as the New Year resolution. 抠走 resolution 一词，但那只是把项目比作‘新
年愿望’的修辞，不是‘如何让双方受益’的办法，答非所问。
借用原文：company volunteer programs could be the perfect 2025 resolution
C) 原词陷阱
录音 Most people cite time and conflicting work schedules as major barriers 把 work
schedules 说成‘障碍’，本项 By improving work schedules. 把它翻成‘改善作息’当对策，
正是 but 转折前的干扰内容，与录音给的真正办法不符。
借用原文：conflicting work schedules as major barriers

questions.stem: What did 75% of employees say about volunteering in a survey?

options.label: A
options.text: It was very important to their well-being.

options.label: B
options.text: It had taken little of their spare time.

options.label: C
options.text: It was an outlet for their personal fulfillment.

options.label: D
options.text: It helped improve their working environment.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） It was very important to their well-being.
【定位】In one survey, 89% of employees perceived companies that sponsored volunteer activities
as creating a better working environment, and 75% said volunteering was critical to their
well-being.
在一项调查中，89% 的员工认为赞助志愿活动的公司营造了更好的工作环境，75% 的员工
则表示志愿服务对他们的幸福感至关重要。
【信号】数字 75% 直接领出答案，须与相邻 89% 切开。录音连说两个数字，75% said
volunteering was critical to their well-being 才是题干要的 75%；听到 75% said 就锁定
它后半句，切勿被前面 89% 那句串台。
【替换】critical to their well-being ↔ It was very important to their well-being.
critical 同义替换为 very important
【排除】B) 未提及
本项 It had taken little of their spare time. 说志愿‘几乎没占业余时间’，录音 75% 的人说
的是它‘至关重要’，方向不符；录音只在前文把 time 说成‘障碍’，从没说它‘占用很少’。
C) 张冠李戴
录音确有 the workplace becomes an outlet for personal fulfillment，本项 It was an
outlet for their personal fulfillment. 几乎照搬这句，但那是作者自己的论述，不是 75%
员工‘在调查中说’的内容，张冠李戴。
借用原文：the workplace becomes an outlet for personal fulfillment
D) 张冠李戴
It helped improve their working environment. 取自 89% of employees perceived
companies…as creating a better working environment，是相邻的 89% 那句的内容；
题干问 75%，本项把另一个数字的说法搬过来，是典型数字串台。
借用原文：89% of employees perceived companies that sponsored volunteer activities as creating
a better working environment

questions.stem: What do we learn about the UK's retail sector food waste?

options.label: A
options.text: It amounts to 2,000 tons daily.

options.label: B
options.text: It mostly comes from supermarkets.

options.label: C
options.text: It is estimated at 11% of the UK's total food supply.

options.label: D
options.text: It has a lot to do with independent luxury food suppliers.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） It mostly comes from supermarkets.
【定位】The vast majority of the UK's 200,000 tonnes of retail sector's annual food waste comes
from supermarkets.
英国零售业每年 20 万吨的食物浪费，绝大部分来自超市。
【信号】首句正面定性 the vast majority。这是段落开篇的总起句，用 The vast majority（绝大部
分）直接给 "来源" 下定性结论——细节题的答案常落在这种正面交代主体的句子上，而不
是后面的补充。
【替换】The vast majority of the UK's 200,000 tonnes of retail sector's annual food waste comes from
supermarkets
↔ It mostly comes from supermarkets.
the vast majority = mostly
【排除】A) 未提及
录音只说全年总量是 200,000 tonnes（20 万吨/年），选项 It amounts to 2,000 tons
daily. 把数字改成 "2,000 吨/天"，数额和 "每日" 的口径都是录音没说的，属于拿一个貌似
听过的数字来骗。
借用原文：200,000 tonnes
C) 原词陷阱
录音说的是 It's estimated at less than one per cent of the UK's food waste total
——"不到 1%，且是占食物浪费总量"。选项 It is estimated at 11% of the UK's total
food supply. 盗用了 "estimated" 这个原词，却把 "less than one per cent" 改成
"11%"、把 "food waste total" 改成 "food supply"，数字与口径全反了。
借用原文：It's estimated at less than one per cent of the UK's food waste total
D) 张冠李戴
录音说浪费主要来自超市，只是 it's a problem that impacts independent luxury food
suppliers too——高端供应商只是 "也受影响" 的次要对象。选项 It has a lot to do with
independent luxury food suppliers. 盗用 "independent luxury food suppliers" 这串原
词，把次要对象说成主因，张冠李戴。
借用原文：it's a problem that impacts independent luxury food suppliers too

questions.stem: What does Sophie André's business do in London?

options.label: A
options.text: It rents bicycles to deliver food.

options.label: B
options.text: It sells sought-after coffee beans.

options.label: C
options.text: It delivers luxury hand-made food.

options.label: D
options.text: It recycles waste food from the city.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） It delivers luxury hand-made food.
【定位】In 2016 she moved to London and began by setting up a business delivering luxury hand-
made food across the city.
2016 年她搬到伦敦，先创办了一家在全城配送高端手工食品的公司。
【信号】creating/setting up 引出业务定义。began by setting up a business delivering luxury
hand-made food 用 "setting up a business doing…" 的句式直接给这家公司的主营下定
义——这种 "创办一家做……的公司" 句就是业务题的答案句。
【替换】setting up a business delivering luxury hand-made food across the city ↔
It delivers luxury hand-made food.
几近原词的定性概括
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
录音里 "自行车" 出现在 I started delivering products by bicycle——自行车只是配送 "工
具"。选项 It rents bicycles to deliver food. 盗用 "bicycle" 原词，却把 "用自行车送货" 偷
换成 "出租自行车"，业务定位完全错了。
借用原文：I started delivering products by bicycle
B) 原词陷阱
"coffee beans" 出现在第一段 sought-after coffee beans gets thrown away，说的是 "被
浪费的高端食材举例"，根本不是这家公司在卖的东西。选项 It sells sought-after coffee
beans. 盗用这串原词，安到公司业务上，答非所问。
借用原文：sought-after coffee beans gets thrown away every day
D) 与原文相反
录音明确说这家公司 the idea is not simply to redistribute waste food, but to provide
a high-quality product——明确否定了 "只是重新分配废弃食物"。选项 It recycles waste
food from the city. 盗用 "waste" 原词，恰好把录音否定掉的那层意思当成业务，与原文相
反。
借用原文：the idea is not simply to redistribute waste food, but to provide a high-quality product

questions.stem: In what way does Sophie André's business differ from many food waste projects?

options.label: A
options.text: It pays special attention to the size and shape of its products.

options.label: B
options.text: It tries to escape the constraints of the current food system.

options.label: C
options.text: It cooperates closely with local producers.

options.label: D
options.text: It aims to provide high-quality products.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） It aims to provide high-quality products.
【定位】Unlike many food waste projects that have sprung up in recent years, the idea is not simply to
redistribute waste food, but to provide a high-quality product.
与近年涌现的许多食物浪费项目不同，这个想法不只是重新分配废弃食物，而是提供高品质
产品。
【信号】Unlike + not…but 双重对比。这句同时挂着两个信号：开头 Unlike many food waste
projects 是明示对比，中间 not simply…but… 把真正不同之处推到 but 之后——答案句就
是这种 "对比词 + 转折落点" 叠加的句子。
【替换】to provide a high-quality product ↔ It aims to provide high-quality products.
but 后落点的同义保留
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
"size or shape" 出现在 a small part of the production is sometimes wasted due to
problems with size or shape——是在解释 "为何会有剩余"，不是公司的产品特点。选项
It pays special attention to the size and shape of its products. 盗用这两个词，编出 "特
别关注尺寸形状" 这个录音没说的差异。
借用原文：wasted due to problems with size or shape
B) 过度推断
录音只说它 "不只是再分配废弃食物，而是提供高品质产品"，并没说它要 "摆脱现有食物体
系的束缚"。选项 It tries to escape the constraints of the current food system. 把朴素
的 "提供高品质" 拔高成宏大的体制叙事，是录音支撑不了的引申。
C) 原词陷阱
录音只说她 Talking with local producers I learned that…——只是 "和本地生产者交谈"
从而得知信息，并未说 "紧密合作"。选项 It cooperates closely with local producers. 盗
用 "local producers" 原词，把 "交谈" 夸大成 "closely cooperate"，且这也不是题问的差
异点。
借用原文：Talking with local producers I learned that…

questions.stem: Why will suppliers always have a certain amount of surplus?

options.label: A
options.text: To ensure a regular supply.

options.label: B
options.text: To maintain a unique menu.

options.label: C
options.text: To make up for the waste products.

options.label: D
options.text: To meet customers' urgent demand.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） To ensure a regular supply.
【定位】Perhaps unlike other waste food, the supply is regular. Suppliers will always have a certain
amount of surplus. So the menus remain regular too.
也许与其他剩余食物不同，这里的供应是稳定的。供应商总会有一定量的剩余。所以菜单也
保持稳定。
【信号】the supply is regular 的因果链。这题的因果不在 "surplus" 那句本身，而在它前面的 the
supply is regular——正因要保证 "稳定供应"，所以供应商总会留出一定剩余；"surplus"
那句与 "so the menus remain regular" 共同把 "regular（稳定）" 这条逻辑钉死。
【替换】the supply is regular ↔ To ensure a regular supply.
regular supply 几乎原词对应
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
录音说的是 So the menus remain regular too——菜单 "保持稳定（regular）"。选项 To
maintain a unique menu. 盗用 "menu" 原词，却把 "regular（稳定）" 偷换成 "unique
（独特）"，把听过的词配上录音没说的形容词。
借用原文：So the menus remain regular too
C) 原词陷阱
"waste products" 出现在 Elysia uses waste products to create…meals——是说公司 "用
剩余食材做餐"，并非 "供应商留剩余是为弥补废弃"。选项 To make up for the waste
products. 盗用 "waste products" 这个主题原词，编出一个录音没有的因果，答非所问。
借用原文：Elysia uses waste products to create "simple, natural, straightforward" meals and snacks
D) 未提及
录音通篇没说 "满足顾客的紧急需求"，只讲了供应稳定、菜单稳定。选项 To meet
customers' urgent demand. 里的 "urgent demand" 是录音完全没出现的内容，属凭空捏
造。

questions.stem: How did Tariq make corn taste better?

options.label: A
options.text: By slapping some butter on it.

options.label: B
options.text: By enhancing its nourishment.

options.label: C
options.text: By growing it in South Dakota.

options.label: D
options.text: By cooking it in vegetable oil.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） By slapping some butter on it.
【定位】Everything changed for 7-year-old Tariq when he slapped some butter on an ear of corn. He
knew it tasted good, but butter made it better.
对 7 岁的塔里克来说，当他往一根玉米上抹了点黄油时，一切都变了。他本就知道玉米好
吃，但黄油让它更好吃了。
【信号】but 后点出"黄油让它更好吃"。答案句的信号是转折词 but：but butter made it better 直
接把 butter 和 made it better 挂钩，正好回答"怎么让玉米更好吃"，转折之后的这半句才
是落点。
【替换】he slapped some butter on an ear of corn ↔ By slapping some butter on it.
an ear of corn 被代词 it 概括
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
录音第2段确实提到玉米能 provides nourishment across the globe，B 项 By enhancing
its nourishment. 盗用了 nourishment 这个原词，但那是讲玉米向全球提供营养，跟"塔里
克怎么让玉米更好吃"无关，听到 nourishment 就选就中陷阱。
借用原文：The corn provides nourishment across the globe.
C) 原词陷阱
C 项 By growing it in South Dakota. 盗用了录音里的 South Dakota 这个高频地名，
South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America 说的是它是产玉米大州，
与"让玉米更好吃"是两码事，属听到地名就想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：South Dakota is one of the top corn producers in America.
D) 未提及
D 项 By cooking it in vegetable oil. 听起来也是个合理做法，且和正确项 A 的"加黄油"形
成对立诱惑，但录音从头到尾只提了抹黄油，没说用植物油烹饪，属凭常识硬造、原文未提
及。

questions.stem: Why were Tariq and his family invited to South Dakota?

options.label: A
options.text: To introduce their corn to tourists.

options.label: B
options.text: To attend an honorary ceremony.

options.label: C
options.text: To share experience with other corn growers.

options.label: D
options.text: To exhibit their corn at the state's Corn Palace.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （目的题） To attend an honorary ceremony.
【定位】Tariq and his family were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony at the
state's Corn Palace.
塔里克和他的家人受邀前往南达科他，去参加该州玉米宫举行的荣誉典礼。
【信号】invited to… to attend… 把人和目的连起来。答案信号是 invited 后接的目的不定式：
were invited to South Dakota to attend the honorary ceremony，to attend 直接说明
受邀目的就是参加荣誉典礼，这句一字对上题干所问。
【替换】to attend the honorary ceremony ↔ To attend an honorary ceremony.
the→an，去掉地点状语，核心动作不变
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
录音确实提到官方想突出 tourism and agriculture，A 项 To introduce their corn to
tourists. 盗用了 tourism 引申出的 tourists，但那是官方的产业意图，不是塔里克一家"被
邀请"的目的，二者主体不同，听到游客相关词就选会被带偏。
借用原文：Officials wanted to highlight South Dakota's two largest industries: tourism
and agriculture.
C) 未提及
C 项 To share experience with other corn growers. 借 corn 这个全篇高频词造出"和其他
玉米种植者交流经验"的合理场景，但录音通篇没说塔里克要去交流经验，属凭话题臆造、
未提及。
D) 原词陷阱
D 项 To exhibit their corn at the state's Corn Palace. 盗用了答案句里真实出现的地名 at
the state's Corn Palace，极具迷惑性；但录音说的是去玉米宫"参加典礼"，不是去那里"展
出他们的玉米"，偷换了在玉米宫做的事，听到 Corn Palace 就选会中招。
借用原文：to attend the honorary ceremony at the state's Corn Palace
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Two arrests were announced Thursday. The arrests were in connection with a string of mail thefts
from U.S. Postal Service's collection boxes in Marion County and for the possession of a stolen postal
key, according to the Department of Justice.
周四宣布了两起逮捕行动。据司法部称,这些逮捕与Marion County美国邮政管理局收集箱的一系列邮件
盗窃案以及持有被盗邮政钥匙有关。
2 Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman, both 23, were arrested after evidence gathered in an investigation
showed the pair stole mail on multiple occasions using a postal key, according to a news release.
据新闻稿称,23岁的Jordan Jax和Tarod Goodman在调查中收集的证据显示两人多次使用邮政钥匙盗窃邮
件后被逮捕。
3 Jax and Goodman stole mail for around four months. Investigators reviewed videos of the collection
boxes; the video showed the two men loading the stolen mail into Jax's vehicle. Investigators were also
able to recover the key that was used to open the collection boxes.
Jax和Goodman盗窃邮件约四个月。调查人员查看了收集箱的监控视频;视频显示两名男子将被盗邮件装
入Jax的车辆。调查人员还找回了用于打开收集箱的钥匙。
4 Jax and Goodman each face up to five years in federal prison in the mail thefts and up to ten years
for possession of the postal key.
Jax和Goodman各自面临邮件盗窃罪最高五年联邦监禁,以及持有邮政钥匙罪最高十年监禁。

questions.stem: What did Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman do according to a news release?

options.label: A
options.text: Stole mail several times.

options.label: B
options.text: Forged postal keys illegally.

options.label: C
options.text: Attacked postmen on multiple occasions.

options.label: D
options.text: Broke a number of postal collection boxes.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Stole mail several times.
【定位】Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman, both 23, were arrested after evidence gathered in an
investigation showed the pair stole mail on multiple occasions using a postal key, according
to a news release.
据一份新闻稿，乔丹·贾克斯和塔罗德·古德曼，两人均为 23 岁，在一项调查所收集的证据显
示二人多次盗窃邮件、并使用了一把邮政钥匙后，被逮捕。
【信号】题干来源词回扣定位。题干里的 according to a news release 与录音 according to a
news release 逐字对应，这处来源短语就是定位信号：它出现的那一句正是承载答案的句
子，紧接的 stole mail on multiple occasions 即两人所做之事。
【替换】stole mail on multiple occasions ↔ Stole mail several times.
多次的同义改写
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
录音说两人 using a postal key，是使用一把邮政钥匙作案，并非 Forged postal keys
illegally. 所说的非法伪造钥匙；选项盗用了 postal key 这一原词，却把使用偷换成伪造，
答非所问。
借用原文：using a postal key
C) 张冠李戴
录音里的 on multiple occasions 修饰的是盗窃邮件，Attacked postmen on multiple
occasions. 却把这个多次短语套到攻击邮递员上；录音通篇没有任何袭击邮差的内容，属盗
用频次短语的张冠李戴。
借用原文：stole mail on multiple occasions
D) 原词陷阱
录音多处提到 collection boxes，如 collection boxes，但说的是两人用钥匙打开邮筒取
信，从无砸坏之意；Broke a number of postal collection boxes. 盗用 collection boxes
原词，硬加上 Broke 这一录音没有的动作。
借用原文：collection boxes

questions.stem: What do Jordan Jax and Tarod Goodman face?

options.label: A
options.text: A sentence for life.

options.label: B
options.text: Loss of all their possessions.

options.label: C
options.text: Twenty-three years' hard labor.

options.label: D
options.text: Up to fifteen years in prison.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Up to fifteen years in prison.
【定位】Jax and Goodman each face up to five years in federal prison in the mail thefts and up to ten
years for possession of the postal key.
贾克斯和古德曼二人因盗窃邮件各面临最高五年的联邦监禁，并因持有邮政钥匙各面临最高
十年监禁。
【信号】题干动词 face 原句重现。题干的 face 在录音 each face up to five years 里原样念出，这
处动词回扣即定位信号；该句把两项刑期 up to five years 与 up to ten years 一并给出，
正是答案所在。
【替换】up to five years in federal prison ↔ Up to fifteen years in prison.
两项刑期相加得十五年
up to ten years for possession of the postal key ↔ Up to fifteen years in prison.
另一项刑期并入总数
【排除】A) 未提及
录音只说面临有期的 five years 与 ten years，从未提无期；A sentence for life. 是夸大到
终身监禁的后果，录音并无对应内容。
B) 未提及
录音谈的全是坐牢的年限，未提任何财产损失；Loss of all their possessions. 所说丧失全
部财产在录音里毫无依据。
C) 原词陷阱
录音里的 23 出自两人年龄 both 23，并非刑期；Twenty-three years' hard labor. 盗用 23
这个数字，硬安成二十三年苦役，且 hard labor 录音也从未提及，把年龄数偷换成刑期。
借用原文：both 23

questions.stem: Why has the clothing industry come under attack?

options.label: A
options.text: It escapes regulation and misleads consumers.

options.label: B
options.text: It ignores economically feasible recycling options.

options.label: C
options.text: It creates waste and severely impacts the environment.

options.label: D
options.text: It produces clothes affordable only to a tiny minority.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） It creates waste and severely impacts the environment.
【定位】Recently, the clothing industry has come under attack for creating a waste problem with
serious environmental consequences.
最近，服装业因制造废物问题、带来严重环境后果而受到抨击。
【信号】题干原词 come under attack 复现处。录音中 has come under attack for 与题干 come
under attack 几乎一字不差，听到这个短语就锁定这句；紧跟 for 后面的内容正是被抨击的
原因，即答案所在。
【替换】creating a waste problem ↔ It creates waste
动名词转一般现在时
serious environmental consequences ↔ severely impacts the environment
名词短语改写成动词短语
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 说 misleads consumers（误导消费者），其中 consumers 是录音后文反复出现的原
词，听到就想选；但录音说行业被抨击的原因是制造废物、害环境，从没说它误导消费者，
A 借原词制造错觉。
借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers
B) 偷换概念
B 说 ignores economically feasible recycling options（忽视经济可行的回收方案），其
中 recycling、economically feasible 直接来自录音 environmentally and economically
feasible recycling options；但录音说的是这类回收方案本就缺失（in the absence of），
不是行业故意忽视，B 把客观缺失偷换成主观无视。
借用原文：In the absence of environmentally and economically feasible recycling options
D) 与原文相反
D 说 produces clothes affordable only to a tiny minority（生产只有极少数人买得起的
衣服），clothes、produces 是录音原词，但录音明说快时尚是 low-quality clothes
produced in high volumes（低质、量产），价格便宜、人人能买，与 D 说的只有极少数
人买得起恰好相反，录音也没提价格门槛。
借用原文：low-quality clothes produced in high volumes

questions.stem: Why did the researchers put forth such policies as production tax?

options.label: A
options.text: To cut consumers' expenses in buying quality clothes.

options.label: B
options.text: To enable the whole fast-fashion industry to be sustainable.

options.label: C
options.text: To incentivize manufacturers to be more consumer-friendly.

options.label: D
options.text: To urge manufacturers and consumers to reduce waste.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （目的题） To urge manufacturers and consumers to reduce waste.
【定位】The researchers put forth policy contributions, ranging from sustainable disposal of leftover
stock to production tax to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more
waste conscious.
研究者提出了一系列政策建议，从对剩余库存的可持续处理到征收生产税，目的是激励生产
商和消费者都更有减废意识。
【信号】目的状语 to incentivize。录音里 to incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to
be more waste conscious 是 production tax 后面的目的状语，to incentivize 就是表目
的的信号，它后面的内容正是这些政策要达成的目标。
【替换】incentivize both manufacturers and consumers ↔ urge manufacturers and consumers
同义动词替换
to be more waste conscious ↔ to reduce waste
概括式改写
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 说 cut consumers' expenses in buying quality clothes（替消费者省下买好衣服的
钱），consumers 是录音原词，但录音讲政策目的是减废，从没说为消费者省钱，A 把减
废目的偷换成省钱目的。
借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers
B) 过度推断
B 说 To enable the whole fast-fashion industry to be sustainable（让整个快时尚业可
持续），sustainable 是录音开头出现的原词，但生产税这类政策的直接目的录音说得很具
体——是激励双方减废，而非让整个行业可持续，B 把目的范围夸大了。
借用原文：Can fast-fashion be sustainable?
C) 偷换概念
C 说 incentivize manufacturers to be more consumer-friendly（激励生产商更体贴消费
者），incentivize、manufacturers 是录音原词，但录音说的是激励双方更有减废意识，不
是让生产商对消费者更友好，C 把减废目的偷换成讨好消费者。
借用原文：incentivize both manufacturers and consumers to be more waste conscious

questions.stem: What should be done first to eliminate the harm caused by the clothing industry?

options.label: A
options.text: Recognizing the impact on consumers.

options.label: B
options.text: Identifying the source of the problem.

options.label: C
options.text: Abandoning the current business model.

options.label: D
options.text: Establishing powerful regulatory bodies.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Identifying the source of the problem.
【定位】In order to devise effective policies to curb the environmental impact of the clothing industry,
it is important to identify the source of the problem in the supply chain.
为了制定有效政策来遏制服装业对环境的影响，关键是先找出供应链中问题的根源。
【信号】强调句 it is important to。录音 it is important to identify the source of the problem
用 it is important to 强调首要之事，这就是表先后、表首要的信号词；它后面的动作
identify the source 即题目问的第一步。
【替换】identify the source of the problem ↔ Identifying the source of the problem
动词原形转动名词，近乎原句
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 说 Recognizing the impact on consumers，其中 recognize、impact 来自录音
recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion，听到就想选；但录音把这一步放
在找出根源之后，而且说的是认识环境影响、不是对消费者的影响，既不是第一步、对象也
被改了。
借用原文：recognize the environmental impact of fast-fashion
C) 过度推断
C 说 Abandoning the current business model（放弃现有商业模式），business model
取自录音 create new business models，但录音说的是创造新商业模式，从没说要放弃现
有模式，C 把创造夸张成放弃。
借用原文：create new business models to manage waste
D) 原词陷阱
D 说 Establishing powerful regulatory bodies（建立强有力的监管机构），regulatory
bodies 出现在录音 Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies 中，但录音只是
提到监管机构是参与方之一，从没说要先建立强有力的监管机构，D 是凭原词编出来的。
借用原文：Manufacturers, consumers, and regulatory bodies can then take an informed approach

questions.stem: Why is the woman complaining?

options.label: A
options.text: The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable.

options.label: B
options.text: She cannot avoid rush-hour traffic.

options.label: C
options.text: The local government is inefficient.

options.label: D
options.text: The city is too big to move around easily.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable.
【定位】Rush hour in this city is killing me.
这座城市的高峰期真要把我折腾死了。
【信号】她开口的第一句直接吐槽。男方问"你怎么这么烦/出什么事了"之后，女方应答的第一句
Rush hour in this city is killing me. 就是直接吐槽，is killing me 这种强烈情绪用语正是
抱怨的落点信号——被问者的第一反应往往就是答案句。
【替换】Rush hour in this city is killing me. ↔ The city's rush-hour traffic is intolerable.
is killing me 改写成 intolerable
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
B 盗用了录音里反复出现的 Rush hour 来勾人，但她抱怨的是高峰期"让人受不了"，从没
说"她躲不开高峰"。She cannot avoid rush-hour traffic. 是凭空加上的内容，属听到原词
就想选的陷阱。
借用原文：Rush hour is terrible
C) 原词陷阱
录音后面女方确实提到 the local government could help improve things，C 盗用"政
府"这个原词，却编成"政府效率低"。她说的是"政府本可以帮忙改善"，并没说政府无能，C
答非所问。
借用原文：the local government could help improve things
D) 原词陷阱
男方说过 a city this big，D 盗用"城市大"这个原词，编成"城市太大不好出行"。但那是男
方的话，且女方抱怨的对象是高峰期本身，不是城市大小，D 既张冠李戴又答非所问。
借用原文：a city this big

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest doing?

options.label: A
options.text: Upgrading subway carriages.

options.label: B
options.text: Increasing the number of bus routes.

options.label: C
options.text: Air conditioning the city's subway.

options.label: D
options.text: Learning from other big cities.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Air conditioning the city's subway.
【定位】Well, for example, the subway system could have air conditioning. I know many cities in the
world have air conditioning in their subway, so why can't we?
比如说，地铁系统可以装空调嘛。我知道世界上很多城市的地铁都有空调，咱们为什么不能
有呢？
【信号】建议信号 could 与 why can't we。the subway system could have air conditioning 里
的 could（可以…）就是建议信号，紧接着 why can't we（咱为什么不能）用反问加重了这
条提议——could + 反问，正是"我建议这么做"的落点。
【替换】the subway system could have air conditioning ↔ Air conditioning the city's subway.
句子改写成动名词短语
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 盗用录音里的 subway carriages（地铁车厢）来勾人。"车厢"确实念到了，但女方的建
议是"装空调"，不是"升级车厢"。况且后面 The trains here are too old 是男方说的，不是
女方的建议，A 答非所问。
借用原文：strangers packed close together in the subway carriages
B) 未提及
增开公交线路这件事女方从没提过。录音只在男方那段提到 Bus No. 36，与"增加线路"无
关，B 属凭空捏造的措施。
D) 原词陷阱
D 盗用了 many cities in the world 里的"别的城市"来勾人，但女方提"很多城市有空调"是
为论证"应给地铁装空调"，并非建议"向别的大城市学习"。D 把具体建议偷换成空泛口号，
答非所问。
借用原文：I know many cities in the world have air conditioning in their subway

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?

options.label: A
options.text: He suffers from rush-hour crowding too.

options.label: B
options.text: He is fortunate to live very near to work.

options.label: C
options.text: He takes a half-hour bus ride to work.

options.label: D
options.text: He is going to move closer to his office.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） He takes a half-hour bus ride to work.
【定位】Yeah, it's more convenient. Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office. It's a 30-
minute ride and I don't have to make any changes.
对，公交更方便。36 路车从我家直达办公室，车程 30 分钟，中途不用换乘。
【信号】男方自述上班方式 + 数字 30-minute。Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the
office 是男方在讲自己怎么上班，紧跟的 It's a 30-minute ride 给出具体时长——"自述 +
数字"是细节题最硬的落点信号，听到数字就要立刻记下。
【替换】It's a 30-minute ride ↔ He takes a half-hour bus ride to work.
30-minute 换说成 half-hour
Bus No. 36 goes straight from my house to the office ↔ bus ride to work
坐公交去办公室=坐公交上班
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
A 盗用录音里 rush-hour crowds 这个"高峰拥挤"原词来勾人，但受高峰挤之苦的是女方
（坐地铁），男方说自己坐公交、还自称 fortunate。把女方的处境安到男方身上，是张冠
李戴。
借用原文：the rush-hour crowds with strangers packed close together
B) 原词陷阱
B 盗用男方说的 I'm fortunate（我算幸运）来勾人。他幸运是因为"坐公交方便、不用挤地
铁"，而不是"住得离公司很近"——通勤还要 30 分钟，谈不上很近。B 把"幸运的原因"偷换
了。
借用原文：I guess I'm fortunate I take the bus instead
D) 张冠李戴
D 盗用了 move closer to the office 这个原词，但说"也许我该搬得离公司近点"的是女
方，不是男方。把女方的打算记到男方头上，张冠李戴。
借用原文：Maybe I should move closer to the office

questions.stem: What does the woman ask the man to do at the end of the conversation?

options.label: A
options.text: Recommend to her a good house near his office.

options.label: B
options.text: Send her his housing agent's telephone number.

options.label: C
options.text: Tell her exactly what kind of property to look for.

options.label: D
options.text: Make sure the agent finds something good for her.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Send her his housing agent's telephone number.
【定位】Hmm, could you send me his number, please?
嗯，你能把他的电话号码发给我吗？
【信号】请求句 could you…please。could you send me his number, please? 用 could you…
please 提出请求，正是"请对方做某事"的标准信号，且出现在对话末尾，与题干"at the
end"对得上——这就是答案句。
【替换】could you send me his number, please? ↔ Send her his housing agent's telephone number.
his number 补全为中介的电话号码
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 盗用了对话里 move closer to the office、flat 这一带"房子"话题来勾人，但她请的是"发
中介电话"，不是"请他直接推荐一套好房子"。把"给电话"偷换成"荐房"，答非所问。
借用原文：I found the flat I'm living in now through him
C) 张冠李戴
C 盗用了男方那句 tell him exactly what you are looking for，但那是男方让"她去告诉中
介"要什么，不是她请男方做的事，也不是"由男方告诉她该找什么样的房"。既张冠李戴又把
方向弄反。
借用原文：Just tell him exactly what you are looking for
D) 原词陷阱
D 盗用男方那句 he will find something good 来勾人，但那是男方对中介能办好的预期，
不是女方请男方"确保中介给她找到好的"。把一句预期偷换成她的请求，答非所问。
借用原文：I'm sure he will find something good

questions.stem: What does the man say about Johnny?

options.label: A
options.text: He was remembered for the scar on his cheek.

options.label: B
options.text: He received a heart operation a few days ago.

options.label: C
options.text: He used to wear a sad face in school.

options.label: D
options.text: He had some plastic surgery done.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） He had some plastic surgery done.
【定位】He had some plastic surgery done.
他做了整形手术。
【信号】对方一开口的核心信息。男生在被问『他还好吗』之后，第一句给出的实质消息就是 He
had some plastic surgery done.，这是整段对话的引子和核心事件，承载本题答案。
【替换】He had some plastic surgery done. ↔ He had some plastic surgery done.
几乎原句照搬
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 He was remembered for the scar on his cheek. 借了录音里真出现过的 scar 和
cheek（女生说 I always remember him having that on his cheek），但那是女生说『记
得他脸上有疤』，并非男生关于 Johnny 所说的核心事件；题问 the man 说了什么，答非
所问。
借用原文：I always remember him having that on his cheek
B) 偷换概念
选项 He received a heart operation a few days ago. 蹭了录音里的 operation 一词（He
had an operation done on it, plastic surgery），却擅自改成 heart operation（心脏手
术）；录音说的是脸上的整形手术，不是心脏，属偷换。
借用原文：He had an operation done on it, plastic surgery
C) 未提及
选项 He used to wear a sad face in school. 里的 sad face（哭丧脸）录音根本没说，只
是借了 school 一词（女生提到 I've known him since primary school）凑出来的；属无
中生有。
借用原文：I've known him since primary school

questions.stem: What does the woman find puzzling?

options.label: A
options.text: The man's deep sympathy for Johnny.

options.label: B
options.text: The man's use of the expression 'fixed'.

options.label: C
options.text: The man's covering up of what happened.

options.label: D
options.text: The man's good memory of his childhood.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） The man's use of the expression 'fixed'.
【定位】Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar.
修好？你什么意思？疤是没法『修好』的。
【信号】对某个用词的反问。女生紧接男生说的 he had it fixed，立刻反问 Fixed? What do you
mean? You can't fix a scar.——她重复并质疑了 fixed 这个词，反问语气正是『困惑』的
信号，答案句就在此。
【替换】Fixed? What do you mean? You can't fix a scar. ↔ The man's use of the expression 'fixed'.
把疑问句概括为『对用词不解』
【排除】A) 未提及
选项 The man's deep sympathy for Johnny. 说男生对 Johnny 深表同情，录音里男生从
头到尾没有表达同情，更不是女生困惑的点；属未提及。
C) 原词陷阱
选项 The man's covering up of what happened. 蹭了录音里 in order to cover it and
make it less noticeable 的 cover，但原文 cover 是『遮盖那道疤』，选项偷换成『掩盖发
生的事（隐瞒）』，且女生并不为此困惑。
借用原文：in order to cover it and make it less noticeable
D) 张冠李戴
选项 The man's good memory of his childhood. 里『好记性』其实是女生自己说的（I
always remember him having that on his cheek），却被安到 the man 头上，且与『困
惑』无关；属张冠李戴。
借用原文：I always remember him having that on his cheek

questions.stem: What did the man think of Johnny's scar?

options.label: A
options.text: It gave him a noticeable smartness.

options.label: B
options.text: It made him appear even more manly.

options.label: C
options.text: It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness.

options.label: D
options.text: It seemed to make up for his physical defects.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （态度观点题） It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness.
【定位】In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave him a certain uniqueness.
其实我觉得那道疤还添了几分个性……好像让他有种独特感。
【信号】I thought 引出的主观评价。男生用 In fact, I thought it added character… like it gave
him a certain uniqueness，I thought 直接亮出他对疤的看法，且 In fact 加重了肯定语
气，是承载态度的答案句。
【替换】it gave him a certain uniqueness ↔ It seemed to give him a certain uniqueness.
近乎同句，只换了语气词
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 It gave him a noticeable smartness. 蹭了录音里多次出现的 noticeable（make it
less noticeable），但 smartness（精明/帅气）男生从没说过；属用熟词拼凑的原词陷
阱。
借用原文：make it less noticeable
B) 未提及
选项 It made him appear even more manly. 说疤让他更有男子气概，录音里男生评价用
的是 character、uniqueness，从未说 manly；属未提及。
D) 与原文相反
选项 It seemed to make up for his physical defects. 蹭了录音 physical defects 一词，
但男生说的是『有些缺陷确实丑、可 Johnny 的疤不是』，并不认为疤在弥补缺陷；这是反
着用了原文，张冠李戴加曲解。
借用原文：I can understand some scars and physical defects can be ugly and distracting, but
not Johnny's

questions.stem: How could we describe the speakers' attitude towards Johnny's girlfriend?

options.label: A
options.text: Liberal.

options.label: B
options.text: Hostile.

options.label: C
options.text: Indifferent.

options.label: D
options.text: Critical.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （态度观点题） Critical.
【定位】What? That's so superficial and selfish of her. If Johnny's girlfriend doesn't like him for who
he is, then she does not deserve to be his girlfriend.
什么？她这么做也太肤浅、太自私了。如果 Johnny 的女友不能接受真实的他，那她就不配
做他女友。
【信号】连串贬义评价词。女生对女友连用 so superficial and selfish（肤浅、自私）和 does not
deserve（不配），都是强烈负面用词；加上男生附和 You are right，两人态度一致偏负
面，这几句是态度答案句。
【替换】That's so superficial and selfish of her ↔ Critical.
贬义评价归为『批评』
【排除】A) 与原文相反
选项 Liberal.（开明、宽容）方向与录音相反——两人对女友是 superficial and selfish 的
指责，毫无宽容之意；属与原文相反。
借用原文：That's so superficial and selfish of her
B) 过度推断
选项 Hostile.（充满敌意）程度太重，录音是批评女友的做法（肤浅、自私），并未到仇
视、敌对的地步；属程度过度推断。
C) 与原文相反
选项 Indifferent.（漠不关心）与录音情绪冲突——女生说到激动处骂女友、还评 What a
fool he is，明显在意、不是无所谓；属与原文相反。
借用原文：What a fool he is

questions.stem: How did language come into being according to researchers?

options.label: A
options.text: Through deliberation.

options.label: B
options.text: Through evolution.

options.label: C
options.text: Through invention.

options.label: D
options.text: Through collaboration.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Through evolution.
【定位】Researchers don't think language was invented; instead, they think it evolved.
研究者不认为语言是被发明出来的；相反，他们认为它是进化（演变）而来的。
【信号】否定+instead 的对比落点。这句靠 don't think 先否掉一个说法、再用 instead 引出真正
的答案——『否定 + instead/but』之后才是真意。前半 language was invented（被发
明）是要被排除的，后半 they think it evolved（进化而来）才是研究者的真实立场。
【替换】they think it evolved ↔ Through evolution.
动词 evolved 名词化为 evolution
【排除】C) 原词陷阱
Through invention. 直接套用了录音里的 invented 一词，听到 invent 就想选正中陷阱
——但原文是 don't think language was invented，明确否定了『发明』这个说法，所以
它恰恰是错的。
借用原文：Researchers don't think language was invented
A) 未提及
Through deliberation.（通过深思熟虑/商议）在录音里根本没出现，研究者只在 invented
和 evolved 之间表态，从未说语言是『商量出来的』。
D) 未提及
Through collaboration.（通过协作）听上去合理，但录音只谈『进化还是发明』，从没说
语言是靠人们协作产生的，属于自己脑补、原文未给的内容。

questions.stem: How did language start according to the first theory?

options.label: A
options.text: With people imitating sounds around them.

options.label: B
options.text: With people interacting with animals close by.

options.label: C
options.text: With people showing each other things nearby.

options.label: D
options.text: With people trying to string sounds together.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） With people imitating sounds around them.
【定位】The first theory is that language started with people making different sounds, mostly imitating
the things around them, like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools.
第一个理论是：语言始于人们发出各种不同的声音，主要是模仿周围的事物，比如动物的叫
声、自然的声响和工具发出的声音。
【信号】started with 直接点出起点。这句用 language started with（语言始于……）这种明确的
『起点』标志词，正面回答题干问的『怎么开始』；其后的 imitating the things around
them（模仿周围事物）就是起步的具体动作。
【替换】making different sounds, mostly imitating the things around them ↔
With people imitating sounds around them.
imitating things around→imitating sounds around
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
With people interacting with animals close by. 抓住了录音里的 animal calls（动物叫
声）做诱饵，但原文说的是『模仿动物的叫声』，不是『和身边的动物互动』——听到
animal 就选就掉进陷阱，模仿声音 ≠ 与动物互动。
借用原文：like animal calls, nature sounds, and the sounds of tools
D) 答非所问
With people trying to string sounds together. 套用了原文 stringing the words
together，但那是录音明说『At some point』（在某个时间点）才出现的后期步骤，不是
『怎么开始』；它答的是后来的事，与题干问的『起点』错位。
借用原文：people started stringing the words together to form sentences
C) 张冠李戴
With people showing each other things nearby. 的『互相展示身边的东西』其实更接近
第三段第二个理论里的『比划、用手指东西』，而本题限定 the first theory，张冠李戴把
另一个理论的内容搬了过来。
借用原文：pointing at things with their hands and imitating actions using their bodies

questions.stem: Why did people switch from gesturing to making sounds according to the more recent theory?

options.label: A
options.text: Making sounds can free one's hands for doing other things.

options.label: B
options.text: Making sounds proves markedly easier than sign languages.

options.label: C
options.text: Making sounds enables one to express their ideas more explicitly.

options.label: D
options.text: Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see.
【定位】The reason they switched to making sounds, the theory goes, is that talking out loud lets you
communicate with someone even when you can't see them.
按这个理论的说法，人们之所以改用发声，原因是大声说话能让你即使在看不见对方的时候
也能与之交流。
【信号】The reason…is that 直给原因。这句以 The reason they switched to making sounds
开头、用 is that 直接引出理由，是最明确的因果信号；is that 后面的 even when you
can't see them 就是『为什么改成出声』的答案。
【替换】communicate with someone even when you can't see them ↔
Making sounds helps one communicate with people they can't see.
几乎逐词对应的同义改写
【排除】A) 过度推断
Making sounds can free one's hands for doing other things.『腾出双手做别的事』听
上去很合理，但录音从手语切到发声时只给了『看不见也能交流』这一个理由，从没提过
『腾出手』，这是凭常识自己补出来的，原文未给。
B) 原词陷阱
Making sounds proves markedly easier than sign languages. 借用了录音里的 sign
language，但原文只说手语后来发展出发声，从没比较『出声比手语更容易』，这个
easier 的比较是凭空加上去的。
借用原文：after developing sign languages, people eventually started making sounds
C) 未提及
Making sounds enables one to express their ideas more explicitly.『能更清楚地表达想
法』是个看似合理的好处，但录音给出的唯一理由是『看不见对方也能交流』，从没说出声
能表达得『更明确』，属于无中生有。

questions.stem: How would people describe someone who shows off their social status according to new research?

options.label: A
options.text: Well disciplined.

options.label: B
options.text: Quite confident.

options.label: C
options.text: Somewhat selfish.

options.label: D
options.text: Highly intelligent.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （态度观点题） Somewhat selfish.
【定位】But new research found that people believe someone who shows off their social status cares
more about benefiting themselves than helping others.
但新研究发现，人们认为炫耀自己社会地位的人更在意让自己得益，而非帮助他人。
【信号】转折 But + new research。答案句以 But new research found 起头，转折词 But 加上题
干点名的『new research』双重信号——前一句讲『显得有钱被认为更聪明自律』是铺
垫，But 之后才是新研究的真正结论，这正是答案落点。
【替换】cares more about benefiting themselves than helping others ↔ Somewhat selfish.
整句释义→一词概括
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Well disciplined. 盗用了答案句前那句铺垫里的 disciplined，但那句说的是『显得有钱的
人被认为更自律』，是 But 之前的对比信息，不是新研究对炫耀者的评价，听到
disciplined 就选正中陷阱。
借用原文：people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent, disciplined,
and competent
B) 未提及
Quite confident.『相当自信』录音通篇没有提到，是凭『炫耀的人大概很自信』的常识硬
推出来的，没有原文依据。
D) 原词陷阱
Highly intelligent. 盗用了铺垫句里的 intelligent，同样出自 But 之前『显得有钱者被认为
更聪明』的对比信息，不是新研究对炫耀者的真正评价，与 A 是同一类陷阱。
借用原文：people who appear to be wealthy tend to be considered more intelligent

questions.stem: When were participants more likely to choose someone who signaled their wealth or status?

options.label: A
options.text: When they wanted to have a competitive team member.

options.label: B
options.text: When they were looking for a cooperative workmate.

options.label: C
options.text: When they found collaboration essential to them.

options.label: D
options.text: When they were seeking someone to help them.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） When they wanted to have a competitive team member.
【定位】But participants were more likely to choose that person when they're looking for a
competitive team member.
但当参与者在寻找一名有竞争力的团队成员时，他们更倾向于选这个人。
【信号】转折 But + more likely。本段先说『seeking cooperative members 时不太会选』，But
participants were more likely to choose 用 But 转折并出现题干同款的 more likely to
choose，这句把『更愿意选』明确配给了后面那种情形，正是答案句。
【替换】looking for a competitive team member ↔
When they wanted to have a competitive team member.
近义动词替换
【排除】B) 与原文相反
When they were looking for a cooperative workmate. 盗用了 looking for 的句式和
『合作』概念，但录音说『找 cooperative members 时反而 less likely 选』，正好与题干
问的 more likely 相反，是把『不选』的情形错当成『选』的情形。
借用原文：participants were less likely to choose someone who signals their wealth or status to
join a group seeking cooperative members
C) 原词陷阱
When they found collaboration essential to them. 搬来第一段的 cooperation is
essential 那层意思（collaboration、essential），听着很耳熟，但那是讲『需要合作时该
谦逊』，与本题『更愿意选炫耀者』的情形无关，是典型听到熟词就想选的陷阱。
借用原文：Modesty may be key when cooperation is essential
D) 未提及
When they were seeking someone to help them.『想找人帮忙时』录音从未把『更愿意
选炫耀者』绑到这种情形上，是凭常识臆造的条件，无原文依据。

questions.stem: What should people do when sharing their wealth and status online?

options.label: A
options.text: Avoid frightening competitors.

options.label: B
options.text: Make clear their social goal.

options.label: C
options.text: Adopt persuasive strategies.

options.label: D
options.text: Consider the consequences.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Consider the consequences.
【定位】People can easily share their wealth and status to large audiences, but they need to consider
the consequences.
人们可以轻松地向广大受众展示自己的财富和地位，但他们需要考虑后果。
【信号】建议信号 need to + 转折 but。末段先说『社媒能轻易把财富地位分享给大众』，but
they need to consider the consequences 用 but 转折并带 need to（需要做某事）这一
建议信号，把『该怎么做』直接点出，是答案句。
【替换】need to consider the consequences ↔ Consider the consequences.
建议句去主语即选项
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Avoid frightening competitors. 搬来末段的 frighten competitors，但录音说炫耀『可以
帮你吓退竞争者』，那是分享地位的好处之一，并非『应该做什么』的建议；而且选项加了
Avoid（避免）把意思反成『避免吓退』，与原文方向不符。
借用原文：Posting about luxury purchases and expensive vacations online may help you to
persuade others and frighten competitors
B) 张冠李戴
Make clear their social goal. 借了第二段的 depending on their social goal，但那句讲
的是『按社交目标调整自我展示』，不是末段『网上分享该怎么做』的建议，是把别段内容
安到本题头上。
借用原文：people should change how they present themselves depending on their social goal
C) 原词陷阱
Adopt persuasive strategies. 盗用末段 persuade others 的词根（persuasive），但录音
说炫耀『可以帮你说服别人』也是好处之一，不是建议人去『采取说服策略』，属听到
persuade 就想选的陷阱。
借用原文：may help you to persuade others

questions.stem: What can we see in the oldest cave paintings?

options.label: A
options.text: Much evidence of humans capturing animals.

options.label: B
options.text: More images of animals than humans.

options.label: C
options.text: Fewer images of buildings than animals.

options.label: D
options.text: Little proof of human fascination with animals.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） More images of animals than humans.
【定位】Of the oldest cave paintings discovered, some are up to 40,000 years old, and there are more
images of animals than humans.
在已发现的最古老的洞穴壁画中，有些距今多达四万年，而且其中动物的图像比人类的图像
更多。
【信号】题干原词 oldest cave paintings 复现处。原文 Of the oldest cave paintings
discovered 与题干 the oldest cave paintings 是同一处，紧跟其后的 there are more
images of animals than humans 就是承载答案的关键句，靠题干主题词在原文复现来
定位。
【替换】more images of animals than humans ↔ More images of animals than humans.
几乎原句照搬
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Much evidence of humans capturing animals. 盗用了下一句 humans began to
capture and hold animals 的 capture 一词，但那讲的是后来人类开始圈养动物，不是壁
画内容；题问壁画里能看到什么，答非所问。
借用原文：humans began to capture and hold animals
C) 未提及
Fewer images of buildings than animals. 里的 buildings 在第一段壁画的描述中根本没
提（buildings 出现在第二段讲埃及建筑处），壁画只比较了 animals 与 humans，没说
buildings 的图像，属凭空捏造。
D) 与原文相反
Little proof of human fascination with animals. 用了开头句 Human fascination with
animals 的原词，却说成 Little proof（很少证据）；而原文开头明说人类对动物的迷恋自
古就有、壁画里动物图像还更多，恰恰是证据充分，极性完全相反。
借用原文：Human fascination with animals goes back as far as humans do

questions.stem: What do we learn about the first-known collections of animals?

options.label: A
options.text: They were open to the public.

options.label: B
options.text: They were primarily native.

options.label: C
options.text: They were kept by royalty.

options.label: D
options.text: They were hardly injured.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） They were kept by royalty.
【定位】The first-known collections were held by royalty and were not open to the public.
已知最早的（动物）收藏由王室持有，并且不对公众开放。
【信号】题干主语 first-known collections 在原文复现处。原文 The first-known collections
were held by royalty 与题干 the first-known collections of animals 是同一主语，紧跟
其后对「归谁所有、是否开放」的正面陈述就是答案句，靠题干主语在原文复现来定位。
【替换】were held by royalty ↔ They were kept by royalty.
held 同义替换为 kept
【排除】A) 与原文相反
They were open to the public. 借用了原文 not open to the public 里的 open to the
public 短语，却把否定的 not 去掉，说成对公众开放；原文恰恰说这些最早的收藏不对公
众开放，极性相反。
借用原文：were not open to the public
B) 与原文相反
They were primarily native. 盗用了原文 native 一词，却把意思整个说反：原文是 not
native to Egypt（大象不是埃及本土的），选项却说 primarily native（主要是本土的），
方向相反。
借用原文：which were not native to Egypt
D) 与原文相反
They were hardly injured. 借用了原文 injuries 一词，却说几乎没受伤；原文明说 their
remains show evidence of severe injuries（遗骸显示有严重伤害），是伤得很重，与选
项正好相反。
借用原文：their remains show evidence of severe injuries

questions.stem: What might be the reason the Egyptian Queen created the zoo?

options.label: A
options.text: To enable the public to watch animals close by.

options.label: B
options.text: To introduce to Egyptians animals from Punt.

options.label: C
options.text: To protect the endangered animals.

options.label: D
options.text: To show off her riches and power.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （目的题） To show off her riches and power.
【定位】It's unclear why the Queen built the zoo, but it might have been to show off her wealth
and power.
女王为何建这座动物园尚不清楚，但可能是为了炫耀她的财富与权力。
【信号】转折 but 之后的目的句。答案句的信号是转折加目的：It's unclear why 先说原因不明，转
折词 but 之后 it might have been to show off her wealth and power 才给出真正的可能
原因，but 后 + to do 处即答案。
【替换】to show off her wealth and power ↔ To show off her riches and power.
wealth 同义替换为 riches
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
To enable the public to watch animals close by. 把第三段开头 The first public exhibit
of animals 里的 public 拿来当动机，但 public exhibit 只是给这座动物园定性，原文说的
建园原因是炫耀财富权力，不是为让公众近距离看动物。
借用原文：The first public exhibit of animals
B) 张冠李戴
To introduce to Egyptians animals from Punt. 盗用了原文 a far-off land known as
Punt 的地名 Punt，但原文说 Punt 只是动物的来源地（从那带回动物），不是建园是为了
向埃及人介绍这些动物，张冠李戴。
借用原文：animals brought home from a far-off land known as Punt
C) 未提及
To protect the endangered animals. 说为保护濒危动物，但全文从未提到 protect 或
endangered，建园原因原文只给了炫耀财富权力一种，属凭空添加。

questions.stem: What do we learn about King Henry I's collection of animals in England?

options.label: A
options.text: It was part of the royal estate.

options.label: B
options.text: It was a shelter for wild animals.

options.label: C
options.text: It was the kingdom's best-equipped zoo.

options.label: D
options.text: It was the first public exhibit of animals.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） It was part of the royal estate.
【定位】In England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals in about 1110 as part of the
royal estate.
在英格兰，亨利一世国王约在 1110 年建立了一处动物收藏，作为王室领地的一部分。
【信号】人名 King Henry I 后紧跟的定性。定位靠人名复现：题干问 King Henry I，原文 In
England, King Henry I set up a collection of animals 一出现这个名字，紧跟的 as part
of the royal estate 就是对这处收藏的定性，即答案句。
【替换】as part of the royal estate ↔ It was part of the royal estate.
近乎原句对应
【排除】B) 未提及
It was a shelter for wild animals. 借用了全篇反复出现的 animals，但原文从没把亨利一
世这处收藏说成野生动物的庇护所（shelter），这是凭空添加的定性。
C) 过度推断
It was the kingdom's best-equipped zoo. 用 best-equipped（装备最好的）拔高，但原
文只说它是 part of the royal estate 并养有老虎狮子，从未评价它是王国里设施最好的动
物园，属过度拔高。
借用原文：His collection included tigers and lions
D) 张冠李戴
It was the first public exhibit of animals. 盗用了第三段 The first public exhibit of
animals 的原话，但那说的是埃及女王 Hatshepsut 的动物园，不是英格兰亨利一世这处，
把别处的定性安到了这处头上。
借用原文：The first public exhibit of animals may have been created by Egypt's Queen Hatshepsut
