questions.stem: Why did the police officer stop the SUV car?

options.label: A
options.text: He noticed the driver was too young to drive.

options.label: B
options.text: He found there was no one sitting at the wheel.

options.label: C
options.text: He thought something must be wrong with the driver.

options.label: D
options.text: He saw the driver changing lanes much too frequently.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） He thought something must be wrong with the driver.
【定位】A police officer in the U.S. stopped a large SUV car that was going very slowly and drifting
across lanes on a highway. He expected to find a driver who was either very drunk or having
a medical emergency.
美国一名警察拦下了一辆在高速公路上行驶得非常缓慢、还在车道间飘忽乱晃的大型 SUV。
他原以为会发现一个要么烂醉、要么突发疾病的司机。
【信号】开篇即点题、紧跟一句"原以为"的推断。新闻把核心事件放在第一句：车 going very
slowly and drifting across lanes（开得很慢、车道间乱飘）。紧接着 He expected to
find a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency 这句"警察原
以为"，直接道出他判断"司机一定出了问题"——这正是拦车的真实理由。
【替换】a driver who was either very drunk or having a medical emergency ↔
something must be wrong with the driver
具体病况概括成"司机有问题"
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
录音后面确实揭晓司机是 a five-year-old boy（五岁男孩），A 项 He noticed the driver
was too young to drive.（发现司机太小不能开车）就盗用了这个"年龄小"的事实。但那是
警察拦车"之后"才发现的真相，并非拦车的原因——拦车时他根本看不清开车的是谁。听
到"小孩"就选 A，正中原词陷阱。
借用原文：a five-year-old boy sat on the edge of the driver's seat
B) 与原文相反
B 项 He found there was no one sitting at the wheel.（发现没人坐在方向盘后）听起来
很像那个离奇画面，但录音说的是男孩 sat on the edge of the driver's seat——其实有人
坐在驾驶位，只是个小孩。而且"座位上情况"是拦车后才看清的，拦车当下警察只看到车乱
晃。B 既与原文不符、又答非所问。
借用原文：a five-year-old boy sat on the edge of the driver's seat
D) 偷换概念
D 项 He saw the driver changing lanes much too frequently.（看到司机频繁变道）盗
用了原文 drifting across lanes 里的 lanes。但 drifting across lanes 是"车失控地在车道
间飘移乱晃"（因为开车的是够不着踏板的小孩），不是司机主动、频繁地变换车道。D
把"失控飘移"偷换成"频繁变道"，看似沾边实则两回事。
借用原文：drifting across lanes on a highway

questions.stem: What did the boy tell the police officers he was planning to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Buy a sports car.

options.label: B
options.text: Drive across town.

options.label: C
options.text: Leave California.

options.label: D
options.text: Visit his sister.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Buy a sports car.
【定位】The boy later told confused officers that he was planning to travel to California and buy a
Lamborghini sports car.
男孩后来告诉一脸困惑的警察，他打算开去加利福尼亚，买一辆兰博基尼跑车。
【信号】planning to 直接引出打算做的事。信号词 he was planning to travel to California and
buy a Lamborghini sports car 里的 planning to 正是"表打算"的标志，其后跟着的两个动
作（去加州、买跑车）就是男孩的计划，是题目要的答案落点。
【替换】buy a Lamborghini sports car ↔ Buy a sports car.
去掉品牌名后即同一动作
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
B 项 Drive across town.（开车穿过城镇）盗用了原文 drove three kilometers across
town 里的 across town。但"开车穿城"是男孩已经做过的事（他已经开了三公里穿过城镇
上高速），不是他"打算"做的事。题目问的是 planning to 之后的计划，B 把"已发生"偷换
成"打算做"，答非所问。
借用原文：He then drove three kilometers across town before getting on the highway.
C) 与原文相反
C 项 Leave California.（离开加州）盗用了地名 California，但录音说的是 travel to
California（去往加州），方向恰好相反——是去、不是离开。地名一念到极易被耳朵抓
住，但方向词（to / leave）被悄悄反转，最易让人误选。
借用原文：he was planning to travel to California
D) 原词陷阱
D 项 Visit his sister.（看望他姐姐）盗用了原文出现的 sister。但 sister 在录音里只是"趁姐
姐午睡时拿了车钥匙"的背景人物（while his teenage sister was napping），男孩的计划
是去加州买跑车，从没说过要去看望姐姐。这是把一个出现过的人名硬塞进"计划"里。
借用原文：while his teenage sister was napping
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Mobile phones have changed the way we live, how we read, work, communicate, and shop. But
we already know this. What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us
are changing our skeletons, possibly altering not just the way we behave but even the very shape of
our bodies.
手机已经改变了我们的生活方式，改变了我们阅读、工作、交流和购物的方式。但我们已经知道这一点。
我们尚未理解的是，我们面前的这些小型机器正在改变我们的骨骼，可能不仅改变我们的行为方式，甚至
改变我们身体的形状。
2 New scientific research at the University of the Sunshine Coast in Queensland, Australia, suggests that
young people are developing extra pieces of bone at the backs of their heads. These pieces of bone are
caused by the way people bend their heads when they use the phone. This shifts weight onto the
muscles at the back of the head and causes the bone to grow in a way that is not normal. This process
can be compared to the way the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing or pressure. The result is a
piece of bone like a horn that sticks out from the head by the neck.
澳大利亚昆士兰阳光海岸大学的最新科学研究表明，年轻人的后脑勺正在长出额外的骨块。这些骨块是由
人们使用手机时低头的方式造成的。这会将重量转移到后脑勺的肌肉上，并导致骨骼以不正常的方式生
长。这一过程可以与皮肤因持续摩擦或压力而变硬的方式相比较。其结果是在颈部附近从头部突出的一块
类似角的骨头。

questions.stem: What does the report say we have not yet understood about mobile phones?

options.label: A
options.text: How they change the way we shop.

options.label: B
options.text: How they alter human skeletons.

options.label: C
options.text: How they cause increased headaches.

options.label: D
options.text: How they affect our communication.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） How they alter human skeletons.
【定位】What we have not yet understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us are changing our
skeletons, possibly altering not just the way we behave but even the very shape of our bodies.
我们还没有理解的，是眼前这些小小的机器正在改变我们的骨骼这件事——它们或许不仅改
变我们的行为方式，甚至会改变我们身体的形状。
【信号】题干原话 we have not yet understood 直接复现。录音里 What we have not yet
understood is the way the tiny machines in front of us are changing our skeletons 把
题干的核心短语 "we have not yet understood" 原样念出，这种 "题干关键词在原文出现"
就是答案句的定位信号，紧跟其后的 changing our skeletons 即所求。
【替换】changing our skeletons ↔ How they alter human skeletons.
changing 同义替换为 alter
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
录音开头 how we read, work, communicate, and shop 确实念到 shop 购物，但紧接着
说 But we already know this——购物属于 "我们已经知道" 的部分，而题目问的是 "还没
理解" 的，正好相反，选它就掉进了原词陷阱。
借用原文：how we read, work, communicate, and shop
C) 未提及
选项 How they cause increased headaches. 说手机导致头痛增多，但整段录音从未提到
headaches 头痛，是凭 "手机看多了会头疼" 的生活常识硬加的，属无中生有。
D) 原词陷阱
录音里 how we read, work, communicate, and shop 念到 communicate 沟通，How
they affect our communication. 借此设套；但沟通和购物一样属于 But we already
know this 已知的部分，不是题问的 "还没理解" 的，故错。
借用原文：how we read, work, communicate, and shop

questions.stem: What happens to the skin when rubbed or pressed constantly?

options.label: A
options.text: It loosens.

options.label: B
options.text: It brightens.

options.label: C
options.text: It hardens.

options.label: D
options.text: It softens.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） It hardens.
【定位】This process can be compared to the way the skin hardens in response to constant rubbing
or pressure.
这个过程可以类比皮肤在持续摩擦或受压之下变硬的方式。
【信号】题干关键词 skin、rubbing、pressure 同句聚齐。录音 the skin hardens in response to
constant rubbing or pressure 把题干的 skin、rubbed / pressed（原文作 rubbing /
pressure）几个词凑在同一句，关键词集中出现即答案句信号，紧跟的动词 hardens 就是
结果。
【替换】the skin hardens ↔ It hardens.
the skin 由 It 指代、hardens 原词承接
【排除】A) 未提及
It loosens. 说变松，但录音讲皮肤是 hardens 变硬，没有任何 "变松" 的说法，纯属无中生
有。
B) 未提及
It brightens. 说变亮，录音谈的是皮肤受摩擦后 hardens 变硬的物理硬化，与 "变亮" 毫不
相干，录音也未提及。
D) 与原文相反
It softens. 变软，恰与录音 the skin hardens 变硬相反。这是预读时就标好的反义诱选
——一字方向之差，听不清硬 / 软就会反选。
借用原文：the skin hardens

questions.stem: What does the report say the village is going to do for the cat Wilbur?

options.label: A
options.text: Create Internet pages for him.

options.label: B
options.text: Ask a local pet shop to adopt him.

options.label: C
options.text: Name an orange tree after him.

options.label: D
options.text: Hold a birthday party for him.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Hold a birthday party for him.
【定位】A village is going to throw a birthday party for an orange cat named Wilbur, who has become
famous for making a regular appearance at local shops.
一座村庄即将为一只名叫 Wilbur 的橘猫举办生日派对，这只猫因为经常出现在当地店铺而
声名鹊起。
【信号】开篇 going to 句式即新闻核心事件。新闻第一句 A village is going to throw a birthday
party for an orange cat named Wilbur 用 going to 直接给出整条新闻的核心事件，符合
短篇新闻「开门见山报导何事」的体例，是本题的答案句无疑。
【替换】is going to throw a birthday party ↔ Hold a birthday party for him.
throw=hold 的同义词替换
for an orange cat named Wilbur ↔ for him
具体名词到人称代词的概括
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 Create Internet pages for him. 借用了第二段 Wilbur has his own Internet pages
这一原词，但原文说的是 Wilbur 已经拥有自己的网页（既成事实），而非村庄「将要为他
创建」网页，且这件事不是「村庄为他做的事」，属于答非所问加时态错位的双重陷阱。
借用原文：Wilbur has his own Internet pages
B) 未提及
选项 Ask a local pet shop to adopt him. 抓住了录音里反复出现的 local shops 这一概
念，但录音从未提及 pet shop 或 adopt——Wilbur 是已经有人照看的明星猫，「让宠物
店领养他」是凭借 cat/shops 自行联想的过度推断。
C) 原词陷阱
选项 Name an orange tree after him. 同时盗用了 an orange cat 中的 orange 和
named Wilbur 中的 name，制造「以橘猫之名命名橘树」的错觉，但原文里 orange 修饰
的是 cat、name 是给猫命名，与「橘树」毫无关系。
借用原文：an orange cat named Wilbur

questions.stem: What do we learn from the report about the cat?

options.label: A
options.text: He is a bold and aggressive pet.

options.label: B
options.text: He pays regular visits to village shops.

options.label: C
options.text: He once bit a doctor's receptionist.

options.label: D
options.text: He likes to sit on the hairdresser's chair.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） He pays regular visits to village shops.
【定位】He spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village. He'll just take himself
into any shop, anywhere.
他的大部分时间都泡在村里的店铺和商家里，他会自顾自地走进任何一家店，到处都是。
【信号】频次副词 most of his time 与范围词 any/anywhere 强调常态。He spends most of his
time in shops and businesses around the village 里的 most of his time 与紧接着的
He'll just take himself into any shop, anywhere 中的 any/anywhere，都是高强度的频
次与范围信号，明确告诉考生「经常去店铺」是这只猫的常态行为——这正是 B 项 regular
visits 的答案信号。
【替换】spends most of his time in shops and businesses around the village ↔
pays regular visits to village shops.
频次副词 most of his time 与 regular 等值
shops and businesses around the village ↔ village shops
村庄里的店铺这一对象一致
making a regular appearance at local shops ↔ pays regular visits to village shops.
regular appearance 与 regular visits 直接对应
【排除】A) 与原文相反
选项 He is a bold and aggressive pet. 盗用了录音里 Wilbur is both bold and friendly
中的 bold，但把后半句的 friendly 偷偷换成了 aggressive。bold 在 friendly 与
aggressive 两种语境下意思走向完全相反，原文明确说他是 bold and friendly（大胆又友
好），与 aggressive 截然相反。
借用原文：Wilbur is both bold and friendly
C) 原词陷阱
选项 He once bit a doctor's receptionist. 借用了录音里 the doctor's receptionist came
back and he was sitting on her chair 中 receptionist 这一原词，但原文说的是「前台回
来时发现他坐在自己椅子上」，根本没有「咬人」这一情节。bite 是凭「猫与人接触」自行
加戏的虚构事件。
借用原文：the doctor's receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair
D) 张冠李戴
选项 He likes to sit on the hairdresser's chair. 把「坐在椅子上」这一情节（原文里发生
在 the doctor's receptionist came back and he was sitting on her chair 即医生前台的
椅子上）安到了理发店的椅子上。原文只在 Among his favorite haunts are a local
hairdresser 里提及理发店是他常去的地方之一，但并未说他喜欢坐理发店椅子。
借用原文：Among his favorite haunts are a local hairdresser

questions.stem: What does the pub owner, Lesley Harper, say about the cat?

options.label: A
options.text: He is fond of luxury cat food.

options.label: B
options.text: He likes to stay in villagers' houses.

options.label: C
options.text: He knows everybody in the village.

options.label: D
options.text: He often seeks food around her pub.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） He is fond of luxury cat food.
【定位】She also said he is a cat of expensive tastes who likes his high priced cat food.
她还说他是一只品味奢侈的猫，喜欢吃高价猫粮。
【信号】She also said 引出直接信息源加 expensive/high priced 同向强化。She also said he is
a cat of expensive tastes who likes his high priced cat food 用 She also said 直接把信
息归到 Lesley Harper 名下，且 expensive tastes 与 high priced 在「奢侈高档」这一语
义维度上同向强化，正是 A 项 luxury 的答案信号。
【替换】a cat of expensive tastes ↔ He is fond of luxury cat food.
expensive tastes 与 fond of luxury 同义概括
likes his high priced cat food ↔ fond of luxury cat food
high priced=luxury 的近义替换
【排除】B) 偷换概念
选项 He likes to stay in villagers' houses. 借了录音中 happy for customers and
villagers young and old to come in and say hello 里的 villagers 一词，但原文说的是
「乐于让村民和顾客进店打招呼」——他待的是酒馆，村民是进店打招呼的人，「待在村民
家里」这一情节子虚乌有。
借用原文：happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello
C) 过度推断
选项 He knows everybody in the village. 把录音里 happy for customers and villagers
young and old to come in and say hello 这种「乐于和顾客与村民打招呼」的描述夸大成
「认识村里每个人」。原文从未说他「认识」任何人，更没说 everybody，是典型的范围极
大化推断。
借用原文：happy for customers and villagers young and old to come in and say hello
D) 原词陷阱
选项 He often seeks food around her pub. 借了酒馆这一场景设定，但 Lesley Harper 从
未说他「在酒馆附近觅食」。原文里关于「食物」的唯一说法是 high priced cat food，重
点在「高档」而非「在酒馆附近找」。seeks food around her pub 是把场景与食物两个真
实元素硬拼出的虚构动作。
借用原文：high priced cat food

questions.stem: What are the speakers talking about in this conversation?

options.label: A
options.text: Who to order the food.

options.label: B
options.text: Whether to have sandwiches.

options.label: C
options.text: When to go for their meal.

options.label: D
options.text: Where to have their lunch.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （主旨题） Where to have their lunch.
【定位】M: So, where do you want to go for lunch?
男：那你想去哪儿吃午饭？
【信号】开门见山的话题问句。where do you want to go for lunch? 是对话的第一句，用 So 起头
直接抛话题，正是听力主旨题最常用的开头点题信号。后续整段所有讨论（三明治店、汉堡
店、意大利餐厅）都是围绕这句话在选地方吃午饭。
【替换】where do you want to go for lunch? ↔ Where to have their lunch.
where to go 与 where to have 同义
【排除】A) 未提及
全篇对话围绕选餐厅展开，从头到尾没有任何一句提到由谁来点食物，纯属 Who to order
the food. 制造的无中生有。
B)
录音里 What about the Sandwich Place on Camden Street? 与 I don't feel like
sandwiches today. 确实念到了 sandwiches，Whether to have sandwiches. 就盗用了这
个原词，让「听到原词就想选」的考生中招。但实际上三明治只是男方第一个提议的备选之
一，被否决后整段对话又讨论了汉堡、意大利餐厅，三明治远不足以代表主旨。
借用原文：I don't feel like sandwiches today.
C)
录音里 I need to get back by 2:30 for a conference call. 出现了具体时间，但那是女方解
释自己时间紧、不要选服务慢的店的附带理由，整段对话从未围绕「几点去吃」展开讨论，
When to go for their meal. 把次要约束当主线。
借用原文：I need to get back by 2:30 for a conference call.

questions.stem: Where did the speakers see Brigette Clark, the famous movie star?

options.label: A
options.text: In the shopping center nearby.

options.label: B
options.text: In the expensive Italian style diner.

options.label: C
options.text: At the Sandwich Place on Camden Street.

options.label: D
options.text: At the American restaurant they frequent.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） At the Sandwich Place on Camden Street.
【定位】M: That's true. Remember that's where we saw Brigette Clark, the famous movie star.
男：确实。记得吗？我们就是在那儿见过 Brigette Clark，那个有名的电影明星。
【信号】that's where + 回指。that's where we saw Brigette Clark 用 that's where 把「那个地
方」指回上一句男声提到的 the Sandwich Place on Camden Street，回指词 that 是细节
定位的关键信号——它不是新地点，而是回指刚出现过的那个地点。
【替换】the Sandwich Place on Camden Street ↔ At the Sandwich Place on Camden Street.
原句锁回指对象
that's where we saw Brigette Clark, the famous movie star ↔
At the Sandwich Place on Camden Street.
回指 that = 三明治店
【排除】A)
录音里只在第 7 段提到 on the way to the mall（去商场路上）作为美式餐厅的位置描述，
但商场本身从未作为见明星的地点出现，In the shopping center nearby. 属于无中生有。
借用原文：on the way to the mall
B) 原词陷阱
录音里 We could try Mario's, the new Italian restaurant on the corner. 与 I haven't,
but I've noticed that it has great reviews 都明确说 Mario's 是他们还没去过的新意餐
厅，与「在那儿见过明星」在逻辑上完全冲突，In the expensive Italian style diner. 盗用
了 Italian 这个原词制造干扰。
借用原文：Mario's, the new Italian restaurant on the corner
D)
录音里 There's that American style diner on the way to the mall. 出现了 American 这
个原词，At the American restaurant they frequent. 就盗用它制造干扰；但原文从未说他
们常去那家美式餐厅，而且这家餐厅是男方拿来作为今天午饭的备选，与见明星这件已发生
事毫无关联。
借用原文：There's that American style diner on the way to the mall.

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she needs to get back by 2:30?

options.label: A
options.text: There is to be a conference call.

options.label: B
options.text: She has to meet with her boss then.

options.label: C
options.text: There will be crowds of people waiting for her.

options.label: D
options.text: She will have a photo taken with Brigette Clark.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） There is to be a conference call.
【定位】W: I like that place. Their chips are great, but their service takes a long time. And I need to
get back by 2:30 for a conference call.
女：我喜欢那家。他们的薯条很棒，但上菜慢。而且我得在 2:30 之前赶回去开电话会议。
【信号】for + 原因短语。I need to get back by 2:30 for a conference call. 中的 for 是原因介
词，直接把 2:30 这个时间点和「开电话会议」这个理由焊死。Why 类题听到
for/because/so that 就要立刻锁定，理由就在它后面。
【替换】for a conference call ↔ There is to be a conference call.
for + 名词转 there is to be
【排除】B)
录音从头到尾没有任何 boss、manager、meet with 之类的词，She has to meet with
her boss then. 完全是无中生有。
C) 原词陷阱
录音 There were crowds of people around her asking for a photo with her. 里确实出
现了 crowds of people，There will be crowds of people waiting for her. 就盗用了这个
原词；但原文里那群人围的是 Brigette Clark，不是女方，C 把围观对象张冠李戴到她身
上，且时态从过去 were 偷换成将来 will be。
借用原文：There were crowds of people around her asking for a photo with her.
D) 原词陷阱
录音 asking for a photo with her 出现 photo，Brigette Clark 出现人名，She will have
a photo taken with Brigette Clark. 把这两个原词拼成「女方将与 Brigette Clark 合影」
的新事件——这件事原文从未发生，是典型的原词拼接陷阱。
借用原文：asking for a photo with her

questions.stem: Why does the woman say Jeremy should throw his soup in the bin?

options.label: A
options.text: She doesn't deem homemade soup tasty.

options.label: B
options.text: She doesn't think his wife cooks well.

options.label: C
options.text: She feels Jeremy would rather dine out.

options.label: D
options.text: She has found the soup smells terrible.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （推断题） She doesn't think his wife cooks well.
【定位】W: Poor Jeremy. His wife is a terrible cook. He should throw that soup in the bin and join us.
女：可怜的 Jeremy。他妻子是个糟糕的厨师。他真该把那碗汤扔了，跟我们一起去。
【信号】终判式因果链。His wife is a terrible cook. He should throw that soup in the bin 是一
个语义上的因果链：先下评判 His wife is a terrible cook，再据此建议 He should
throw…。前一句就是建议的真正原因，是答案句中最关键的承载句。
【替换】His wife is a terrible cook. ↔ She doesn't think his wife cooks well.
贬义形容词转含蓄否定
【排除】A) 偷换概念
录音里女方的批评对象是 His wife（人 - 妻子的厨艺），不是汤本身。She doesn't deem
homemade soup tasty. 把矛头从「妻子厨艺差」偷换成「她觉得家常汤本身不好吃」，是
范围偏移。她没有否定家常汤这个品类，只是否定他妻子做的这一碗。
借用原文：His wife is a terrible cook.
C)
录音 He should throw that soup in the bin and join us. 出现了 join us，She feels
Jeremy would rather dine out. 就据此过度推断成「她觉得 Jeremy 更愿意出去吃」。但
女方建议他出来吃是她的提议，不是 Jeremy 自己的偏好；原文里 Jeremy 自己说的是 He
has brought his own lunch today, so he will stay in.，恰恰是要留下不出去。C 把女方的
建议错认成 Jeremy 的意愿，过度推断且方向反了。
借用原文：He should throw that soup in the bin and join us.
D) 原词陷阱
录音里女方说的是 His wife is a terrible cook.——评价做菜人的水平，从未提到汤闻起来
怎么样。She has found the soup smells terrible. 盗用了 terrible 这个原词，但把它从修
饰 cook 偷换为修饰 smells，是经典的「原词换搭配」陷阱。
借用原文：His wife is a terrible cook.

questions.stem: Who is the man talking to in the conversation?

options.label: A
options.text: A landlady.

options.label: B
options.text: A waitress.

options.label: C
options.text: A receptionist.

options.label: D
options.text: A saleswoman.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） A receptionist.
【定位】Hi, there. How are you today? Do you have a reservation with us already?
你好，今天感觉如何？您已经在我们这里预订了吗？
【信号】开场专属话术。Do you have a reservation with us already? 是酒店前台接待客人时最典
型的开场询问——问『是否有预订』。这种『询问预订』的话术是接待员的专属标记，是定
身份的信号句。
【替换】Do you have a reservation with us already? ↔ A receptionist.
话术 → 身份的同义替换
I can get you all checked in and show you to your rooms. ↔ A receptionist.
结尾办理入住二次确认
【排除】A) 未提及
A landlady. 是出租房屋的房东，话术应是 rent/deposit/lease，不会用 reservation 这类
酒店术语；录音里也没有出现任何与租房相关的词。
B) 原词陷阱
A waitress. 是餐厅服务员。录音 has all kinds of food and cool little shops 确实提到了
food，但讲的是夜市，不是接待方提供餐饮服务，属于典型原词陷阱——听到 food 就误以
为对方是 waitress。
借用原文：has all kinds of food and cool little shops selling souvenirs and local jewelry and
clothing made by hand
D) 原词陷阱
A saleswoman. 是售货员。录音 cool little shops selling souvenirs and local jewelry
and clothing made by hand 确实提到了『卖纪念品和手工衣物的小店』，但卖东西的是
夜市的小店，不是这位接待者，属于典型原词陷阱。
借用原文：cool little shops selling souvenirs and local jewelry and clothing made by hand

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man's father-in-law from the conversation?

options.label: A
options.text: He was involved in a terrible car accident last April.

options.label: B
options.text: He has much difficulty getting up and down stairs.

options.label: C
options.text: He is expected to undergo a knee operation.

options.label: D
options.text: He prefers to stay next door to the children.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） He has much difficulty getting up and down stairs.
【定位】My father-in-law has had terrible problems getting up and down stairs since his knee
operation last April.
我岳父自从去年四月做了膝关节手术以来，上下楼梯一直有很大困难。
【信号】现在完成时 + since 圈定当前状态。has had terrible problems getting up and down
stairs since his knee operation last April 中 has had 是现在完成时，配合 since…，明确
这是『从手术之后一直延续到现在的状况』。手术（knee operation）是过去事件、上下楼
梯困难（getting up and down stairs）才是当前状态——也就是题目要问的『现在我们了
解到他怎么样』。
【替换】has had terrible problems getting up and down stairs ↔
He has much difficulty getting up and down stairs.
terrible problems = much difficulty
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
He was involved in a terrible car accident last April. 盗用了录音里的 terrible 与 last
April 这两个高辨识度词，制造『我好像听见 terrible 和 last April』的错觉，但录音里 last
April 修饰的是 knee operation（膝关节手术），不是 car accident（车祸）；车祸录音里
根本没提。
借用原文：has had terrible problems getting up and down stairs since his knee operation last April
C) 与原文相反
He is expected to undergo a knee operation. 用 is expected to undergo（将要做）描
述膝关节手术，但录音里 since his knee operation last April 说的是『自从去年四月做了
手术之后』——手术已经做完。时态从过去/完成偷换成将来，与原文相反。
借用原文：since his knee operation last April
D) 张冠李戴
He prefers to stay next door to the children. 借用了录音 right next to each other on
the ground floor 里 next to 的安排关系，但录音说的是『前台把两间房安排在彼此隔
壁』，并不是岳父 prefers（更愿意）住孩子隔壁，主语与动机都被替换。
借用原文：right next to each other on the ground floor, since you mentioned in your message that
they have trouble with stairs

questions.stem: Why does the man say they will explore all the options available?

options.label: A
options.text: To please his parents-in-law.

options.label: B
options.text: To find the best trip for his kids.

options.label: C
options.text: To satisfy his curiosity.

options.label: D
options.text: To compare prices.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） To compare prices.
【定位】We were thinking of renting a car, but we will explore all the options available for sure. So,
yes, that would be very helpful in comparing prices.
我们本来打算租辆车，但我们一定会把所有可选方案都看一遍。所以，是的，这对比价会很
有帮助。
【信号】So + that would be very helpful in...。So, yes, that would be very helpful in
comparing prices. 中 So 是结果连词，紧跟前一句『会把所有方案都看一遍』，that
would be very helpful in 直接说明这样做的好处/目的——comparing prices（比价）。
这就是男方自报动机的关键句。
【替换】that would be very helpful in comparing prices ↔ To compare prices.
be helpful in V-ing → To do
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
To please his parents-in-law. 利用了录音 another double room for your parents-in-
law 里 parents-in-law 这个原词，让人误以为『探索所有方案是为了照顾岳父母』，但录
音里只说他们『住一楼』，从未把『探索方案』的动机归到讨好岳父母上。
借用原文：another double room for your parents-in-law
B) 原词陷阱
To find the best trip for his kids. 利用了录音 The kids will love it 里出现的 kids 与 trip
两个原词，制造『是为了给孩子找最佳旅程』的错觉。但 The kids will love it 是女方推荐
boat trip 时说的，男方说『探索所有方案』的动机不是这件事。
借用原文：The kids will love it and there are so many islands nearby to explore
C) 未提及
To satisfy his curiosity. 录音里完全没有出现 curiosity 或与好奇心相关的表达；选项是凭
空加的目的，属于未提及型干扰。

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest the man and his family do close to the end of the conversation?

options.label: A
options.text: Visit a local art gallery.

options.label: B
options.text: Go on a boat trip.

options.label: C
options.text: Take some photos of the islands.

options.label: D
options.text: Try her hand-made clothing.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Go on a boat trip.
【定位】I would recommend getting out on a boat trip. The kids will love it and there are so many
islands nearby to explore.
我会推荐你们去坐船出游一趟。孩子们会很喜欢，附近还有很多岛屿可以探索。
【信号】I would recommend... 建议句。I would recommend getting out on a boat trip. 中 I
would recommend 是最显性的建议信号词，紧跟的动作 getting out on a boat trip 就是
被建议的事。
【替换】getting out on a boat trip ↔ Go on a boat trip.
getting out on = Go on
【排除】A) 未提及
Visit a local art gallery. 录音里完全没有提到 art gallery（艺术画廊）；女方推荐的是
boat trip 和 night market，画廊纯属选项添加的迷惑活动。
C) 原词陷阱
Take some photos of the islands. 利用了录音 there are so many islands nearby to
explore 里出现的 islands 一词，让人以为『建议去拍岛屿照片』。但原文里 islands 是
boat trip 时『可以探索』的对象，女方从未建议『拍照』；take photos 这个动作录音里
没有出现。
借用原文：there are so many islands nearby to explore
D) 张冠李戴
Try her hand-made clothing. 利用了录音 clothing made by hand 这个原词组，但录音
里 clothing made by hand 是『夜市小店在卖』的东西，不是『她』（前台接待员）自己
手工做的，也不是被建议的核心动作；同时 try（试穿/尝试）这个动作录音里也没有。
借用原文：clothing made by hand

questions.stem: What does the passage say about artificial intelligence agents?

options.label: A
options.text: They are more intelligent than many of us.

options.label: B
options.text: They have already become our new friends.

options.label: C
options.text: They have begun to affect our social behavior.

options.label: D
options.text: They play increasingly more important roles.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） They play increasingly more important roles.
【定位】Artificial intelligence agents play ever more influential roles in our lives.
人工智能代理在我们的生活中扮演着越来越具有影响力的角色。
【信号】篇章首句即点题句。答案句正是录音的第一句 Artificial intelligence agents play ever
more influential roles in our lives.：篇章独白的开头第一句几乎一定是点题句，直接给出
对象 + 总体评价，这是篇章听力定位最强的信号——比任何转折词都更稳。
【替换】play ever more influential roles ↔ play increasingly more important roles
ever more 与 increasingly 同义改写
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
They are more intelligent than many of us. 利用了录音里 Artificial intelligence agents
中 intelligence 这个词，把 "人工智能" 偷换成 "它们比我们许多人更聪明"。录音从未把 AI
与人做智力比较，主体考生一听到 intelligence 就反射性挑 intelligent 是典型的原词陷
阱。
借用原文：Artificial intelligence agents
B) 与原文相反
They have already become our new friends. 利用了录音里 suggesting new friends
（替我们推荐新朋友），把 "推荐朋友" 偷换成 "它们自己已经成为我们的新朋友"。这是
already + 完成时把功能性服务夸大为既成事实，方向已经反了。
借用原文：suggesting new friends
C) 偷换概念
They have begun to affect our social behavior. 利用了录音里 play ever more
influential roles in our lives（在生活中起越来越重要的作用），把宽泛的 "生活" 偷换成专
指的 social behavior（社交行为）。录音从未提及 social behavior 这一具体范畴，属于把
宽口径收窄到一个录音没说过的窄范畴。
借用原文：play ever more influential roles in our lives

questions.stem: What does the new study want to find out about using an artificial intelligence agent?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether it might have any effect on the way we negotiate.

options.label: B
options.text: Whether it might actually outperform human negotiators.

options.label: C
options.text: Whether it can facilitate business transactions.

options.label: D
options.text: Whether it can speed up legal procedures.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Whether it might have any effect on the way we negotiate.
【定位】So, it's important to know whether using an artificial intelligence agent might affect how
we negotiate.
因此，弄清楚使用人工智能代理是否会影响我们谈判的方式，是很重要的。
【信号】So 引出结论 + know whether 引出研究问题。答案句以 So, it's important to know
whether using an artificial intelligence agent might affect how we negotiate. 出现：
So 是结论信号，it's important to know whether… 是研究问题的固定起手式——这是篇
章里 "研究想搞清什么" 最强的语言信号，几乎不会与别的句子搞混。
【替换】might affect how we negotiate ↔ might have any effect on the way we negotiate
动词 affect 与名词 effect 同根改写
it's important to know whether ↔ Whether it might have any effect on the way we negotiate.
Whether 从句被独立保留
【排除】B) 过度推断
Whether it might actually outperform human negotiators. 把研究问题从 "是否影响我
们的谈判方式" 强行升级为 "是否真的胜过人类谈判者"。录音里只问 affect，没有任何
outperform / beat / better than 的提法，是典型把 "有影响" 推到 "胜过" 的两步跳跃。
C) 原词陷阱
Whether it can facilitate business transactions. 直接搬用了录音里 commercial
transactions（商业交易）这个场景词。录音只是把 commercial transactions 列为 AI 代
理可能介入的应用场景之一，并没有把它定为研究问题；选项把 "场景" 偷换成 "研究问
题"，是典型听到原词就想选的陷阱。
借用原文：commercial transactions
D) 原词陷阱
Whether it can speed up legal procedures. 同样借用了录音里 legal disputes（法律纠
纷）这个场景词，再把名词改成 legal procedures（法律程序）。录音没有提加快速度
（speed up）这一研究目标，是 "原词靠近 + 概念替换" 的双重陷阱。
借用原文：legal disputes

questions.stem: What did participants tend to do when assigned an AI agent to negotiate on their behalf?

options.label: A
options.text: Choose to be tough.

options.label: B
options.text: Sympathize with their opponent.

options.label: C
options.text: Use deceptive strategies.

options.label: D
options.text: Appear to be pleasant.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Use deceptive strategies.
【定位】Participants were more willing to employ deceptive strategies when assigned an agent to
negotiate on their behalf.
当被安排一个代理替自己谈判时，参与者更愿意采用欺骗性策略。
【信号】段末 were more willing to 是结论信号。答案句出现在录音末尾 Participants were more
willing to employ deceptive strategies when assigned an agent to negotiate on their
behalf.：段末 + were more willing to 是研究类篇章给出实验结论最稳的双重信号——前
面 tough / sympathy / anger / dissatisfaction 都是为它做铺垫的策略列举，真正的结论
压到最后一句。
【替换】were more willing to employ deceptive strategies ↔ Use deceptive strategies.
employ 与 Use 同义替换
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Choose to be tough. 直接借用录音 participants could choose to be tough by making
an opening demand far greater than what they'd be willing to accept 中 "choose to
be tough" 几个原词。但这一句只是研究方法里 "参与者可以做出哪些选择" 的举例之一，
不是研究结论里 "被安排代理时实际倾向做" 的事。听到 tough 就选是典型原词陷阱。
借用原文：participants could choose to be tough
B) 原词陷阱
Sympathize with their opponent. 借用了录音 choose to express sympathy with their
opponent to appear pleasant 里 sympathy with their opponent。这句同样是研究方法
的举例选项之一，是受试者 "可以选" 的策略，不是结论性倾向；选项把 sympathy 改成
sympathize 听起来更顺耳，但只是原词陷阱。
借用原文：express sympathy with their opponent
D) 原词陷阱
Appear to be pleasant. 借用了录音 to appear pleasant 的几个字。但 to appear
pleasant 在录音里只是说明 "表达同情" 这种策略的目的（让自己看起来友好），仍属于研
究方法的举例铺垫，并不是结论。把目的状语当作结论行为是典型 "听到 pleasant 就选" 的
原词陷阱。
借用原文：to appear pleasant

questions.stem: What do we learn about the benefits the participants gained from the healthy cooking course?

options.label: A
options.text: They were perceived differently by some academics.

options.label: B
options.text: They still existed six months after the course ended.

options.label: C
options.text: They varied greatly among the course participants.

options.label: D
options.text: They were only measurable within seven weeks.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） They still existed six months after the course ended.
【定位】These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course.
这些益处在课程结束六个月之后依然存在。
【信号】段落收束句 + 时间锚点 six months。These benefits remained six months after the
completion of the course. 是第二段最后一句，承担收束作用：前两句 Course
participants saw significant improvements in general health. 与 They also reported
improved mental health and subjective vitality immediately after the program. 先讲
了课程结束后“立即”的好处，最后一句一个 remained + six months 把时间窗拉长——这
正是预读时圈出的时间锚点。
【替换】These benefits remained six months after the completion of the course. ↔
They still existed six months after the course ended.
remained = still existed；completion of the course = course ended
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项里 perceived differently by some academics 听起来像在说“被某些学者看法不一”，
它盗用了第一段里 Academics measured the program's effect on cooking confidence
and self-perceived mental health. 出现过的 Academics 与 self-perceived，但录音从未
说 academics 之间对这些好处有不同看法，是把原文里出现过的词重新拼装成一个新意
思。
借用原文：Academics measured the program's effect on cooking confidence and self-perceived
mental health.
C) 与原文相反
选项 They varied greatly among the course participants. 说好处在参与者之间差异巨
大，但第四段 Also, the mental health benefits were equal among participants who
were overweight or obese and those in a healthy weight range. 反而说好处在不同体
重人群之间是相等的，方向恰好与本选项相反。
借用原文：the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or
obese and those in a healthy weight range
D) 原词陷阱
选项 They were only measurable within seven weeks. 表面有 seven weeks 这个录音里
念到的数字（a seven-week healthy cooking course），听起来像是“原话”。但 seven-
week 在录音中只是课程的时长，不是好处的可测时间窗；而且加了 only 限定，与第二段
的 six months 直接矛盾。
借用原文：a seven-week healthy cooking course

questions.stem: What do the new research findings suggest about mental health benefits?

options.label: A
options.text: They can be easily seen among participants in a healthy weight range.

options.label: B
options.text: They should be attributed to participants' change in diet behaviors.

options.label: C
options.text: They are linked to cooking confidence and cooking satisfaction.

options.label: D
options.text: They actually result from eating more fruits and vegetables.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） They are linked to cooking confidence and cooking satisfaction.
【定位】This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking, and mental
health benefits.
这一点表明，烹饪信心与对烹饪的满足感和心理健康益处之间存在关联。
【信号】转折 However 之后的 This suggests 结论句。第四段首句 However, the study showed
participants' mental health improved even if their reported diet did not change after
completing the program. 用 however 翻盘——把第三段“也许是因为多吃果蔬”的猜测推
翻；段尾 This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around
cooking, and mental health benefits. 用 This suggests 直接给出研究真正归因。这两个
信号（however + This suggests）是听力定位结论句的金标准。
【替换】This suggests a link between cooking confidence and satisfaction around cooking, and mental health
benefits.
↔ They are linked to cooking confidence and cooking satisfaction.
a link between A and B = A are linked to B
satisfaction around cooking ↔ cooking satisfaction
of/around 短语 ↔ 复合名词
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 They can be easily seen among participants in a healthy weight range. 把录音里
the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or
obese and those in a healthy weight range 中的 healthy weight range 摘出来，但录
音强调的是“无论超重还是健康体重，效果都相等”——选项却暗示“只在健康体重组里更容易
看到”，把“相等”偷换成“在某一组更明显”。
借用原文：the mental health benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or
obese and those in a healthy weight range
B) 与原文相反
选项 They should be attributed to participants' change in diet behaviors. 把心理健康
益处归给“饮食行为的改变”，但 participants' mental health improved even if their
reported diet did not change after completing the program. 直接说“即便饮食没变，
心理健康也改善了”——选项与原文方向恰好相反。
借用原文：participants' mental health improved even if their reported diet did not change after
completing the program
D) 原词陷阱
选项 They actually result from eating more fruits and vegetables. 几乎逐字盗用
Researchers have previously found a link between eating more fruits and
vegetables, and improved longer term mental health.，听感非常“对”。但录音明确指出
这只是“之前的研究”和“可能的解释”，被第四段 however 推翻；本研究真正的结论是烹饪信
心与满足感，而不是多吃果蔬。
借用原文：Researchers have previously found a link between eating more fruits and vegetables,
and improved longer term mental health.

questions.stem: What plays a role in determining who benefits most from learning to cook?

options.label: A
options.text: Gender.

options.label: B
options.text: Confidence.

options.label: C
options.text: Health.

options.label: D
options.text: Practice.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Gender.
【定位】Who benefits most from learning to cook? Gender plays a part.
谁从学做饭中获益最多？性别在其中起了作用。
【信号】段首设问 + 直接应答。Who benefits most from learning to cook? 是段首设问，几乎是
把题干 What plays a role in determining who benefits most from learning to cook?
原样念了一遍——这种设问句之后的第一句 Gender plays a part. 就是答案句。设问+应答
是篇章独白里最强的答案信号。
【替换】Gender plays a part. ↔ Gender.
原词直出，无需改写
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
选项 Confidence. 与录音 77 per cent of female participants were confident about
cooking, but just 23 per cent of males were confident. 中反复出现的
confident/confidence 同根——录音确实在大量谈“信心”，但 confidence 是“差异表现的
指标”而非“决定谁受益最多”的那个变量；真正决定的是性别（女生先有信心、男生后追
上）。
借用原文：cooking confidence and skills were equal across both counterparts
C) 原词陷阱
选项 Health. 利用了全文反复出现的 health/mental health/general health 主题词的熟悉
感，但录音从未把 health 作为“决定谁受益最多”的变量；恰恰相反，the mental health
benefits were equal among participants who were overweight or obese and those in
a healthy weight range 还说健康状态不同的人受益是相等的。
借用原文：Course participants saw significant improvements in general health.
D) 未提及
选项 Practice. 的 practice（练习/实践）在录音中没有任何对应：第五段讨论性别差异和家
庭烹饪平衡，从未把“练习多少”列为决定受益的变量。

questions.stem: What does research show about our personal space?

options.label: A
options.text: It keeps others away.

options.label: B
options.text: It causes discomfort.

options.label: C
options.text: It remains visible.

options.label: D
options.text: It varies in size.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） It varies in size.
【定位】Research shows, however, that we actually have bubbles of different sizes.
然而，研究表明，我们实际上拥有不同大小的（个人空间）气泡。
【信号】Research shows + however 转折。答案句一头连了两个强信号：Research shows 是题
干 What does research show 的原句对应，however 是转折信号，转折之后才是真意
——前半『以为是同一个气泡』被推翻，后半『其实大小不同』才是结论。
【替换】bubbles of different sizes ↔ It varies in size.
bubbles of different sizes = varies in size
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 It keeps others away. 借用了原文 others can't enter 里的 others 来制造『听到
others 就想选』的诱惑；但原文说的是『别人进不来（指气泡的功能描述）』，并不是『研
究发现』那条结论。研究发现的真意在转折 however 之后，不在转折之前。
借用原文：others can't enter
B) 原词陷阱
选项 It causes discomfort. 抓住了原文 without causing discomfort 里的 discomfort 来
制造原词陷阱；但原文是说『别人进入气泡会带来不适』，描述的是『进入气泡的后果』，
不是研究本身的结论。这条信息在 23 题才用得上，放到 22 题就是张冠李戴。
借用原文：without causing discomfort
C) 与原文相反
选项 It remains visible. 说气泡『一直可见』，而原文 an invisible bubble of space 明确
说 invisible（看不见）。选项盗用了气泡这个话题，却把极性反过来了，是典型的极性反转
陷阱。
借用原文：an invisible bubble of space

questions.stem: What happens if a mere acquaintance enters our intimate space?

options.label: A
options.text: It makes us feel uncomfortable.

options.label: B
options.text: It renders the acquaintance a stranger.

options.label: C
options.text: It brings the acquaintance closer to us.

options.label: D
options.text: It causes the bubble around us to vanish.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） It makes us feel uncomfortable.
【定位】A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space makes us uncomfortable.
一个仅仅是熟人的人进入我们的亲密空间，会让我们感到不舒服。
【信号】题干定位词原句重现。录音里 A mere acquaintance entering our intimate space 几乎是
题干 a mere acquaintance enters our intimate space 的原句搬运，定位词全中；其后紧
跟的 makes us uncomfortable 就是直白结果，是典型的『触发条件 + 紧跟结果』结构。
【替换】makes us uncomfortable ↔ It makes us feel uncomfortable.
几乎逐词对应
【排除】B) 过度推断
选项 It renders the acquaintance a stranger. 借用录音里反复出现的 acquaintance 和
strangers 来制造『听到原词就选』的诱惑；但原文从未说『熟人会变成陌生人』，只是分
别为不同人群分配了不同空间。从『让人不适』推到『熟人变陌生人』属于过度推断。
借用原文：Friends and acquaintances can comfortably occupy this zone
C) 与原文相反
选项 It brings the acquaintance closer to us. 说『把熟人拉近』，但原文 makes us
uncomfortable 明确说会让我们不适，属于结果方向反了。同时它盗用了 acquaintance 这
个原词来骗你选。
借用原文：makes us uncomfortable
D) 未提及
选项 It causes the bubble around us to vanish. 借用整组核心词 bubble 来吸引点击，但
录音从未说过『熟人进入亲密空间会让气泡消失』，只是说会让我们不舒服。bubble
vanish 这一结果属于原文未提及。

questions.stem: Where do people feel comfortable interacting with new acquaintances or strangers?

options.label: A
options.text: In personal space.

options.label: B
options.text: In social space.

options.label: C
options.text: Within a distance of 18 inches.

options.label: D
options.text: Over 2 feet away from one another.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） In social space.
【定位】Extending from 4 to 12 feet away from us is "social space". Here people feel comfortable
conducting routine social interactions with new acquaintances or total strangers.
从距离我们 4 到 12 英尺的范围被称为『社交空间』。在这里，人们与新熟人或完全陌生的
人进行日常社交互动时感到舒适。
【信号】题干关键词原句重现 + 空间命名句。录音里 new acquaintances or total strangers 几乎
与题干 new acquaintances or strangers 一字不差对应；这句又紧跟在 "social space" 的
定义之后，定位极其稳。
【替换】"social space" ↔ In social space.
专有概念名直接对应
routine social interactions with new acquaintances or total strangers ↔
interacting with new acquaintances or strangers
行为限定原句对应
【排除】A) 张冠李戴
选项 In personal space. 借用了原文中的 personal space 这个原词，但录音里 personal
space 是给『朋友和熟人』用的（friends and acquaintances 在『informal
conversations』里使用），并不是给陌生人用的。配的人群对不上。
借用原文：Friends and acquaintances can comfortably occupy this zone, especially during
informal conversations, but strangers are forbidden.
C) 原词陷阱
选项 Within a distance of 18 inches. 盗用了录音 18 inches 这个原词数字，但原文里 18
inches 是给 intimate space 的尺寸（只允许家人、宠物和最亲密的朋友进入），与题干问
的『陌生人交往的距离』完全不是一回事。
借用原文：18 inches in every direction
D) 原词陷阱
选项 Over 2 feet away from one another. 里的 2 feet 看起来很像录音里反复出现的几个
距离数字，但录音里给陌生人/新熟人互动的距离是 4 to 12 feet，不是 2 feet。选项偷偷把
数字换小了，是典型的数字偷换。
借用原文：Extending from 4 to 12 feet away from us is "social space"

questions.stem: When are the sizes of our bubbles fixed?

options.label: A
options.text: When we begin to feel fear.

options.label: B
options.text: When we develop a sense of space.

options.label: C
options.text: When we are 3 or 4 years old.

options.label: D
options.text: When we enter our teens.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） When we enter our teens.
【定位】The sizes of our bubbles are fixed by our teens.
我们（个人空间）气泡的大小在我们进入青少年时期时就被定型了。
【信号】题干原句重现 + 关键介词 by。录音 The sizes of our bubbles are fixed by our teens 几
乎逐词复述题干 the sizes of our bubbles fixed，再加上时间介词 by our teens，定位与
时间一并锁定。这是题干原句重现 + 时间限定词紧跟的双信号。
【替换】by our teens ↔ When we enter our teens.
介词短语 ↔ 时间状语从句
are fixed ↔ fixed
动作原词重现
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 When we begin to feel fear. 盗用了录音 the brain region involved in fear 里的
fear 来吸引点击，但原文从未把 fear 当作一个时间节点，只是顺带提到大脑里负责恐惧的
区域参与构建气泡。这是把『脑区话题』偷换成『时间节点』。
借用原文：These bubbles are constructed and monitored by the brain region involved in fear.
B) 答非所问
选项 When we develop a sense of space. 盗用了录音 we begin to develop our
individual sense of personal space 里的 develop 和 sense of space，但这一句对应的动
作是 develop（开始发展），不是题干问的 fixed（被定型）。同一段里两个动作各配一个
时间，选项把动作和时间故意错配。
借用原文：we begin to develop our individual sense of personal space around age 3 or 4
C) 张冠李戴
选项 When we are 3 or 4 years old. 直接盗用了录音里的数字 around age 3 or 4，但这
个年龄绑的是『开始发展空间感』(develop)，不是『定型』(fixed)。题干问的是 fixed 的
时间，故 3 or 4 岁是错配。
借用原文：around age 3 or 4

questions.stem: What may be the reason that friends are similar to each other according to the recent research?

options.label: A
options.text: Their brains work in harmony.

options.label: B
options.text: They are generally the same age.

options.label: C
options.text: Their interests are quite similar.

options.label: D
options.text: They have the same ethnic background.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Their brains work in harmony.
【定位】It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other.
这可能是因为你们的大脑彼此协同运作。
【信号】因果信号 because。录音开头先抛问句“有没有发现你和朋友很像“，紧接 It may be
because your brains operate in harmony with each other —— because 就是把答案点
亮的因果信号词，because 后面那句正是“相似的原因“，直接命中题干所问。
【替换】your brains operate in harmony with each other ↔ Their brains work in harmony.
operate 换说成 work
【排除】B) 原词陷阱
录音确实念到 friends are more likely to be the same age，They are generally the
same age. 正盗用了这个 same age。但这句前面有 We know that，是“早已知道的旧结论
“，并非题干所问的“近期研究发现的相似原因“——原因落在大脑那句，不在同龄这句。
借用原文：friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and ethnic background
C) 未提及
Their interests are quite similar. 听起来很合常识，但录音通篇没提“兴趣（interests）“相
似，只说了年龄、性别、族裔背景与大脑。它靠的是考生“朋友兴趣相投“的生活常识，而非
录音内容，属未提及。
D) 原词陷阱
They have the same ethnic background. 盗用了录音的 ethnic background。和 B 一
样，这句出自 We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and
ethnic background，是“已知的旧情况“，不是近期研究新发现的相似原因，答非所问。
借用原文：the same age, gender and ethnic background

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the relationship between friends?

options.label: A
options.text: It can be touching.

options.label: B
options.text: It is hard to predict.

options.label: C
options.text: It can work both ways.

options.label: D
options.text: It resembles family ties.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） It can work both ways.
【定位】The relationship probably goes two ways. We are drawn to people who think like us; we then
influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely
resembling our own.
这种关系很可能是双向的。我们被与自己想法相近的人吸引；随后我们又会逐渐影响他们的
想法，这可能促使他们的大脑活动变得更接近我们自己的。
【信号】定性句 goes two ways。录音第二段结尾用 The relationship probably goes two ways
直接给“关系“下定性，后面 We are drawn to people…; we then influence their
thoughts 一来一回正是对“双向“的解释。这句“主语就是题干 relationship + 紧跟一个性质
判断“的结构，就是答案句信号。
【替换】The relationship probably goes two ways ↔ It can work both ways.
two ways 换成 both ways
We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts ↔
It can work both ways.
一来一回印证双向
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
It can be touching. 盗用了录音的 touching，可那个 touching 出现在 Some people
might find a romantic scene touching——是在举例说明“不同人对同一画面反应不同“，
说的是“浪漫场景“感人，根本不是在评价“朋友关系“。张冠李戴，答非所问。
借用原文：Some people might find a romantic scene touching, for instance
B) 与原文相反
It is hard to predict. 借了录音的 predict。但录音说的是 it could be used to predict
whether two people were already friends or not——意思是“大脑相似度高到能用来预测
两人是不是朋友“，是说“能预测“，根本没说“关系难预测“。选项把“能预测“反着说成了“难预
测“，与原文相反。
借用原文：it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not
D) 未提及
It resembles family ties. 听着像那么回事，但录音全程没把朋友关系比作“家庭纽带
（family ties）“，只说了关系“双向“。它纯靠考生自行联想，录音无任何对应，属未提及。
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 Two men who have been best friends for 60 years have just realized they are actually brothers. It's
reported that Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald met in the 6th grade at a school in Hawaii. They
have been best friends ever since. Alan was given away for adoption soon after he was born, and Walter
never knew his father. So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover
more about their ancestry. Walter was astonished to find that he matched with website user Robi 737. He
knew immediately that this was his best friend Alan, whose friends call him Robi and flew 737 airplanes
when he was a pilot. The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.
两名保持了60年最佳友谊的男子刚刚意识到他们实际上是兄弟。据报道，Alan Robinson和Walter
MacDonald在夏威夷的一所学校读六年级时相识。从那时起他们就一直是最好的朋友。Alan出生后不久
就被送去领养，而Walter从未见过自己的父亲。因此最近，他们分别在DNA匹配网站上尝试了解更多关
于自己祖先的信息。Walter惊讶地发现他与网站用户Robi 737匹配。他立即知道这就是他最好的朋友
Alan，Alan的朋友们都叫他Robi，而且他当飞行员时驾驶737飞机。这对朋友出生于同一位母亲，相隔
15个月。

questions.stem: What did both Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald attempt to do on DNA matching websites?

options.label: A
options.text: Search for their half-brothers.

options.label: B
options.text: Identify their biological fathers.

options.label: C
options.text: Find out more about their ancestry.

options.label: D
options.text: See whether they are actually related.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） Find out more about their ancestry.
【定位】So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about
their ancestry.
所以最近，他们俩各自在DNA配对网站上做了尝试，想多了解一些自己的家世血统。
【信号】题干原词attempt复现+目的句。题干问 attempt to do，录音里恰好出现 made separate
attempts on DNA matching websites，attempt 和 DNA matching websites 原词对
上，紧跟其后的 to discover more about their ancestry 用 to do 带出目的——这个‘题干
关键词复现 + to do 目的句’就是答案信号。
【替换】to discover more about their ancestry ↔ Find out more about their ancestry.
discover换成find out，ancestry原样
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 说去 Search for their half-brothers.(寻找同父异母的兄弟)。录音确实出现 they are
actually brothers‘他们其实是兄弟’，A 盗用了 brothers 这个词，但录音里这是新闻最后揭
晓的真相，不是他俩上网时‘想去找的目标’——而且他们是同母兄弟、不是 half-brothers，
张冠李戴。
借用原文：they are actually brothers
B) 原词陷阱
B 说去 Identify their biological fathers.(确认亲生父亲)。录音有 Walter never knew his
father，B 盗用了 father 一词，但这只是介绍背景，两人上网的目的写得很清楚是
discover more about their ancestry(查家世)，不是专门去认父亲。
借用原文：Walter never knew his father
D) 原词陷阱
D 说去 See whether they are actually related.(看看俩人是否真有亲属关系)。录音里 they
are actually brothers 用了 actually 一词，D 盗用了 actually 并改写成 related，可他们上
网时压根不知道彼此有血缘、不是‘去验证是否有关系’，验出是兄弟是意外结果，不是上网
动机。
借用原文：they are actually brothers

questions.stem: What did the news report say about Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald?

options.label: A
options.text: They were both given up for adoption.

options.label: B
options.text: They were born to the same mother.

options.label: C
options.text: They flew 737 airplanes as pilots.

options.label: D
options.text: They were both 60 years of age.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） They were born to the same mother.
【定位】The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.
这两个人是同一个母亲所生，出生时间相差15个月。
【信号】结尾收束句给出血缘真相。新闻把最关键的血缘结论放在末句 The pair were born to the
same mother 15 months apart——新闻报道常把核心事实或结局压在结尾，这个‘篇末收
束’位置就是答案信号，born to the same mother 与选项 B 直接对应。
【替换】born to the same mother ↔ They were born to the same mother.
原句几乎照搬主语换成They
【排除】A) 与原文相反
A 说两人 They were both given up for adoption.(都被送养)。录音里确有 Alan was
given away for adoption，A 盗用了 adoption，但录音只说 Alan 一个人被送养，A 却说
成 both(两个人都)，把范围从一人扩大到两人，与原文不符。
借用原文：Alan was given away for adoption
C) 张冠李戴
C 说两人 They flew 737 airplanes as pilots.(都当飞行员开737)。录音念到了 flew 737
airplanes when he was a pilot，C 盗用了 737 和 pilot 这两个醒目词，但 he 指的只是
Alan 一人，C 说成 They(两人都飞)，把一人之事安到两人头上。
借用原文：flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot
D) 偷换概念
D 说两人 They were both 60 years of age.(都60岁)。录音开头有 best friends for 60
years，D 盗用了数字 60，但这60是‘做了60年好朋友’，是友谊的年数，不是两人的年龄；
偷换了60所修饰的对象。
借用原文：best friends for 60 years

questions.stem: Why did one of the male tourists feel sad?

options.label: A
options.text: One of his friends was caught littering.

options.label: B
options.text: Other tourists refused to join in the cleanup.

options.label: C
options.text: The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash.

options.label: D
options.text: The kilometer-long beach was practically deserted.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash.
【定位】He felt so sad to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash.
他看到如此美丽的地方却被这么多垃圾弄得脏乱不堪，感到非常难过。
【信号】feel sad 与题干同词直接命中。答案句直接出现题干里的 He felt so sad，紧跟其后的 to
see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash 就是难过的原因；听到与题干情
绪词同样的‘sad’，那一句就是答案句。
【替换】such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash ↔
The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash
同义改写：美景被垃圾糟蹋
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 项借用录音里的 his friends 一词，但原文只说他和朋友一起去捡垃圾，从没说‘朋友被抓
乱扔垃圾’，是把出现过的原词拼成一个录音根本没说的情节。
借用原文：he and his friends decided to grab a few trash bags
B) 未提及
录音说的是‘nobody was doing anything’（没人去管这些垃圾），并非‘其他游客拒绝加入
清理’；‘refused to join in’这一情节录音从未出现，属凭空捏造。
D) 与原文相反
D 项盗用录音里的 kilometer-long beach，却说海滩‘practically deserted（几乎空无一
人）’；而录音强调的是海滩满是垃圾、不够美，与‘空无一人’语义不符，方向反了。
借用原文：Yesterday two male and three female tourists were spotted walking the kilometer-
long beach

questions.stem: Who put the good deed video on the internet?

options.label: A
options.text: A passerby.

options.label: B
options.text: A local woman.

options.label: C
options.text: The beach authorities.

options.label: D
options.text: One of the five tourists.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） A passerby.
【定位】A man passing by decided to video their good deed and put it on the internet.
一名路过的男子决定把他们的善举拍下来并发布到网上。
【信号】动作 put it on the internet 与题干同动作。答案句出现与题干同样的动作 put it on the
internet，前面的主语 A man passing by 就是施动者；听到题干里的关键动作时，紧抓它
的主语即可锁定答案。
【替换】A man passing by ↔ A passerby
短语压缩成单词
【排除】B) 张冠李戴
B 项盗用录音里的 One local woman，但这位本地女子做的是‘评论说自己很尴尬’，并非上
传视频；把别人做的事安到她头上，属人物错位。
借用原文：One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up
their beach
C) 未提及
录音通篇没出现‘beach authorities（海滩管理方）’这个角色，上传视频的也不是任何官方
机构，属凭空捏造的身份。
D) 张冠李戴
D 项盗用录音里的‘游客’，游客确实是事件主角、在捡垃圾，但发视频到网上的是路过男子
而非游客中的某人；把上传动作错记到游客身上。
借用原文：they were most likely traveling together

questions.stem: Why did one local woman say she was embarrassed?

options.label: A
options.text: The tourists' good deed was not noticed by the locals.

options.label: B
options.text: Some natives were selling poor-quality food to tourists.

options.label: C
options.text: The number of tourists to the beach is on a steady decline.

options.label: D
options.text: It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach.
【定位】One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up
their beach.
一名本地女子评论说，她为游客在清理他们本地的海滩这件事感到尴尬。
【信号】embarrassed that 直接引出原因。答案句出现题干同词 embarrassed，紧跟的 that
tourists were cleaning up their beach 由 that 直接引出尴尬的原因；听到 embarrassed
后那句 that 从句就是答案句。
【替换】that tourists were cleaning up their beach ↔
It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach
补出隐含对照：游客而非本地人
【排除】A) 与原文相反
A 项说‘游客善举没被本地人注意到’，但录音里本地女子明明注意到了才会尴尬，路人还拍
了视频，恰恰说明被注意到了；‘not noticed’与录音事实相反。
借用原文：One local woman commented on being embarrassed
B) 偷换概念
B 项盗用录音里的 food and drinks，但原文是说本地人‘带来食物饮料后留下垃圾’，绝非
‘卖劣质食物给游客’；把‘带来食物乱丢垃圾’偷换成‘卖劣质食物’。
借用原文：it was actually the natives who brought food and drinks then left trash all along
the island
C) 未提及
录音通篇没提‘游客数量在持续下降’这一信息，本题谈的是清理海滩与尴尬，与游客增减无
关，属凭空捏造的全新话题。

questions.stem: Why can't the man go for a run Saturday morning?

options.label: A
options.text: He has to play football with workmates.

options.label: B
options.text: He has got some books to read.

options.label: C
options.text: He is going to visit a friend.

options.label: D
options.text: He is physically unfit for it.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） He is physically unfit for it.
【定位】I'd love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues.
我很想去，但我上周末和同事踢足球时弄伤了脚踝。
【信号】转折 but 后才是真理由。男士先说 I'd love to（很想去）是客套，紧跟的 but 才转出真正
原因——I hurt my ankle，所以答案句落在 but 之后。
【替换】I hurt my ankle ↔ He is physically unfit for it.
具体伤情概括成"身体不适合"
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 He has to play football with workmates. 把原文里的 playing football with work
colleagues 原词搬来，但原文是说"踢球时受了伤"、不是"周六要去踢球"，听到 football
就选会落进陷阱。
借用原文：playing football with work colleagues
B) 张冠李戴
选项 He has got some books to read. 说的是他后面提到的读书 I've been catching up
on some reading，那是第11题的内容，与"为何不能去跑步"无关，属张冠李戴。
借用原文：I've been catching up on some reading
C) 未提及
选项 He is going to visit a friend. 在对话里根本没出现，男士不能去跑步的理由是脚伤，
不是去看朋友，纯属编造。

questions.stem: Why is the woman's whole family going to the zoo next Saturday?

options.label: A
options.text: To teach kids about animal protection.

options.label: B
options.text: To learn how popular zoos could be.

options.label: C
options.text: To see some rare animals in cages.

options.label: D
options.text: To give her little nephew a treat.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） To give her little nephew a treat.
【定位】My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo, so the whole family is going.
我的小侄子要满六岁了，他很喜欢动物园，所以全家一起去。
【信号】因果 so 引出去的原因。so the whole family is going 里的 so 把前因"小侄子过六岁生
日、又喜欢动物园"和后果"全家去"连起来，so 之前就是"为什么去"的答案。
【替换】My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo ↔ To give her little nephew a treat.
为侄子庆生=给侄子一份开心
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 To teach kids about animal protection. 借了女士后面说的 they are fun and
educational for children 里的 educational，但原文只说动物园对孩子有趣又有教育意
义，从没说全家去是为了"教孩子动物保护"，是把原词拔高到原文没说的目的。
借用原文：they are fun and educational for children
B) 原词陷阱
选项 To learn how popular zoos could be. 套用了 They are nowhere near as popular
as they used to be 里的 popular，但那只是女士顺口评论动物园不如从前受欢迎，绝不是
全家去的目的。
借用原文：They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be
C) 原词陷阱
选项 To see some rare animals in cages. 借了 the poor animals stuck in cages 里的
cages，但原文是女士同情笼中动物，没说去看"珍稀"动物，rare 更是凭空添加。
借用原文：the poor animals stuck in cages

questions.stem: What do we learn about Dan from the man's description?

options.label: A
options.text: He enjoys excellent health.

options.label: B
options.text: He is keen on extreme sports.

options.label: C
options.text: He coaches tennis players every week.

options.label: D
options.text: He spends most of his time in the gym.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） He enjoys excellent health.
【定位】Dan is extremely fit and healthy. He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times
a week.
Dan 非常健壮、健康。他几乎每天去健身房，外加每周打两三次网球。
【信号】直接给出对 Dan 的总评。男士 Dan is extremely fit and healthy 是对 Dan 的直接定性评
价，后面 gym、tennis 都是佐证，这句总评就是答案句。
【替换】Dan is extremely fit and healthy ↔ He enjoys excellent health.
extremely fit and healthy = excellent health
【排除】B) 未提及
选项 He is keen on extreme sports. 把 Dan 的运动夸大为"极限运动"，原文只说他常去健
身房、打网球，从没提 extreme sports，属无中生有。
C) 偷换概念
选项 He coaches tennis players every week. 搬来原文的 tennis 和 a week，但原文是
Dan 自己"打"网球 plus tennis two or three times a week，不是"教"网球选手，把"打"偷
换成"教"。
借用原文：plus tennis two or three times a week
D) 原词陷阱
选项 He spends most of his time in the gym. 借了 He goes to the gym most days 里
的 gym 和 most，但原文是"多数日子去健身房"，选项偷偷改成"把大部分时间花在健身
房"，频率被夸大成时长。
借用原文：He goes to the gym most days

questions.stem: What has the man been doing since last weekend?

options.label: A
options.text: Tending to his swollen ankle.

options.label: B
options.text: Concentrating on reading.

options.label: C
options.text: Writing three book reports.

options.label: D
options.text: Planning Christmas celebrations.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Concentrating on reading.
【定位】I've been catching up on some reading. I was given three books over Christmas, and I'm only
now getting around to reading them.
我一直在补读一些书。圣诞节别人送了我三本书，我现在才腾出空来读它们。
【信号】I've been doing 直接应答。女士问他脚伤期间在干嘛，男士直接以 I've been catching
up on some reading 应答，被问者的这句应答就是答案句，与题干时态对应。
【替换】I've been catching up on some reading ↔ Concentrating on reading.
catching up on reading = concentrating on reading
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项 Tending to his swollen ankle. 借了女士问句里的 that swollen ankle，但脚踝肿只是
他读书的背景，他并没说"一直在护理脚踝"，把背景说成正在做的活动。
借用原文：that swollen ankle
C) 原词陷阱
选项 Writing three book reports. 搬来原文的 I was given three books 里的 three 和
books，但原文是别人送他三本书"读"，不是他"写三份读书报告"，把"读书"偷换成"写报
告"。
借用原文：I was given three books over Christmas
D) 原词陷阱
选项 Planning Christmas celebrations. 借了 over Christmas 里的 Christmas，但原文
Christmas 只是"圣诞期间收到书"的时间状语，他并没在"筹备圣诞庆祝"，纯属对原词的曲
解。
借用原文：over Christmas

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man's book published recently?

options.label: A
options.text: It is being debated by hundreds of retirees.

options.label: B
options.text: It is attracting many people's attention.

options.label: C
options.text: It partly records his own experience.

options.label: D
options.text: It argues for postponing retirement.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） It is attracting many people's attention.
【定位】John, your book is getting a lot of attention, partly because you write that most people can
retire by 40.
约翰，你的书正受到很多关注，部分原因是你在书里写道大多数人能在 40 岁退休。
【信号】主持人开场对书的正面定性句。主持人介绍书时直接给出定性：your book is getting a lot
of attention。这种"主持人开场对作品的概括"就是介绍类细节题的答案信号——它把书的
核心特点一句点明。
【替换】getting a lot of attention ↔ attracting many people's attention
"获得关注"换说成"吸引关注"
【排除】C) 偷换概念
录音里作者说 I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40，是"采访了几百
人"，并没说书"记录他自己的经历"；C 把"研究别人"偷换成"写他自己"，答非所问。
借用原文：I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40
D) 与原文相反
录音说书主张 most people can retire by 40，是"提前到 40 岁退休"，而 D 说书主张"推
迟退休"(postponing retirement)，正好反了。这是把"提前"听成"推迟"的反向陷阱。
借用原文：most people can retire by 40
A) 原词陷阱
录音里 hundreds 来自 I interviewed hundreds of people，指作者"采访了几百人"，A 却
说书"正被几百名退休者讨论"(debated by hundreds of retirees)，把"被采访的人"偷换
成"在讨论书的人"，是听到 hundreds 就想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40

questions.stem: What do the articles the woman read recommend?

options.label: A
options.text: One should foresee a financial crisis.

options.label: B
options.text: One should trust financial planners, figures.

options.label: C
options.text: One should have one million dollars to retire.

options.label: D
options.text: One should start saving as early as possible.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） One should have one million dollars to retire.
【定位】I've read articles recommending one million dollars as a good figure for retirement.
我读过一些文章，推荐一百万美元作为退休的合适数额。
【信号】女士转述文章的 recommend 句。女士说 I've read articles recommending one million
dollars，动词 recommend 与题干 recommend 完全对应，这句"女士转述文章推荐什
么"就是答案信号——题目问的正是这个来源。
【替换】one million dollars as a good figure for retirement ↔ have one million dollars to retire
"一百万作合适数额"="应有一百万才退休"
【排除】B) 张冠李戴
financial planners 确实在录音出现 most financial planners do give numbers，但那是
嘉宾说"规划师爱给数字、我觉得没用"，文章并没"推荐相信规划师"。B 把原词搬来、又把
内容安错了人(文章 vs 规划师)。
借用原文：most financial planners do give numbers, I don't think that's useful
D) 答非所问
"尽早储蓄"听着像理财常识，但录音里文章推荐的是"一百万这个数额"，并没说"尽早储
蓄"；至于储蓄、投资是嘉宾在后面(P14)讲的做法，不是"女士读的文章"推荐的。D 答非所
问。
借用原文：investing half your monthly income
A) 未提及
选项 A 的 financial crisis 借了话题里"financial"的语感，但文章推荐的是具体金额，从没
让人"预见金融危机"；录音通篇也没出现"危机"的意思。A 是听到 financial 就联想出来的干
扰。

questions.stem: What does the man say about retirement?

options.label: A
options.text: It doesn't need to be permanent.

options.label: B
options.text: It shouldn't be considered risky.

options.label: C
options.text: It helps to reduce travel expenses.

options.label: D
options.text: It is the way to quit a job one hates.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） It doesn't need to be permanent.
【定位】Retirement doesn't have to be permanent, and if people need to, they can go back to work.
退休不一定是永久的，如果有需要，人们可以重新回去工作。
【信号】男士对退休下的直接定性句。男士直接断言 Retirement doesn't have to be permanent，
这是他对"退休"本身的一句正面定义，又用 they can go back to work 加以说明，是"他怎
么说退休"的直接答案信号。
【替换】Retirement doesn't have to be permanent ↔ It doesn't need to be permanent
doesn't have to=doesn't need to
they can go back to work ↔ doesn't need to be permanent
"能回去工作"佐证"不必永久"
【排除】B) 与原文相反
risky 来自女士 That sounds risky to me 和男士 I counsel people to take risks——男士
是"劝人去冒险"，承认有风险；B 却说退休"不该被视为有风险"，意思反了，是听到 risk 就
想选的原词陷阱。
借用原文：I counsel people to take risks
D) 原词陷阱
a job they hate 确实出现在 spend their lives working on jobs they hate，但那是男士解
释"很多人因恐惧而困在烂工作里"的背景，不是给退休下定义；D 把这句背景说成"退休就
是辞掉烂工作的途径"，答非所问。
借用原文：spend their lives working on jobs they hate
C) 未提及
C 说退休"有助减少差旅开支"(reduce travel expenses)，录音里 transport 出现在 cutting
housing, food, and transport expenses，那是"怎样攒钱"的省钱办法，与"退休本身是什
么"无关，更没说退休能省路费。C 属嫁接他处原词的无中生有。
借用原文：cutting housing, food, and transport expenses

questions.stem: How does the man say his proposal about retirement can be carried out?

options.label: A
options.text: By keeping close contact with one's employers.

options.label: B
options.text: By retiring when one reaches sixty years old.

options.label: C
options.text: By investing half of one's monthly income.

options.label: D
options.text: By following the counsel of financial planners.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题） By investing half of one's monthly income.
【定位】Simple, by cutting housing, food, and transport expenses, and investing half your
monthly income.
很简单，靠削减住房、饮食和交通开支，并拿出月收入的一半去投资。
【信号】男士回答"怎么做到"的 by 操作句。面对女士"怎么可能 40 岁退休"的追问，男士直接答 by
cutting housing, food, and transport expenses, and investing half your monthly
income，这句"by + 一串具体动作"就是 How 类题的答案信号。
【替换】investing half your monthly income ↔ investing half of one's monthly income
几乎原句对应的"投月收入一半"
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
employers 出现在 you will be attracted to employers，那是男士讲"保持技能就能被雇
主青睐、好重返职场"，回应的是"能否回去工作"，不是"怎么攒钱提前退休"；A 把它说
成"靠和雇主保持密切联系来实现退休"，答非所问。
借用原文：if you keep current with your skills, you will be attracted to employers
B) 与原文相反
sixty 来自女士的反问 most people can't retire at 60，意在质疑"连 60 都退不了，怎么
40 退"；B 却说"靠 60 岁退休来实现"，方向反了——男士主张的是 40 岁提前退，不是等
到 60。
借用原文：how can anyone save enough to retire by 40 when most people can't retire at 60
D) 与原文相反
financial planners 和 counsel 都在录音里——但男士对规划师是 I don't think that's
useful，并不让人"听规划师的"；counsel 是他"劝人冒险"(I counsel people to take
risks)，不是"听规划师劝告"。D 把原词拼到一起，方向与男士立场相反。
借用原文：While most financial planners do give numbers, I don't think that's useful

questions.stem: What was the finding of the new research from America about consumers' food choices?

options.label: A
options.text: They tended to be easily anticipated by those belonging to their own race.

options.label: B
options.text: They tended to be arbitrarily judged by individuals of opposing groups.

options.label: C
options.text: They were readily shared among members of the same social or racial group.

options.label: D
options.text: They were influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） They were influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group.
【定位】This research found college students were more likely to choose healthy food in the presence
of an observer of a different race, as opposed to an observer from their own race.
这项研究发现，与本族观察者在场相比，大学生在不同种族的观察者在场时更可能选择健康
食物。
【信号】结论标志词 found。录音 This research found 直接亮出研究结论，found 后面跟的就
是研究发现，这是篇章交代核心结论的标志，听到 found/showed 这类词就知道答案句
来了。
【替换】in the presence of an observer of a different race ↔
influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group
下位换上位
were more likely to choose healthy food ↔ were influenced
详述换概括
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
A 用了录音后文 participants anticipated more negative judgment 里的 anticipated 一
词，但把它扭成易被同族人预料，与研究发现毫无关系，是听到原词就想选的陷阱。
借用原文：participants anticipated more negative judgment
B) 偷换概念
B 说食物选择被对立群体的个人任意评判，借了录音 they felt less judged by members
of their own group 的 judge 概念，但研究发现的是选择被在场者影响，不是选择本身被
评判，偷换了概念。
借用原文：they felt less judged by members of their own group
C) 与原文相反
C 说食物选择在同族群体内易被共享，但录音 they felt less judged by members of their
own group 讲的是同族在场时人感觉评判更少、影响更小，根本没说共享选择，且方向与
研究重点（外群体才带来改变）相反。
借用原文：they felt less judged by members of their own group

questions.stem: When did 31 percent of students in the experiment select the healthier option?

options.label: A
options.text: When they tried to make a positive impression on the researchers.

options.label: B
options.text: When an unknown student from another university was present.

options.label: C
options.text: When an experimenter from the research team took notice.

options.label: D
options.text: When they were offered both candy and fruit as a snack.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） When an unknown student from another university was present.
【定位】However, this number was 31 percent when in the presence of an unknown student from
another university.
然而，当一名来自另一所大学的陌生学生在场时，这个数字是 31%。
【信号】数字与 when 条件绑定。录音 this number was 31 percent when in the presence of an
unknown student from another university 把 31 percent 与 when 引导的在场条件直接
绑在一起，听到目标数字就顺势抓它后面的 when 从句，即答案条件。
【替换】an unknown student from another university ↔ an unknown student from another university
条件原句对应
in the presence of ↔ was present
名词短语换动词
【排除】A) 未提及
A 说学生想给研究者留好印象，录音只说他们 use healthy food choices to make a
positive impression，但针对的是外群体在场者，不是 researchers，录音从未提对研究者
留好印象这个条件，属无中生有。
C) 原词陷阱
C 借了录音多次出现的 research/experimenter 概念，编出研究团队的实验员注意到时，但
31 percent 绑定的是外校学生在场，与实验员留意无关，是听到 research 就想选的原词陷
阱。
借用原文：Other experiments showed similar results
D) 张冠李戴
D 说同时提供糖果和水果作零食时，candy 和 fruit 确是录音 participants were offered
the choice between candy and fruit as a snack 的原词，但这是整个实验的设置，对应
12% 与 31% 两种情境，不专属 31%，把背景条件错安成 31% 的专属触发，张冠李戴。
借用原文：participants were offered the choice between candy and fruit as a snack

questions.stem: How could a healthy diet be promoted according to the findings of the new research?

options.label: A
options.text: By advertising its social benefits.

options.label: B
options.text: By teaching consumers diet strategies.

options.label: C
options.text: By supporting struggling consumers.

options.label: D
options.text: By maintaining its positive image.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） By advertising its social benefits.
【定位】This research finds that one way to promote a healthy diet could be to advertise the social
benefits of healthy choices.
这项研究发现，推动健康饮食的一种方式可能是宣传健康选择的社会益处。
【信号】建议句 one way to…could be to。录音 one way to promote a healthy diet could be
to advertise the social benefits 用 one way to…could be to 这一建议句式给出对策，这
是篇章结尾提对策的信号，听到就锁定后面的方法。
【替换】advertise the social benefits of healthy choices ↔ advertising its social benefits
动词变动名词
【排除】B) 未提及
B 说教消费者饮食策略，录音虽提到 many attempts to help consumers make healthier
choices，但从未说具体方法是教饮食策略，这个手段是凭空添加的，属未提及。
C) 原词陷阱
C 说支持苦苦挣扎的消费者，借了录音 consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy
diet 的 struggle 一词，但那只是描述现状，不是研究给出的对策，是听到原词就想选的陷
阱。
借用原文：consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy diet
D) 张冠李戴
D 说维持其正面形象，借了录音 make a positive impression 里的 positive 概念，但那讲
的是个人用健康选择给自己留好印象，不是推动健康饮食的对策，张冠李戴。
借用原文：they strategically use healthy food choices to make a positive impression

questions.stem: What does the recent study led by Patricia Pendry aim to examine?

options.label: A
options.text: The academic and learning issues struggling students encounter.

options.label: B
options.text: The risk students face due to a history of mental health problems.

options.label: C
options.text: The effect of interacting with therapy dogs on students under pressure.

options.label: D
options.text: The work universities are doing to help students succeed academically

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （主旨题） The effect of interacting with therapy dogs on students under pressure.
【定位】This study shows that traditional stress management approaches aren't as effective for this
population compared with programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with
therapy dogs.
这项研究表明，对这一人群而言，传统的压力管理方法不如那些专注于提供与治疗犬互动机
会的项目有效。
【信号】总结句 This study shows。This study shows that 是篇章里的"结论/点题"信号——一
旦听到"这项研究表明……"，后面紧跟的就是研究的核心发现/目的，这正是主旨题的答案
落点。
【替换】programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with therapy dogs ↔
The effect of interacting with therapy dogs on students under pressure
动作短语→名词化概括
For college students under pressure ↔ students under pressure
几乎原词对应的对象
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项盗用了录音里的 academic and learning issues 原词，但那只是描述"哪类学生处于风
险"的背景信息，不是研究要考察的内容。听到原词就选会中招。
借用原文：academic and learning issues
B) 原词陷阱
选项搬用了录音的 a history of mental health issues，但那同样是在说明"哪些学生有风
险"的铺垫，不是研究目的。把背景当主旨就错了。
借用原文：a history of mental health issues
D) 原词陷阱
选项几乎照搬录音 Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students
succeed academically，但那是 Pendry 在铺垫"大学在做很多帮扶工作"的大背景，不
是"这项研究"本身要考察的内容；研究聚焦的是治疗犬，不是泛泛的大学帮扶工作。
借用原文：Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students succeed academically

questions.stem: What did the new study measure in the participants?

options.label: A
options.text: Their communicative skills.

options.label: B
options.text: Their executive functioning.

options.label: C
options.text: Their academic networking.

options.label: D
options.text: Their leadership capacities.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Their executive functioning.
【定位】The researchers measured executive functioning in the students involved in the study.
研究人员测量了参与研究的学生的执行功能。
【信号】原词 measured 直接领出宾语。录音用 The researchers measured executive
functioning，measured 这个动词与题干 measure 完全对应，紧跟其后的宾语就是答案，
是最直接的细节定位信号。
【替换】measured executive functioning ↔ Their executive functioning
原词直接对应
【排除】A) 未提及
communicative skills（沟通能力）录音从头到尾没提，是凭"听起来像学生该有的能力"硬
编的干扰项，没有原文支撑。
C) 原词陷阱
academic networking 把录音里多次出现的 academic（学业的）这个原词抓来拼了个新
词，但录音讲的是 academic stress/success，从没说测"学业人脉"，是借原词 academic
制造的假象。
借用原文：academic stress management programs
D) 未提及
leadership capacities（领导力）录音里完全没出现，是又一个"听上去像能力词"的硬凑干
扰，无原文依据。

questions.stem: What does Patricia Pendry think traditional stress management programs may do?

options.label: A
options.text: Rid students of their anxiety.

options.label: B
options.text: Add to some students' stress.

options.label: C
options.text: Contribute little to typical students' success.

options.label: D
options.text: Help students with mental issues pull through.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （态度观点题） Add to some students' stress.
【定位】But they're less helpful for struggling students. Pendry believes those students may
experience the programs as another lecture and feel even more stressed.
但对学习困难的学生而言，这些项目帮助不大。Pendry 认为这些学生可能会把这些项目当
成又一堂讲座，从而感到压力更大。
【信号】转折 But 后才是真实态度。But they're less helpful for struggling students 里的 But 是
关键信号——前半句先肯定"传统项目对普通学生有帮助"，But 一转才说出 Pendry 真正的
判断：对困难学生反而"更有压力"。态度题的答案几乎都在转折后。
【替换】feel even more stressed ↔ Add to some students\' stress
感受描述→施动概括
for struggling students ↔ some students
下位→上位概括
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
选项里的 anxiety 盗用了录音 manage stress or anxiety 的原词，且 Rid\.\.\.of（彻底消
除）把"帮助管理焦虑"夸大成"消除焦虑"，原文从没说传统项目能"根除"焦虑，程度被拔高
了。
借用原文：manage stress or anxiety
C) 与原文相反
录音明说传统项目 help typical students succeed——对普通学生是有帮助的；选项却
说"对普通学生的成功几乎没贡献"，把"有帮助"反成了"没帮助"，正话反说，且对象
（typical students）正是录音说有用的那群人。
借用原文：these workshops help typical students succeed
D) 与原文相反
录音说传统项目对"有困难的学生" less helpful for struggling students——是帮不上忙；
选项却说能"帮有心理问题的学生渡过难关"，把"帮不上"说成"帮得上"，方向反了，对象也
被偷换成"有心理问题的学生"。
借用原文：But they're less helpful for struggling students

questions.stem: What do entrepreneurs have to do when taking risks according to the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Work hard and plan carefully.

options.label: B
options.text: Attempt to succeed at any cost.

options.label: C
options.text: Aim high and expect great results.

options.label: D
options.text: Remain optimistic even in difficulty.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题） Work hard and plan carefully.
【定位】On the contrary, taking risks in entrepreneurship involves careful planning and hard work.
恰恰相反，创业中的冒险需要的是周密的规划和辛勤的努力。
【信号】转折 On the contrary 后是真意。录音先说冒险“不是盲目去做、坐等大成果”，紧接着用
On the contrary 转折，转折之后那句 involves careful planning and hard work 才是正
面答案；听到 On the contrary 就该锁定后半句。
【替换】careful planning and hard work ↔ Work hard and plan carefully
名词短语换成动词短语
【排除】C) 原词陷阱
Aim high and expect great results 几乎照搬了录音被否定那半句的 expecting great
results，但录音是说“冒险”不等于“盲目坐等大成果”，这是被批评的做法，不是创业者“该
做”的；听到 expect great results 就选，正好踩进陷阱。
借用原文：expecting great results
B) 未提及
Attempt to succeed at any cost“不惜一切代价求成功”，录音通篇没说要“不计代价”，反
而强调冒险要靠规划和努力、还提醒“并非所有风险都是好风险”，这种太满的说法是命题人
添加的。
D) 答非所问
Remain optimistic even in difficulty 式的“乐观”确实在录音里出现过，an optimistic risk-
taker 也提到 optimistic，adapting in difficult times 也讲困境中应变，但那是讲“失败时
的心态”，不是回答“冒险时必须做什么”这道题，把别处的内容搬来作答即错位。
借用原文：an optimistic risk-taker

questions.stem: What does the passage say is key to business growth?

options.label: A
options.text: Regarding failure as something inevitable.

options.label: B
options.text: Trying out innovative marketing strategies.

options.label: C
options.text: Venturing into sectors never explored before.

options.label: D
options.text: Being willing to experiment with novel ideas.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Being willing to experiment with novel ideas.
【定位】The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth.
愿意去尝试新点子，是企业成长的关键。
【信号】原文 key 与题干同词对应。录音 is key to business growth 和题干 key to business
growth 用词几乎一模一样，这句话主语 The willingness to experiment with new ideas
就是答案；标志词 key 一响，定位即成。
【替换】The willingness to experiment with new ideas ↔ Being willing to experiment with novel ideas
近义改写 new=novel
【排除】B) 未提及
Trying out innovative marketing strategies 听起来很像“创新”，录音确有“new ideas”的
意思，但根本没提“marketing strategies（营销策略）”；它用“创新”诱你，却塞了原文没有
的“营销”。
C) 过度推断
Venturing into sectors never explored before“进入从未有人涉足的领域”比录音的“尝试
新点子”程度重得多，录音只说 experiment with new ideas，并没说要闯入“全新行业”，这
是把原意拔高了。
借用原文：experiment with new ideas
A) 原词陷阱
Regarding failure as something inevitable 里 failure 是录音高频词，look at failure as
an opportunity to learn 也讲了对失败的看法，但录音说的是“把失败当学习机会”，不是
“把失败当不可避免”，更不是回答“增长关键”；它用熟悉的 failure 制造错觉。
借用原文：look at failure as an opportunity to learn

questions.stem: What are we advised to do when we fail?

options.label: A
options.text: Expect future success so as to move forward.

options.label: B
options.text: Learn from our failure and forge ahead.

options.label: C
options.text: Distinguish between good and bad risks.

options.label: D
options.text: Examine our strategies and find out weaknesses.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题） Learn from our failure and forge ahead.
【定位】But just remember that not all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and
move forward.
但要记住，并非所有风险都是好风险；当你失败时，要从中吸取教训，然后继续前进。
【信号】条件句 when you fail 直接应题。题干问 when we fail，录音正好有 when you fail, learn
from it and move forward 这句条件句，措辞与题干对应；听到 when you fail 后面紧跟
的 learn from it and move forward 就是答案。
【替换】learn from it and move forward ↔ Learn from our failure and forge ahead
代词还原＋近义短语
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Expect future success so as to move forward 借用了录音的 move forward，但把前提
偷换成“指望未来成功”——录音让你“前进”的前提是“从失败中学”，不是“指望成功”；听到
move forward 就选，正中陷阱。
借用原文：move forward
C) 答非所问
Distinguish between good and bad risks 用了录音 not all risks are good ones 的意
思，录音确实提醒“并非所有风险都好”，但那是另一层提醒，不是“失败时”被建议做的事，
答非所问。
借用原文：not all risks are good ones
D) 未提及
Examine our strategies and find out weaknesses“检查策略、找出弱点”录音没有对应说
法，录音只讲“失败教你如何战略性思考”think and plan strategically，并没有让你去“查弱
点”，是凭 strategically 一词联想出来的。
借用原文：think and plan strategically

questions.stem: What does it mean to risk-taking businesses when most people tend to avoid risk?

options.label: A
options.text: Fresher offers.

options.label: B
options.text: Safer operation.

options.label: C
options.text: More challenges.

options.label: D
options.text: Less competition.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题） Less competition.
【定位】Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less competition for
risk-takers.
简单地说，当大多数人远离风险时，对冒险者而言就意味着更少的竞争。
【信号】Simply put 总结句给结论。录音用 Simply put（简而言之）领出一句总结，it means less
competition for risk-takers 直接给出结论，与题干“what does it mean”正好对接；听到
Simply put 这类收束词就知道结论要来了。
【替换】less competition for risk-takers ↔ Less competition
几乎原词截取
【排除】A) 原词陷阱
Fresher offers 借了录音 fresh offers 这个原词，但那句讲的是冒险者“用新点子、新供给、
大胆发明在立标准”，是描述冒险者的做法，不是回答“别人避险意味着什么”，张冠李戴。
借用原文：fresh offers
C) 与原文相反
More challenges“更多挑战”与录音结论方向相反：录音说别人避险对冒险者是“更少竞争”
这种好事，而 challenge 是偏负面的负担，录音的 adapting in difficult times 谈的是冒险
者善应变，并没说“更多挑战”。
借用原文：adapting in difficult times
B) 未提及
Safer operation 像是从录音 stay safe 联想来的，但 as long as you want to stay safe 是
说“你若一味求稳就永远不会知道结果”，是对“守成者”的提醒，并不是说冒险企业能“更安全
地运营”，原文没有这层意思。
借用原文：stay safe
